# Received Actuality, Intrinsic Necessity, and Original Source Unity

## Abstract

An account of received actuality must distinguish the production of an effect from the existential adequacy of the resources that produce it. A local explanation may correctly describe how available materials and powers yield a new product while leaving their own received actuality outside its scope. The argument developed here asks what a complete productive account must cover, how an original intrinsic resource supports an actual bearer, and why complete intrinsic adequacy warrants necessity of that same bearer. Its two substantive judgments are global productive adequacy and the modal reach of intrinsic existential sufficiency. The conditional resource-to-bearer inference is given explicitly, while the warrant for those judgments is argued philosophically. Two challenges receive separate treatment: autonomous collective explanation without an original productive resource, and an unreceived original whose own existence is brute and contingent. Neither challenge is answered by changing its terminology or weakening its proposed ontology. The resulting position is an affirmative, defeasible argument for the same actual original's intrinsic necessity, with the precise contribution and limits of each step preserved. The continuation develops the separate argument for one complete original source of the actual connected field, proves the local and propagation results, and reconciles explanatory countermodels and truthful self-knowledge with the affirmative appraisal. Generic explanation, productive provision and individual bearer identity remain distinct.

*Editorial status: this is a new exposition consolidating the named arguments and their recorded corrections. It does not add owner adoption, independent acceptance of this edition, a new formal verification, or fresh authentication of the underlying Arabic sources.*

## 1. The actuality to be explained

The starting point is received actuality: something actual whose relevant productive basis is not supplied by that thing's nonexistent or insufficient reality. Identifying such a target requires more than introducing a predicate called “received.” The argument needs warranted occurrence, an adequate account of the target's identity, and the relevant productive derivation. An ordinary material-generation case makes those requirements concrete. Fix an actually produced fruit, its continuing tree, and the material contributions involved in its development. The fruit is not numerically the tree, and the existence of the tree before the fruit does not establish that this fruit already existed under another name. [Material origination, §§2–3][s5]

Production from antecedent material does not erase this distinction. “From” can describe a persisting constituent, an expended material input, or a productive supplier; those roles should not be collapsed. A continuing source can produce a different individual. Conversely, some changes are alterations of an existing subject, and a change of description does not create a new bearer. The entry case therefore rests on the conjunction of a distinct product and its described material, developmental, and productive derivation. Temporal novelty alone is insufficient. [Material origination, §§2–3; independent review][s5] [Review of material origination][s6]

This is a generic ordinary case used in the source argument, not a newly recorded observation of a dated fruit. Its use does not require observing raw material arise from absolute nothing or proving that every constituent begins when the whole product begins. A persistent constituent, where warranted, retains its identity. Its persistence nevertheless leaves open whether its own existential actuality is received or intrinsically adequate. Ibn Taymiyya's stronger historical doctrine includes real transformation and the cessation of earlier qualified material realities, and criticises accounts that reduce every new animal or plant to altered accidents of retained material subjects. His continuing-tree, silver and wax examples nevertheless distinguish production of another individual from alteration of a persisting subject. This historical doctrine is not identified with modern microphysics. The selected fruit-case premise depends on distinct product identity and described productive derivation; it neither requires that whole substrate theory nor denies warranted constituent persistence. [Material origination, §§3, 5; current claim FND-003][s5] [Foundational claims][s8]

A developmental explanation can genuinely explain the fruit by using the tree, materials, and capacities as available resources. A further claim—that this explanation supplies a complete original account of those resources' own received actuality—has a larger target. The distinction is between two explanatory tasks, not between a valid local explanation and no explanation at all. What follows concerns the larger task. [Material origination, §§3–4][s5]

For that task, let **F** name the received productive field relevant to the case: the product's derivation together with the received suppliers and resources included in the account's nominated scope. F is plural shorthand for what is to be explained; it need not be an additional substance, world-object, or proposition acting as a producer. Its members need not all coexist at one time. Different effects may have different completed conditions, and an indefinitely extended history is not excluded simply for lacking a first temporal member. [Productive totality, §§3, 5; material origination, §§4–5][s4] [Material origination][s5]

The field must remain the target throughout the relevant inference. A resource contributing to complete provision of F has not thereby been shown to bear every stronger relation of relevance to each individual member, or wholly to provide one fruit by itself. The reviewed material application expressly adopted this field scope after correcting an ambiguity between the fruit as entry case and the field as Completion target. That correction preserves a concrete point of entry without inflating what the inference establishes. [Material-origination review, “Exact interface dependency and the resolved finding”][s6]

<a id="f250-a-material-receipt"></a>

**A material-origination control.** The received *al-Nubuwwāt* study supplies a particularly consequential textual check for this point. At S001L115 the electronic omission makes ordinary observed production appear to be production without material. The reported control at printed 322 restores the contrast: what people observe is God's bringing things about **from something else**, not origination without material. The resulting argument is compatible with the distinct-product entry case above. It neither makes the antecedent material independent of the Creator nor requires observing a constituent arise from absolute nothing. The stronger historical transformation account and the local argument from a genuinely new individual remain distinct from a contemporary theory of microphysical persistence. The control is evidence reported in the admitted reading study, not a new inspection of that printed page. [F250-A160-7-12] [F250-A216-1-19] [F250-A118-69-99]

The broader *Ṣafadiyya* comparison reinforces both sides. It describes the six-day world through antecedent created materials and distinguishes each creature's origination from a first moment of complete divine inactivity. It does not infer the independence or eternity of this particular material from the admissibility of earlier material. Nor may the statement that every created particular is preceded by its own nonexistence be converted into a time at which no creature at all exists. Thus the field question remains compatible with genuine material contribution, successive action and an indefinitely extended history, while retaining the source's affirmative claim that creatures neither originate nor persist independently. [F250-A067-531-549] [F250-A067-689-695] [F250-A067-847-850]

## 2. What complete productive adequacy requires

Suppose a proposed complete productive account consists entirely of suppliers whose own actuality is received. Each supplier may make a real contribution, and their coordination may explain an effect that no member could produce alone. The question is whether those facts also explain the received actuality of the productive basis itself. If a supplier's existence falls within the nominated target, its availability cannot simply be counted as an independently provided starting resource for that target. The same issue remains when the account is expressed in terms of the suppliers' arrangement. Arrangement may be productive, but its description does not by itself provide the actuality of what is arranged. [Productive totality, §3][s4]

The strongest form of the argument has five connected steps:

1. There is actual received productive reality to be accounted for.
2. A complete productive account must cover the relevant received actuality, including that of derivative suppliers it employs.
3. No derivative supplier can serve as the independently adequate provision of this entire target by borrowing its own received actuality from within that target.
4. Collecting or arranging derivative suppliers does not by itself discharge the same existential insufficiency at field scope.
5. The complete productive basis therefore includes actual unreceived productive actuality relevant to F.

The rationale for the fourth step is the inclusion of all relevant existential prerequisites within the scope of completion. The work an arrangement accomplishes does not, merely as arrangement, remove the received status of the actuality on which it depends. The claim is about sufficient productive provision of that actuality. It is not the inference that every property of each member must belong to the plurality. [Productive totality, §3][s4]

This is a substantive **global productive adequacy** judgment. Local external need alone does not prove that an entire plurality has an outside source. A prohibition of reciprocal efficient causation also does not, by itself, establish the global conclusion. The argument supplies the additional rationale that the proposed account must cover the derivative suppliers' own received actuality, and that collective form does not supply it merely by changing how the basis is described. Its force must be assessed at that scope. [Productive totality, §§3, 7; current claim FND-004][s4] [Foundational claims][s8]

No inference from individual possible absence to joint possible absence is required. Nor is a temporally first supplier required. A beginningless received history can still be the subject of the complete productive question. Equally, the argument does not infer original status from persistence across the alternatives represented by a model. A supplier could, under a proposed interpretation, exist in every represented world while receiving its whole existence in each. Its modal persistence would not make it intrinsically sufficient. A field defined by the actuality requiring productive provision must not silently exclude such a received supplier. [Productive totality, §§3, 5][s4]

The relevant sense of dependence must also remain restricted. Actual productive or existential receipt is not established merely by necessary co-presence. A bearer and its intrinsic qualification may be conceptually distinguishable without being separately produced substances. Intrinsic conditions can accompany one another without mutually producing one another. The source reconstruction expressly preserves those distinctions, so a necessary conditional or a list of a thing's features cannot by itself establish the external existential need at issue. [Productive totality, §4][s4]

A related source distinction appears in Ibn Taymiyya's *Darʾ taʿāruḍ al-ʿaql wa-l-naql*, III, 439–441. The exclusive-creation wording continuing onto page 440 belongs to his quotation of Ibn Tūmart's *al-Dalīl wa-l-ʿilm*. Ibn Taymiyya's own reply begins with *qultu* (“I say”). It argues that affirming knowledge, power or choice already affirms determinate qualifications, whereas unrestricted existence as such is a mental abstraction, not a featureless concrete existent. He then identifies the further question whether every determination requires a separate specifier. The passage therefore distinguishes concrete qualification and external specification; its quoted creation formula is not an additional argument here excluding two complete original productive relations. Nor does this limitation establish such a rival's metaphysical possibility. [Quoted passage][dar-qualification-quotation] [Ibn Taymiyya's reply][dar-qualification-reply]

Unity in kind must also be kept separate from numerical identity. In the continuation of this reply, Ibn Taymiyya distinguishes sharing a kind or description from being one individual: existing things share the description of existence, and humans share humanity. On his account, the common universal as universal is conceived rather than one concrete entity subsisting in all its instances. The inference at issue can be exposed without settling every theory of universals. From two bearers’ satisfying the same description it does not follow that they are identical; otherwise any two things correctly described as human would be one person. Nor does analysing a thing under several concepts establish that it was assembled from corresponding external components. These are controls on a proposed inference, not evidence that two entirely adequate originals actually exist. A common existential description supplies neither original productive resources nor numerical unity of their bearers. The latter claim still needs the productive argument in section 9. [*Darʾ*, III, 446–448, continuation of the reply][dar-kind-and-individual]

The positive conclusion is that the received field has a relevant original productive basis under the intended productive interpretation. It is not yet the conclusion that one bearer individually provides every requisite, that all adequate noncausal explanations reduce to this ontology, or that a particular original has been shown necessary. Those claims need their own premises. Keeping this allocation precise strengthens the argument by locating what is affirmed rather than allowing several conclusions to be carried by one ambiguous use of “complete.” [Productive totality, §§5, 7; current claims FND-004–005][s4] [Foundational claims][s8]

### 2.1 Required background and nonnecessitating production

An account can explain an occurrence through an actual productive background without claiming that this background necessitated that particular occurrence. This matters when indeterminism is offered as a defeater of the original-resource argument. Ameri's causal discussion explicitly considers an indeterministic interpretation as a concession within a wider argument that otherwise favours determinism. The concession preserves a physical setting with the requisite capacities and conditions. It does not turn that setting into nothing. [Causal foundations and the original resource bridge, §1; focused review][causal-background] [Focused causal-transfer review][causal-review]

The defensible argument has four steps. First, suppose the occurrence under discussion requires a particular obtaining background. Second, suppose that background can obtain without this occurrence. Third, the actual occurrence still establishes the actuality of its required background. Therefore the absence of necessitation does not establish the absence of every enabling reality. The first and second premises concern different directions of dependence: an event can require a condition that does not suffice for the event. A simple logical control allows three configurations of background and event: both absent, background present without the event, and both present. Every event in that model has its background, although not every instance of the background has the event. This illustrates the distinction; it is not a model of quantum physics or evidence that any particular physical theory has exactly this structure.

The conclusion earns a limited but positive explanatory credit. A proposed field, state, capacity or operative circumstance must be included in the account when the occurrence actually depends on it. Indeterminism alone does not license retaining its explanatory work while omitting its actuality. Nor does this require dismissing a probabilistic local explanation as no explanation. Such an explanation can answer a legitimate question about outcomes while leaving another question about the actuality of its background unanswered. [Causal foundations, §§1–2][causal-background]

That local result still falls short of original provision. Three targets must remain distinct: why this event occurs; why its enabling background exists; and whether a complete account of the received productive field includes an actual unreceived resource. An actual background may itself be wholly received. The proposition that an event requires it establishes neither that it is unreceived nor that one has already accounted for all the received reality used in the explanation. If the background is received and belongs within the target field, the complete productive question must include its actuality. The global adequacy argument above supplies the additional rationale; the local indeterministic example does not become an independent proof of it. [Causal foundations, §§1–2; contextual reconciliation][causal-background] [Causal context and explanatory scope][causal-context]

The distinction also fixes the meaning of Completion in section 3. Its resource must be actual, relevant to the received target, and unreceived. Its definition does not say that this resource by itself deterministically necessitates the effect. A genuinely original probabilistic productive resource would therefore not be excluded merely for failing to necessitate one particular outcome. Conversely, a deterministically sufficient but wholly received background would not acquire original status from its sufficiency. Determinism and original nonreceipt answer different questions. Neither a temporal first event nor sole entire production is built into that resource condition. [Causal foundations, §2; original resource/bearer interface][causal-background] [Original resource/bearer interface][s10]

Two further identifications remain substantive. A nomologically required condition is not automatically an efficient contributor: the truth of a law-proposition differs from an instantiated productive capacity. And identifying an actual background does not by itself identify a resource intrinsic to a particular bearer or establish that whole reception of the bearer carries reception of that resource in the same respect. Those are the separate Realisation and support-transport requirements. The later intrinsic-necessity and complete-source conclusions likewise need their own premises. Making the local occurrence deterministic would not supply them. [Causal foundations, §2; focused review][causal-background] [Focused causal-transfer review][causal-review]

The causal case also has affirmative epistemic content. A sound inferential relation between propositions is not yet an account of a person's arriving at a belief through appreciating that relation. In the latter case, the apprehended reasons must actually operate in the formation or maintenance of the belief; an accidentally matching conclusion is insufficient to show that the thinker believes it on those grounds. On the causal reading defended here, this calls for an operative, reason-sensitive cognitive route. It does not make a proposition an efficient producer merely because another proposition entails it. The source's argument thus supports an intelligible connection within actual thinking while preserving the distinction between logical support and productive activity. [Causal foundations, §3; focused review, “Causal intelligibility and selective brute existence”][causal-background] [Focused causal-transfer review][causal-review]

Empirical inquiry supplies a second, connected consideration. Investigating what a concrete thing can do concerns differentiated powers and the conditions of their exercise, rather than an entirely causally empty succession of appearances. On this account, experience can disclose causal structure without creating that structure merely by repeated association. These are positive reasons for taking stable causal relations seriously, not a deduction that every familiar expectation is a law or that every disputed causal theory is correct. Equally, considering an effect while leaving its source out of one's description does not show that the effect could exist without the requisite reality. Conceptual isolation and warranted metaphysical separability are different achievements. The causal claim still needs support for the particular connection asserted; neither the ease of imagining its absence nor the practical success of one investigation decides every such question. [Focused causal-transfer review, “Causal intelligibility and selective brute existence”][causal-review]

These considerations support causal intelligibility in cognition and the investigated world at their stated scope. They neither identify all explanatory relations with efficient production nor establish that every reality has a sufficient explanation. Moving from local cognitive dependence to an original background's intrinsic existential necessity would require an additional argument about that background and the actual epistemic route. The original-resource and intrinsic-adequacy arguments must therefore keep their own premises and rationale. [Causal foundations, §3][causal-background]

The strongest selective brute-original proposal is compatible with much of this causal argument. It can retain a concrete, beginningless productive reality, differentiated intrinsic powers, stable local causal order and appropriately connected cognition, while denying a sufficient explanation of that reality's own obtaining. Rejecting globally empty causation therefore does not yet reject that more selective claim. Equally, displaying the proposal does not establish its metaphysical possibility or defeat the affirmative intrinsic-adequacy judgment developed in sections 5–8. The disagreement concerns the original's existential adequacy, rather than whether local effects have operative sources. Inferential support between propositions must also not be identified without argument with efficient production between realities. [Causal foundations, §3; focused review][causal-background] [Focused causal-transfer review][causal-review]

Temporal claims require the same care. The source's local exclusion of a concurrent external cause does not follow from the impossibility of a thing producing itself: a distinct actual source can act concurrently with its effect without using the effect's nonexistent power. Ameri's later explicit distinction between causal and temporal priority permits that concurrence and controls interpretation of the book's considered position. His separate finite-past argument is not thereby identified with the beginningless-activity account used here. No new physical adjudication, universal causal principle or proof of original uniqueness follows from this bounded causal comparison. Its contribution is the exact separation of required actuality, outcome necessitation and original provision. [Focused causal-transfer review, “The local temporal inference”; causal foundations, §4][causal-review] [Causal foundations][causal-background]


The distinction between temporal order and productive dependence also determines what regress analogies can establish. An unbacked cheque does not supply the funds it promises merely because another equally unbacked cheque is offered behind it. Likewise, if every purported authorization only postpones the exercise of authority to another step, the description has not yet supplied an actual exercise that authorizes the action. The relevant defect is the missing operative resource or authority. It is not established merely by counting infinitely many links: a finite collection of promises without the required backing does not acquire that backing from its finitude either. [Causal foundations, §4][causal-background]

To transfer such an argument to a beginningless succession, one must establish the same dependence structure. Having no first temporal member does not by itself show that every occurrence lacks an actual enabling basis, that every productive resource is merely promised, or that a standing producer is unavailable at every stage. A proposed history in which each particular occurrence has an actual enabling basis is therefore not answered simply by renaming it an infinite chain of unfulfilled permissions. Conversely, describing such a history does not establish its metaphysical possibility, the adequacy of its whole productive account, or the absence of an original resource. The complete-field argument asks whether the received actuality used throughout has been provided; a temporal-regress argument must establish its own premise about successive origination. Neither question can be settled by substituting the other's conclusion. [Causal foundations, §4; section 2 above][causal-background]

Ibn Taymiyya's discussion of time in *Minhāj al-sunna al-nabawiyya* makes a relevant distinction explicit. Time as a measure of motion is not confined to one particular motion such as that of the sun. His account connects continuing voluntary speech and activity with the times in which particular products arise, while maintaining that each particular product is originated. Continuing activity and an individually beginningless product are consequently not interchangeable claims in this passage. This gives a positive textual reason to keep his account distinct from an argument requiring a first member of every succession. It is a source-specific doctrinal distinction, not a new cosmological observation or a proof that every proposed beginningless history is possible. [*Minhāj*, discussion of time, motion and particular products][minhaj-time]

A shared definition of time, or a citation of a reported consensus, cannot by itself identify two authors' complete arguments about the past. The scope of the definition and the alleged agreement both require independent support. No universal theological consensus is assumed here. A proposed beginning of the observed cosmos must likewise be distinguished from a beginning of all productive reality; establishing either requires evidence appropriate to that target. The present argument does not import unverified physical or comparative-scriptural premises to cross that boundary. [Causal foundations, §4; contextual reconciliation][causal-background] [Causal context and explanatory scope][causal-context]

#### Cosmological confirmation and the wise-design fallback

Ameri's wider case assigns different tasks to causal reasoning, physical cosmology and design. He presents his rational argument for temporal origination as independently conclusive, then treats scientific cosmology as corroboration. This reconstructs the source's position; it does not transfer that claimed conclusiveness to the original-resource argument above. Nor does the indeterministic-background result by itself establish a finite past. Its conclusion concerns an actual required basis, whereas a beginning argument must establish the relevant temporal premise. [Cosmology context, “Main finding” and §§1–3, reported book pp. 87–114][ameri-cosmology-context]

The source expressly recognizes that a beginning of the observed universe would not alone prove a beginning of every wider process. The missing step requires an argument about the proposed wider setting, rather than a change of name from “our universe” to “all physical reality.” Ameri consequently considers eternal alternatives and offers further objections to them. His final fallback has a different positive target: even if an alleged wider structure were eternal, its carefully ordered character could still require wise design. That conditional explanatory argument leaves the temporal premise open. It can therefore support a design conclusion without proving a first event; conversely, a beginning alone does not supply the explanatory account of the order. Each route needs its own premises. [Cosmology context, §§4–6, especially the reported discussions at pp. 126 and 129–131][ameri-cosmology-context]

The alternatives must be individuated carefully. Cyclicity, a past without a first member and a future without an end are different claims; the source can reject one while allowing another. A temporal beginning also need not be identified with a singular mathematical point. In considering vacuum production, claims about the ages, persistence, collisions or visibility of products require the corresponding physical model. An eternal producer does not by that description make every individual product eternal. Yet merely allowing successive finite products would not answer a particular observational prediction if that model's premises actually entailed it. Likewise, a permanently motionless material state and an already active vacuum do not present the same problem about the onset of change. For the motionless case, Ameri asks whether the first change has a cause or is causeless. He rejects an uncaused transition and attributes the caused alternative to a nonmaterial entity beyond time and the inert cosmos, explicitly assigning it ontological rather than earlier temporal priority. His physical supplement invokes energy or heat from outside; that auxiliary claim is reported here, not independently established. These distinctions preserve the positive force of a properly specified causal or empirical objection without turning it into an unrestricted conclusion about all beginningless activity. [Cosmology context, §§3–6 and “Relevance and limits for eternal successive activity”][ameri-cosmology-context]

Scientific support retains its conditions and evidential dependence. The contextual report describes a twenty-seven-item inventory substantially mediated through Hugh Ross, not twenty-seven independently authenticated proofs. Assertions about heat death, expansion-based past incompleteness or the dark night sky concern stated physical domains and hypotheses; their stronger universal paraphrases need additional justification. Testimony about scientific opinion is evidence of another kind, and an allegation about an opponent's motives supplies no further measurement. These limits do not reduce a cumulative case to no case. They identify what would have to be checked before its components could independently support the conclusion. The report's possible wording anomaly in the page 130 recap remains a textual question, not permission to silently emend the book or reverse its overall argument. [Cosmology context, §§2–3 and “Textual and argumentative cautions”][ameri-cosmology-context]

This cosmological programme must also be kept distinct from the affirmative *Minhāj* account already discussed. Criticism of a specified material cosmology does not by itself address continuing voluntary divine activity with individually originated products. Ameri's finite-past commitment and Ibn Taymiyya's account cannot be identified merely because both use a motion-related concept of time. Their relevant premises and objects differ. The contextual source preserves that difference while allowing the causal-background argument to retain its own positive contribution. [Causal context, “Eternal production and successive products”][causal-context] [Cosmology context, “Relevance and limits for eternal successive activity”][ameri-cosmology-context]

#### Scriptural identification and positive corroboration

The comparative-scriptural argument begins after the causal case. It first asks whether a tradition, correctly interpreted, is consistent with the independently defended account of creation. Consistency can satisfy that initial condition without establishing the tradition's truth. Ameri then advances a stronger positive argument: the Qur'an's alleged divergence from inherited cosmological descriptions, together with its claimed agreement with the independently supported account, is offered as evidence for revelation. The intended inference assumes that the Qur'an is well acquainted with biblical tradition yet omits or corrects the cited features without an available seventh-century scientific explanation. On that premise, familiarity with the earlier tradition makes the divergences an explanatory question rather than merely a lack of contact. Ameri includes the proposed rejection of a solid firmament and of water as the material source of the entire cosmos among these contrasts. The historical-availability assumption and the interpretation of each contrast remain premises to be justified; agreement alone does not establish them. Nor can a scriptural identification retroactively supply the causal case's missing original-resource or practical-basing premise. Keeping the steps distinct preserves the affirmative corroborative argument rather than reducing the appendix to a catalogue of compatible statements. [Scriptural context, “Main finding,” “Why insert the comparison here” and “The Qur'an and Sunna as a positive alternative,” especially the reported book pp. 240–246][ameri-scriptural-context]

Both sides of the comparison require cumulative interpretation. A creation verb taken alone need not settle whether antecedent matter is denied; Ameri's positive Islamic case likewise appeals to several terms and their contexts. Competing readings of Genesis are acknowledged. An account of arranging pre-existing matter is weaker than a claim that the matter is beginningless, so the former cannot simply substitute for the latter. An appeal to later Christian texts also does not, without the necessary interpretive premise, settle the meaning of the earlier passage. Criticism of a harmonization or a scriptural chronology remains distinct from the validity of a cosmological proof presented by a Christian. [Scriptural context, “Genesis and creation from nothing,” “Scientific chronology and competing Christian responses” and “The Qur'an and Sunna as a positive alternative”][ameri-scriptural-context]

The positive alternative has its own internal controls. Ameri's use of Qur'an and Sunna includes a filter on hadith authenticity, distinctions between initial material production, its ordering and later terrestrial preparation, and an acknowledged difference from the reported Ibn Abbas sequence. The concessions have substantive content. Similarities between Babylonian and biblical narratives may, on Ameri's account, coexist with an inherited true narrative supplemented by borrowed details; similarity need not imply total fabrication. Albright's support for a temporal translation is reported alongside his rejection of direct borrowing, so agreement on the translation cannot be counted as agreement on that historical explanation. Ameri also acknowledges capable defenders of the traditional translation, distinguishes the duration of Sproul's six creation days from Earth's present age, and praises Schroeder's anti-atheist argumentation while criticizing his biblical harmonization. His objections consequently do not erase every positive contribution by the interlocutors he criticizes. These qualifications constrain the comparison; they do not erase its proposed positive conclusion. At the same time, the source's reported judgments about transmission and authenticity are not independently established here. A chronology of fossils is not, merely as such, endorsement of a theory of biological descent, and an interpretation of creation periods does not by itself determine an exact age for humanity. [Scriptural context, “Scientific chronology and competing Christian responses,” “The Qur'an and Sunna as a positive alternative” and “Qualifications that must survive synthesis”][ameri-scriptural-context]

The distinction between source, act and product remains decisive. Creation without antecedent material does not alone entail that there was a first divine act. Conversely, continuing divine activity does not make a particular created product beginningless. The scriptural appendix is not an independent primary witness for the whole Taymiyyan ontology, and its isolated attribution of criticism of the Saturday-creation report cannot supply that larger doctrine. The affirmative account of continuing voluntary activity and originated particulars above consequently remains intact; neither author's position is silently rewritten to make the comparison easier. [Scriptural context, “Use in T20 necessity and agency”][ameri-scriptural-context]

Specific checks must stay proportionate to their consequences. Using only the reported values 4.5 and 13.7 gives the ratio 45/137, approximately 0.32847, which is less than one third by 2/411. The comparison is approximate, not an exact equality; this arithmetic neither updates cosmological estimates nor refutes the broader concordance argument. The contextual report separately flags a printed negation, an attributed Ibn Hazm quotation boundary and a conflated bibliographic entry. Those are leads for exact collation, not established primary-source errors or general defeaters. Bibliographic totals also do not certify independent consultation of every listed work, especially where the source says some materials were omitted from the list. [Scriptural context, “Local verification cautions,” “Primary-check queue” and “Apparatus inspection”][ameri-scriptural-context]

These two contextual returns support a source-grounded reconstruction of the arguments and their transitions. They do not constitute fresh authentication of physical theories, biblical philology, hadith criticism or classical editions. The focused causal-transfer review expressly limits its final endorsement to the focal report and timing control, rather than independently reviewing both contextual programmes. The positive causal, design and scriptural arguments are therefore retained with distinct warrants: the already-retained local causal inference, a reported wider cosmological case and its conditional design fallback, and a comparative revelation argument whose additional premises remain explicit. No one of these warrants is silently borrowed to complete another. [Focused causal-transfer review, “Scope and novelty” and “Final report rebinding”][causal-review]

### 2.2 Standing resources and a selected occurrence

The distinction between required actuality and outcome necessitation also fixes the status of a proposed comparison between a standing necessary bearer and one realized occurrence. A probability law can specify an experiment's possible realizations without identifying which realization obtains. Supplying a realized assignment can determine the endpoint under a given outcome map, but that supplied coordinate is not automatically an antecedent hidden variable or an explanation of its own selection. The actual background, the law, the realized productive exercise and the selected event remain different objects of explanation. [R18-G145]

The prospective source proposed to connect one unguarded productive route and a singleton endpoint to the already defined probability-model and resource/bearer interfaces. Its planned discrimination compared a standing bearer and law, a supplied realized success coordinate, and the full premise package for an actual original resource and bearer. It explicitly retained nonvacuous contingency and the receipt interpretation rather than replacing the latter by the endpoint equation alone. The outcome map can determine its result **conditional on** the realization while the particular realization still calls for its own account. The proposed comparison also allowed a particular intrinsic act to vary without treating that variation as whole-existence receipt of its bearer. [R18-G145]

That prospective document is a design record, not a report that the proposed composed model was built or checked. Its stop condition required a verified interface witness and a matrix of omitted premises, or a concrete obstruction. The body supplies neither completed outcome. In particular, it does not establish an all-pure-perfection interpretation, the wisdom of a selected event, a complete actual cause, or physical eligibility. Its omission of these premises is part of the scientific scope, not permission to treat them as satisfied. The original-bearer proof in §3 remains the already established conditional argument; neither this prospective experiment nor a law-to-endpoint calculation is counted as another proof of its application. [R18-G145]


**The completed diagnostic.** A later construction realizes the prospective comparison without enlarging its metaphysical claims. It retains exactly the seven original-bearer premises of §3: actual target occurrence, original completion, realization, support transport, receipt representation, contingency-as-need and constitutive reception. Its two-index fixture has an actual index $w=0$, an original bearer $b=0$ existing at both indices, and a received bearer $b=1$ existing only at $w=0$. The same original resource and bearer witness satisfy the necessity and essential-nonreceipt conclusions; contingency and receipt are not made vacuous. Here $0,1$ denote the source's Boolean values `false,true`. [Completed diagnostic][productive-scope-report] [Exact fixture][productive-scope-fixture]

One nonempty route has success and failure realizations of mass $1/2$ each under a fixed normalized law. With realization $u_w(*)=\neg w$, its endpoint is

$$
E(u_0)=\{*\},\qquad E(u_1)=\varnothing,
\qquad \operatorname{Exists}(w,b=1)\iff *\in E(u_w).
$$

This last equivalence is an **additional endpoint/bearer correspondence**. The framework's actual-only `targetReceived : T → Prop` has no world argument and belongs to a different sort: it must not be identified with existence of the contingent $B$-bearer. Its target occurrence remains true even when $b=1$ is absent at the alternative index. The construction therefore preserves the original premise package rather than silently replacing its target predicate by the endpoint equation. [Scope proof][productive-scope-proof] [Resolved interface qualifications][productive-scope-review]

The two endpoints differ while the law and original bearer's existence remain fixed. No endpoint-valued function of a single `Unit` input can reproduce both: it would give $f(*)=\{*\}$ and $f(*)=\varnothing$. But `Unit` is only a fixed-record proxy, **not** a representation of the complete essence, reasons or productive conditions. Conversely, equal supplied realizations have equal endpoints by ordinary function congruence. Neither calculation explains selection of the realization, makes it a prior hidden variable, or authenticates a causal interpretation. The result concerns what these declared inputs determine, not the impossibility of a genuine stochastic cause. [Scope proof][productive-scope-proof]

A separate `Act` signature assigns one token at each index without assigning the same token everywhere. This coexists with the seven premises because those premises do not constrain the added occurrence relation; even its nonemptiness is additional, not derived. No intrinsic-bearer relation, willing, wisdom, causal efficacy, temporal history or nonreceipt of an act is established. A type distinction is thus not a proof of intrinsic divine willing or of the stronger always-active doctrine. [Resolved interface qualifications][productive-scope-review]

The substantive comparison remains the one developed in §§12.9–12.10. The retained source appraisal requires particular differentiating determination of willing, not an unexplained token called “will”; it grants no reasonless divine-choice exception. It does not thereby prove a unique maximizing reason-set or an external necessitator. Its affirmative perfection argument joins independence, effective power and informed wise agency, rather than defining a rival out of eligibility. The thin diagnostic neither preserves that entire account nor defeats it. The saved review reports a bounded dependency replay and source appraisal, not an unrestricted rebuild or complete-work authentication; the present reconciliation inspects the exact proof and relevant declarations without new Lean execution or primary-source authentication. [Completed diagnostic][productive-scope-report] [Historical bounded review][productive-scope-review]

<a id="f250-a-conditioned-and-comprehensive"></a>

#### Conditioned causes and comprehensive original agency

The *Ṣafadiyya* reconstruction makes the scope of a causal claim decisive. A finite source can produce a different outcome when an independently supplied recipient becomes ready: sunlight reaches a place after a roof or cloud is removed without requiring a corresponding new intrinsic act in the sun. An alleged active intellect is likewise not independently complete if other sources furnish the recipient's preparation. The reply concerning the comprehensive Creator is different because those preparations are themselves among what that Creator produces. This provides a reason to require an account of the new conditions within the comprehensive account. It is not a theorem that every contributing source, merely as a source, must independently supply every requisite. [F250-A067-43-59] [F250-A067-553-561] [F250-A000-31-47] [F250-A145-55-63]

The positive alternative does not make original agency wait for its own prior production. It distinguishes “he cannot act until he acts,” which presupposes agency before its origin, from “he does this after another act,” which can describe successive acts of an already effective bearer. S002L521 explicitly allows a particular creation to be conditional on another creation while denying that original creatorhood depends on an external giver. It also distinguishes efficacy in general, efficacy toward this particular and efficacy toward everything. Permanent agency therefore need not be one permanent act-token, and a permanent type of intransitive activity does not by itself entail a created product. These restrictions preserve the source's affirmative continuous-activity account rather than replacing it with a model of complete inactivity. [F250-A067-61-75] [F250-A067-445-453] [F250-A067-519-527] [F250-A221-9-42]

Complete present determination is itself more specific than the availability of an earlier enabling capacity. In the source's voluntary account, complete Power and decisive Will entail the intended act; that is not necessitation by a bare unwilled essence. Conversely, pure absence does not efficiently produce an occurrence. Removal of an obstacle may still matter as part of the positive complex that becomes effective. Nor should all language of contemporaneity be read as strict simultaneity: the later act/product discussion allows immediate succession and treats the hand, ring and key motions as correlated effects of an agent rather than automatically identifying one motion as the complete efficient maker of the other. These are qualifications on a historical causal account, not new measurements of physical time. [F250-A067-85-99] [F250-A067-597-609] [F250-A067-621-647] [F250-A052-13-39]

Finally, a real natural power is not an exhaustive explanation merely because it can produce some effects of a broad kind. The work expressly grants created powers, psychic contributions and prayer's causal relevance while requiring conditions and allowing impediments. Establishing a capacity, its possible reach, its actual operation in the case and the exclusion of other causes are separate steps. The opening rejection of reducing every prophetic sign to psychic powers consequently does not deny secondary efficacy, and the converse inference from one conceded psychic effect to a complete account of all signs fails as well. [F250-A067-153-157] [F250-A067-175-214] [F250-A067-268-280] [F250-A186-7-38] [F250-A206-7-56]

## 3. From an original resource to its actual bearer

The retained formal interface separates a **target**, a **resource**, and a **bearer**. A resource is intended to be a concrete intrinsic instantiation in the same existential respect as the receipt question. It is not an arbitrary true proposition or an unrestricted explanatory fact. The following notation makes the existing conditional reasoning explicit. [Original resource/bearer interface][s10]

| Notation | Meaning in the declared interpretation |
|---|---|
| $`a`$ | The actual world |
| $`E(w,g)`$ | Bearer g exists at world w |
| $`D_T(t)`$ | Target t is received |
| $`A_R(r)`$, $`D_R(r)`$ | Resource r is actual, and resource r is received |
| $`I(g,r)`$ | Resource r is intrinsic to bearer g |
| $`V(r,t)`$ | Resource r is relevant to target t |
| $`D_B(w,g)`$ | g is wholly received at w in the specified existential respect |

The interface states three relevant premises:

```math
\begin{aligned}
\text{Completion:}\quad
&\forall t\,[D_T(t)\Rightarrow
  \exists r\,(V(r,t)\land A_R(r)\land\neg D_R(r))],\\
\text{Realisation:}\quad
&\forall r\,[A_R(r)\Rightarrow
  \exists g\,(E(a,g)\land I(g,r))],\\
\text{Support transport:}\quad
&\forall g,r\,[E(a,g)\land I(g,r)\land D_B(a,g)
  \Rightarrow D_R(r)].
\end{aligned}
```

**Conditional bearer result.** Given a received target t and these premises, there are a resource r and a bearer g such that r is actual, unreceived, and relevant to t; r is intrinsic to g; and g actually exists without whole receipt in the specified respect. [Interface, `original_bearer_of_completion`][s10]

**Proof.** Completion applied to the actual received target supplies r with $`V(r,t)`$, $`A_R(r)`$, and $`\neg D_R(r)`$. Realisation supplies g with $`E(a,g)`$ and $`I(g,r)`$. Suppose $`D_B(a,g)`$. Support transport would then yield $`D_R(r)`$, contradicting the resource's unreceived status. Hence $`\neg D_B(a,g)`$. The same t, r, and g satisfy the complete witness statement. This is the reasoning implemented by `original_bearer_of_resource` followed by `original_bearer_of_completion`. [Original resource/bearer interface][s10]

The proof uses no modal necessity premise. It also does not infer a bearer merely from the truth of a sentence: Realisation concerns the stated actual resource domain. Its support transport is a claim about receipt in the same existential respect, not about mere concomitance. The proof establishes the conditional inference; the argument for applying its premises to actual reality remains philosophical. In the field application, Completion receives its warrant from global productive adequacy, while the concrete-resource and receipt interpretations must be maintained through Realisation and transport. [Productive totality, §5; interface opening and definitions][s4] [Original resource/bearer interface][s10]

The intended breadth of whole-existence receipt matters. A real contribution by a dependent reality is compatible with its needing an external existential contribution. Receipt must not be defined to require total passivity and then negated to produce a spurious conclusion of complete independence. Conversely, intrinsic qualification or necessary co-obtaining is not automatically foreign existential receipt. The later application check explicitly preserves both points. [Restored result and operation decision, §2C][s7]

For the philosophical continuation, retain this actual g. The next question is whether its existential character warrants necessity. The witness is not replaced by the fruit, a proposition, or a different original selected for each alternative. [Affirmative intrinsic-necessity argument, §§1, 7][s1]

## 4. The strongest collective alternative

A serious objection to global productive adequacy need not offer another all-received causal chain. The inherited comparison considers a stronger qualitative proposal: an autonomous obtaining basis explains a structure collectively, and existential laws determine the dependent history within it. All concrete productive resources in that history might remain received. The proposal challenges whether complete existential explanation must include an original productive resource in the specified sense. Its explanatory ambition should be taken seriously before assessing whether it reaches that conclusion. [Productive totality, §§6–8][s4]

The proposal has positive arguments behind its separate components. Dasgupta's 2009 qualitative-first account appeals to symmetry and ontological economy: a fundamental description in terms of universals and obtaining states can avoid treating primitive material individuals as additional unexplained structure, while allowing derivative individual discourse. That is an argument about material ontology, not an elimination of every entity, bearer or possible immaterial source. The 2014 argument for collective grounding appeals abductively to coordinated discourse and actual linguistic judgments: some facts are more adequately explained together than by assigning a separate fundamental explanation to each. This is substantive evidence for an explanatory form, beyond the mere availability of plural syntax. It does not by itself establish the proposed qualitative ontology or account for the obtaining basis's own actuality. [Productive totality, §§6–7][s4] [Dasgupta 2009][d09] [Dasgupta 2014][d14]

The 2016 autonomy proposal distinguishes an autonomous ground from an unexplained fact that remains apt for further grounding. Its qualitative existence-grounding alternatives therefore deserve separate assessment: autonomy is meant to answer an explanatory demand, not simply to label a brute stopping point. The inherited reading does not, however, supply an actual qualitative essence that covers this complete productive field. The law-relative alternative is likewise strongest when its laws have existential content. Removing that content to make nonexistence easy would weaken the objection. The unresolved question is the laws' warranted existential authority and coverage of the resources and bearers at issue. The underlying Billon paper was not completely available to the inherited inquiry; this exposition does not fill that evidential gap or claim a full-paper adjudication. [Productive totality, §6][s4] [Dasgupta 2016][d16] [Law-relative proposal and access boundary][b23]

These arguments support taking qualitative ontology, collective explanation and autonomy seriously at their respective scopes. Their conjunction—an autonomous qualitative basis with existential laws covering the whole received productive field while excluding every original productive resource—is a proposed synthesis, not a result jointly established by those sources. The positive evidence must be preserved without transferring the warrant of each component to that stronger conjunction. [Productive totality, §§6–7][s4]

Three cases need different treatment. First, if the proposed basis Q is simply the contingent obtaining arrangement of the received field, collective explanatory form has not yet established Q's adequacy for its own obtaining. An account may correctly explain why the relevant explanandum is collective while leaving the actuality of the obtaining basis itself unprovided. Calling Q fundamental relative to individualistic descriptions does not by itself establish autonomy in the existential respect under discussion. The objection here does not require reducing every collective explanation to a list of separate explanations of primitive individuals. [Productive totality, §6][s4]

Second, suppose Q is independently warranted as intrinsically adequate and autonomous. It would then supply an original explanatory basis in a broader sense. The dispute is whether it also supplies, or must coexist with, original productive actuality. The defender's reason is that an account of received production must cover its actual productive prerequisites. The rival replies that autonomous noncausal grounding can settle actuality while all local production occurs within the grounded field. An additional original productive stock would then be unnecessary. The positive productive judgment bears the burden here; changing the word “ground” into “resource” would not settle it. [Productive totality, §§6, 8][s4]

An alternative adequate description also does not automatically establish that original productive resources are absent. Noncausal and productive accounts might coexist. To rebut the specific Completion claim for F, a proposed case must warrant both the actual received target and the relevant absence of an actual unreceived concrete productive resource. To undercut the inference, it can instead give an independent reason why the productive-adequacy judgment is unreliable or inapplicable. An undercutter need not prove the opposite conclusion or describe an entire alternative cosmos. Its reason must nevertheless reach the target and explanatory sense actually used. [Productive totality, §7][s4]

Third, a qualitative-first proposal could allow an actual independent concrete field with an intrinsic unreceived productive resource. Under an established intrinsic relation and the same receipt interpretation, that field could qualify as a bearer in the broad interface. It would then satisfy the relevant original-resource commitment rather than refute it. The interface does not require a primitive material individual or a personal agent. A true assertion about a field, the content of that assertion, an obtaining state, and a concrete field bearing resources remain different candidates; their substitution requires argument. [Productive totality, §6][s4]

The comparison leaves a precise result. Collective or qualitative explanation has positive philosophical significance, but it does not by itself entail the denial of original productive provision. The source argument supplies a substantive reason for global productive adequacy while leaving its exhaustive application across rival ontologies open to appropriate criticism. The current foundational record retains the affirmative, defeasible judgment; the existence of that applicability question does not itself count as a new defeater. Nor may the positive side insulate itself by defining every adequate ground to be the kind of productive resource it seeks. [Productive totality, §§7–8; current claim FND-004][s4] [Foundational claims][s8]

### 4.1 Qualitative description and collective grounding

The qualitative alternative becomes sharper when its language, modal claims and explanatory claim are kept distinct. The source appraisal of Dasgupta's *The Bare Necessities* treats grounding as noncausal metaphysical explanation, with talk of facts serving a sentential explanatory apparatus rather than automatically introducing another class of abstract objects. A claim about whether space exists differs from a claim about whether it depends on matter. Likewise, the manifold, metric and other mathematical ingredients of a physical model do not by themselves decide the ontology of the represented world. Necessary co-obtaining also leaves explanatory direction open: a necessitarian theology can still distinguish a ground from what it grounds. This compatibility observation is not an endorsement of such a theology by the author under discussion. [R18-G302, §2][R18-G302]

The Hole Argument supplies a reason to inspect the interpretation of apparently different models, but it does not alone prove qualitative priority. One can revise a determinism claim, deny that a proposed pair represents distinct possibilities, or adopt a suitable counterpart interpretation. Even agreement that two particular models represent one world does not prove that no other distinct possibilities exist. A view retaining substantive individuals can share some antihaecceitist modal claims. Thus modal covariance, qualitative discernibility and metaphysical grounding cannot be substituted for one another. The positive qualitative proposal still needs an obtaining basis and an explanation of the derivative individualistic truths. [R18-G302, §2][R18-G302]

Its economy argument is correspondingly conditional and defeasible. If the physical theory supplies the relevant complete laws, allegedly surplus distinctions may add no discriminable explanatory work. This is a comparative reason to prefer the leaner account, not the verificationist principle that every undetectable distinction is unreal. Absolute velocity, for example, can affect later absolute velocities within the theory that posits it; the alleged redundancy is not absence of any consequence whatsoever. The truth of a law and its status as a law are further distinct questions. Reliable indexical answers likewise need not discriminate the proposed surplus. These qualifications preserve the positive motivation while preventing it from becoming an automatic proof of the whole ontology. [R18-G302, §2][R18-G302]

The algebraic qualitative language retains relations, equality and numerical plurality. Its two-sphere illustration has the form

```math
c\,c\,(F\mathbin{\&}pF\mathbin{\&}R
                 \mathbin{\&}\sigma R\mathbin{\&}\neg I).
```

With the declared operations, this says that two distinct $`F`$-witnesses stand in $`R`$ in both directions. It does **not** say that these are the only two objects or that the displayed predicates describe the complete world; totality clauses would be additional. Nor does it require every individual to have a unique qualitative role. The finite extensional proof and its exact padding and permutation conventions appear in [Tensor Moments, §§1.5–1.9](../mathematics/tensor-moments-and-corrective-dynamics.md#15-finite-relations-as-boolean-tensors). That proof preserves the described truth conditions; it does not establish a direction of grounding. If weak discernibility is meant to supply a substantive qualitative distinction, simply using inequality as its own discriminator would not answer that further question. [R18-G273, §§2, 6–7][R18-G273] [R18-G302, §3][R18-G302]

The source's distinctive explanatory proposal is plural on the **grounded** side. Let $`Q`$ express the obtaining of the complete qualitative state, let $`Y`$ be the complete plurality of the relevant individualistic facts, and let $`e_b\in Y`$ express the existence of a particular region. Write $`G(X,Y)`$ schematically for the proposed grounding explanation. Its relevant form is

```math
G(\{Q\},Y),
```

while it rejects a separate qualitative explanation $`G(\{Q\},\{e_b\})`$ of that individualistic fact taken alone. This is more specific than allowing several grounds for one conclusion. It proposes that individualistic facts can all be nonfundamental without each having an individual qualitative ground. The concern that the whole cosmos is an unsuitable separate explanation of just one person's existence motivates that proposal; it does not by itself settle every question about plural explanatory adequacy. The 2011 discussion defers fuller defense of the plural form. [R18-G300, §§1–3][R18-G300] [R18-G302, §3][R18-G302]

The 2014 development supplies a positive reason for collective adequacy, beyond removing objections to singleton explanations. Within the assumed relational account of mass, coordinated numerical predicates recover underlying mass ratios without requiring a privileged material standard or an additional intrinsic magnitude for each object. The proposed explanation identifies what makes the assertions true as a system. Their coordinated role is a reason to assess explanatory completeness at that level, rather than demand separately parcelled fundamental grounds. The source also tests the connection to ordinary discourse with apparent-standard cases involving a nonexistent standard and one half as massive as believed; its support is not confined to a stipulated fictional language. The analogy for individuals appeals to the coordinated quantificational role of singular terms, although its development here is less extensive. [collective-adequacy] [collective-adequacy-review]

This is substantive, defeasible explanatory support conditional on the qualitative or relational ontology, not a deduction of metaphysical priority from linguistic usefulness. An opponent may accept the representational success while disputing whether it explains the nonsemantic facts, but must address that positive case rather than require distributivity by definition. Ordinary compositional truth conditions and higher-level explanations through particular origins or constituents remain available. A proper subset of individualistic facts may be plurally grounded, with others grounded singly in it. Thus neither ordinary existence questions nor every singular explanation becomes meaningless. Conversely, changing the apt fundamental explanandum does not establish that the obtaining qualitative basis is actual, autonomous or existentially adequate through itself. The whole-field question in §4.3 remains. [collective-adequacy]

### 4.2 Modal projection does not distribute a ground

Suppose the joint explanatory assertion is used factively: $`Q`$ and all the members of $`Y`$ obtain. Suppose also the source's plural necessitation condition: whenever the grounds obtain, all the grounded facts obtain. For a possibly infinite plurality this is a metalanguage condition, not a tacit infinite conjunction in a finitary formula. For each particular $`e_b\in Y`$, it yields

```math
\Box(Q\longrightarrow e_b).
```

**Reason.** At any world satisfying $`Q`$, plural necessitation supplies every member of $`Y`$, hence this member. The same pointwise implication holds throughout the modal range. This uses projection of truth from a plurality. It does not project the grounding relation itself. [R18-G300, §§2–3][R18-G300]

The rejected extra step would be

```math
G(\{Q\},Y)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad G(\{Q\},\{e_b\}).
```

That is right-distribution of grounding, the very principle the proposed interpretation denies. It cannot be obtained by reversing necessitation: necessary implication is not sufficient for grounding. Treating $`Y`$ as a conjunction and applying conjunction elimination **inside the grounding operator** likewise adds an explanatory rule, rather than merely using ordinary truth-functional logic. Factivity supplies the actual $`e_b`$ but not its separate ground. [R18-G300, §3][R18-G300]

Transitivity does not silently supply the missing rule. The source's single-output schema has the shape

```math
G(X,\{z\})\ \land\ G(U\cup\{z\},\{v\})
   \quad\Longrightarrow\quad G(X\cup U,\{v\}).
```

The plural output $`Y`$ is not the singleton output required by that first premise. One can propose a whole-plurality extension,

```math
G(X,Y)\ \land\ G(Y\cup Z,V)
   \quad\Longrightarrow\quad G(X\cup Z,V),
```

but applying it to derive a singleton output still requires an additional grounding premise from the intermediate plurality to that singleton. The membership $`e_b\in Y`$ is not such a premise. Similarly, irreflexivity is an explanatory constraint; it is not a license to regard a collection as explaining a member merely because the collection entails it. The source changes the logical form of grounding without providing a complete revised plural calculus, so this mapping analysis does not certify consistency of every intended plural axiom. It identifies the precise unprovided step in the attempted distribution. A substantive criticism of plural adequacy remains possible; replacing the advertised proposal by a distributive one would address a different proposal. [R18-G300, §§2–3][R18-G300]

Fine-grained explanatory roles must also survive translation between languages. An ordinary first-order existential assertion $`P`$ can be an extensional counterpart of an algebraic obtaining assertion $`Q`$ while having a different grounding role. The 2011 paper's note 74 allows ordinary existential truths to be grounded in their individual instances; their algebraic qualitative counterpart is intended as fundamental in the proposed explanation. Extensional equivalence therefore does not authorize identifying the assertions inside $`G`$. The intended direction can be qualitative obtaining, then the collectively grounded individualistic facts, then ordinary existential truth, without treating the three descriptions as three newly introduced concrete objects. This attribution sharpens the comparison already made in §4; it does not discover a new logical flaw in the existing productive argument. [R18-G300, §§1, 3][R18-G300] [R18-G302, §3][R18-G302]

The 2014 treatment makes a further distinction between primitive ground G and its derivative closure D. Writing $`+`$ for collecting the indicated pluralities, its two context-preserving patterns are

```math
G(X,Y),\ G(Y+U,Z)\ \Longrightarrow\ D(X+U,Z),
```

```math
G(X,Y+U),\ G(Y,Z)\ \Longrightarrow\ D(X,U+Z).
```

The corresponding derivative steps can iterate, but primitive G is not thereby assumed transitive or identified with D. The first rule preserves unused input U; the second preserves unused output U. Neither permits arbitrary logical-equivalence substitution, deletion of explananda or addition of irrelevant grounds. “Accounting for” a logical consequence of a plurally grounded body is a weaker relation than grounding that consequence with the required relevance. [collective-rules] [collective-adequacy-review]

For example, write the individualistic plurality as $`\{e\}+J`$ and let E mean that something exists. Even granting the additional grounding premise $`G(\{e\},\{E\})`$, the second rule yields only $`D(\{Q\},J+\{E\})`$ from $`G(\{Q\},\{e\}+J)`$. If J is nonempty, that step does not erase it to yield $`D(\{Q\},\{E\})`$. A separately justified premise grounding E in the whole intermediate plurality would permit that derivative conclusion by the first rule. Likewise, a substantive premise that the conjuncts ground their conjunction can yield derivative grounding of the conjunction; it does not make the conjunction ground each conjunct. The source's objection to a conjunction-only reconstruction is an explanatory assessment of that arrangement, not a general ban on multiple complete grounds: it explicitly permits alternative full grounds of a true disjunction. No causal nonduplication or common-original-source theorem follows from this objection. [collective-rules]

### 4.3 A whole received field remains an available target

The failure of right-distribution does not negate Completion. Completion in §3 concerns an actual received target and an actual unreceived resource productively relevant to it. It does not mention $`G`$. Even a valid extraction of a separate ground would leave the need to establish the target's receipt, a concrete intrinsic resource, productive relevance and nonreceipt, an actual bearer, and transport of receipt in the same respect. An obtaining assertion or a universal is not automatically that resource. Conversely, successful collective grounding does not show that no original productive resource coexists with it. Failure of one argument for Completion is not proof of its negation. [R18-G300, §4][R18-G300]

The affirmative route has a stronger response than demanding distributivity: take the relevant whole field as the target. Suppose that field is an actual received target $`t`$, Completion supplies $`r`$ actual, relevant and unreceived, Realisation supplies an actual $`g`$ with $`I(g,r)`$, and Support transport applies. If $`g`$ were wholly received, transport would make $`r`$ received, contradicting the selected resource. Thus the same conditional original-bearer argument in §3 applies to this whole target. Its proof uses neither a distinct resource for every individual nor a singleton grounding explanation for every member of the field. [R18-G300, §5][R18-G300]

This is an application of the existing conditional theorem, not a second proof of actual global adequacy. The whole field's eligibility as a received target, and the relevant productive resource, remain to be warranted. A whole target need not itself be one individual or one intrinsic resource. Calling a state qualitative does not exclude every broad interpretation of a bearer, but identifying it with an actual concrete resource-bearing field requires argument. The strongest rival and the affirmative therefore continue to disagree over the exhaustive applicability and warrant of productive Completion, rather than over a distributive rule that the original-bearer inference never needed. [R18-G300, §§4–5][R18-G300] [R18-G302, §4][R18-G302]

This also fixes what an adequate counterexample would have to do. It would retain the actual received productive target while justifying the relevant absence of every qualifying original productive resource, or supply an independently supported undercutter to the adequacy inference. Merely producing a qualitative description or a noncausal explanatory alternative does neither automatically. The rival can challenge the positive judgment without constructing an entire cosmos, but the challenge must reach that judgment's actual target. The existing affirmative and defeasible appraisal is preserved.

### 4.4 Necessitation, identity and autonomy

The conditional modal content should be stated at full strength. The proposal says that the **same fact-specific plurality** $`Y`$ obtains wherever $`Q`$ obtains; replacing this by agreement only up to qualitative isomorphism would weaken it. But the condition neither proves that $`Q`$ is necessary nor provides a unique qualitative role for each symmetric individual. If $`U`$ is the class of $`Q`$-worlds, universal truth over $`U`$ remains conditional on membership in that class. When $`Q`$ actually obtains, the actual world belongs to it. If $`U`$ is empty, vacuous universal truths supply no actual individual. A zero-world frame likewise supplies no actual-world interpretation. [R18-G300, §6][R18-G300] [R18-G302, §5][R18-G302]

Even necessary $`Q`$, together with an adequately interpreted de re conditional for a bearer, would establish necessary existence only under that interpretation. It would not establish existence through that bearer's own essence, intrinsic productive adequacy or nonreceipt. A counterpart account need not employ the fixed outer bearer domain used by the chart construction in §§10.5–10.9. The source allows a sentential necessitation formulation where facts obtaining across worlds would otherwise be ill-defined. Neither that option nor the extensional tensor translation supplies a modal correspondence atlas, its transport maps, or the reflection of supplier witnesses required when bearer domains are restricted. Those remain independent interpretation conditions; the accepted transport theorems are conditional on them. [R18-G300, §6][R18-G300] [R18-G302, §5][R18-G302]

Autonomy makes a further claim: the grounding question is inapplicable to the proposed autonomous fact, not merely unanswered and not merely lacking a singleton answer. The 2016 paper's singular presentation explicitly sets plural grounding options aside. It therefore does not, by its singular notation alone, contradict the earlier collective proposal. Nor does its qualitative-essentialist possibility establish that the actual complete qualitative obtaining has an essence making the question inapplicable. Relative fundamentality to individual descriptions is insufficient for that conclusion. No actual counterexample to Completion, full plural-autonomy theory, or proof of the proposal's incoherence is supplied by these comparisons. [R18-G300, §7][R18-G300] [R18-G302, §§5–6][R18-G302]

The 2014 measurement comparison imposes an additional modal guard. Common rescaling preserves ratio information; changing one object's value changes its ratios, while a mass-counterpart interpretation determines which ordinary mass claims a relationally described possibility represents. These are different operations. The source concedes the objection at the fundamental sense of possibility and offers its counterpart response in a looser, reduced sense. It leaves unsettled which fundamental or reduced necessity, and which contexts in the latter case, validate the grounding-necessitation premise. Thus neither two scaled arrays nor the context-sensitive reply settles metaphysical grounding, authenticates numerical identity across worlds or supplies a uniform S5 interpretation. This limitation qualifies the proposed modal application without erasing the positive collective explanation. [collective-rules] [collective-adequacy-review]

The resulting limits are substantive. The theory retains derivative individuals, so it is not a denial that regions exist. Its finite qualitative illustrations are not a completed formal account of general relativity; more expressive resources are contemplated for that task. A qualitative property is not automatically a concrete intrinsic instance, and an arity-zero obtaining value is not an actual resource. The 2011 positive proposal, the later autonomy discussion and the separately cited plural-grounding arguments retain their distinct evidential roles. The source reports' full versus targeted historical readings, earlier overlap, and uninspected bibliographic leads are not new external readings by this exposition. Repeated attention to the same proposal is not independent confirmation or a reason by itself to change the comparative judgment. [R18-G302, §§1, 6][R18-G302]


### 4.5 Productive explanation and a justified stopping point

The qualitative rival and the original-bearer argument raise a further question: when does an explanatory account warrant stopping? Three targets must remain distinct. Let $p$ assert that the proposed original $B$ exists, $k$ concern its nature, and $d$ assert its production of a particular effect. Explaining $d$ need not explain $p$; a principled stopping point for $k$ need not be one for $p$. Yet an adequately established account of $p$ through $k$ would answer the existential question. It must not be dismissed merely because an essence is not an efficient producer. These distinctions permit a fair comparison of nonnecessitating agency, autonomous grounding and the positive intrinsic-adequacy argument that follows. [stopping-asymmetry] [principled-boundary]

**What a productive nature explains.** O’Connor's proposal supplies an agent, an intrinsic power, reasons and an actual purposive exercise, rather than an unexplained outcome called free. Conditional on the power and its instantiation being warranted, this gives positive information about the effect's production. If its operation is genuinely indeterministic under the complete relevant conditions, that nature can also explain why no exhaustive necessitating selector is available. A nonzero probability in an incomplete description does not establish this stronger indeterminism; nor does a scientific analogy establish original agency. Conversely, demanding an undiscovered determinant merely because every production is assumed to necessitate would beg the disputed question. [agent-power-comparison] [stopping-asymmetry]

The limit on selection and the adequacy of stopping are nevertheless different conclusions. If an exhaustive answer is defined as a necessitating answer, genuine indeterminism explains why it is unavailable. That can be a substantive explanation of a limit rather than a verbal exemption. It still does not establish why the weaker productive answer is ultimately sufficient.
