### 9.3 Concentrated capacity and eligibility

The source's argument about concentrating powers must be retained alongside actual efficacy. If compatible powers jointly accomplish some source-neutral work, their concentration in one bearer need not reduce that productive capacity. The argument is about possible possession of the powers, not a temporal merger of two necessary beings. It supplies a positive reason to regard independent productive adequacy as an intelligible excellence. [Consolidation of powers and eligibility, “The argument that must be credited”][u-concentration]

Three conclusions remain distinct:

| Question | What would answer it |
|---|---|
| Can the same external work be accomplished with concentrated powers? | A warranted account of those powers and the work they produce. |
| Can each particular existing contributor acquire that fuller power? | A further claim about that bearer's eligibility; a possible different bearer is insufficient. |
| Would every end valued by the original participants survive? | An account of those ends, including any that require two particular participants. |

The third conclusion is not needed for the first. A good constituted by two agents' participation can disappear while all source-neutral external work remains producible. Nor may the two originals' intrinsic acts be silently classified as created outputs just to make the external product require plurality. On the other side, possible concentration does not by itself show that each named bearer can acquire the concentrated powers while preserving its identity. [Consolidation of powers and eligibility][u-concentration]

That last distinction is a limit of one inference, not a surviving general objection to the source's perfection argument. A comparative argument may disqualify an essentially restricted candidate without requiring that this very candidate could be upgraded. The later appraisal expressly corrects the earlier use of identity-preserving acquireability as a standalone objection. A candidate cannot make every restriction irrelevant merely by declaring the restriction essential to its own kind. Whether the compared excellence is pure, eligible and applicable at the stated scope remains substantive. [Public source-unity judgment, “Present assent and exact reservation”][u-judgment]

The distinction between eligibility and acquireability has a precise source argument. In *Darʾ taʿāruḍ al-ʿaql wa-l-naql*, V, 273–274, Ibn Taymiyya describes a technical use of privation restricted to subjects naturally capable of the corresponding attribute: an inanimate wall is not called blind in that usage. He then gives his own reply. The convention does not settle the substantive comparison. He classifies life, knowledge and power as perfections and maintains that inability to possess them is not an exemption from deficiency; on his comparison, it is a greater limitation than their absence from something capable of them. His argument concerns the qualities and their absence, whether or not the selected technical vocabulary calls that absence death, ignorance or inability. The reported opponent's restriction and the author's positive appraisal must not be conflated. [*Darʾ*, V, 273–274][dar-perfection-and-privation]

An elementary reconstruction shows exactly what the terminology can establish. Suppose a privation predicate is defined by two conditions together: the subject is eligible for an attribute, and it lacks that attribute. An ineligible subject then lacks the privation **as defined**, even though it also lacks the attribute. Therefore the inference from “this privation predicate does not apply” to “the subject possesses the excellence” is invalid. Nor does the definition establish that the subject has no relevant deficiency. That stronger judgment requires a comparison of the subject and the excellence, not merely a rule governing the negative word. Conversely, this logical distinction alone does not prove that every attribute absent from a subject is an excellence it ought to have. Both directions matter: a technical exemption is not a positive vindication, and the failure of that exemption is not a complete theory of perfection.

The affirmative comparison must consequently identify its proper standard. A tool can be adequate for its limited function without cognition; failure to understand is not necessarily a defect **as that kind of tool**. The question here is instead whether an unrestricted original source lacks a real excellence relevant to its proposed adequacy. The source's positive classification of life, knowledge and power supplies that broader comparison, rather than deriving it from the word “original.” The reasons developed in section 12.4 give one substantive application: understanding and owning a fitting reason for effective action can contribute an excellence omitted by an account that records only the beneficial outcome. Merely proposing an entity whose kind excludes that relation does not answer those reasons. A rival can dispute their applicability or the comparative premise, but must address that disagreement rather than treating its own definition as the conclusion.

No identity-preserving transformation is required by this argument. To judge a proposed bearer inadequate for an unrestricted role is different from claiming that this very bearer could acquire every qualification while remaining the same individual. The judgment can exclude a candidate rather than describe its repair. Equally, the positive attribute and its mode of realization must be distinguished: the comparison does not, merely by naming knowledge or power, establish a particular creaturely realization, a complete theory of agency or one numerical original. It also does not show that more activity or greater product quantity is invariably better. Standing qualification, fitting exercise and the appropriateness of an occasion retain the separate roles already stated in sections 9.2 and 12.4. The resulting defense of the comparison preserves the affirmative pure-perfection appraisal while exposing the premise that a serious rival must actually contest.

A rival already credited with standing solo capacity does not need that capacity added by concentration. Its live question is whether its **actual joint manifestation** constitutes foreign completion of appropriate original efficacy. Conversely, an internally completed intention or a valued cooperative end does not establish entire actual original provision. The strongest rival retains distinct intrinsic powers and exercises, narrow efficient nonreceipt, primitive cognition and a conditional account of coordinated means. These are real credits. They do not yet establish complete original perfection, unrestricted sovereignty or the particular wisdom of every proposed undertaking. [Consolidation of powers and eligibility][u-concentration] [Public source-unity judgment][u-judgment]

<a id="foundation250-b-positive-highestness"></a>

**Positive fullness and strict highestness.** The received original *al-Ṣawāʿiq* supplies a related but distinct unity argument. Its starting point is not an indeterminate necessary item. It argues that the giver of life, cognition and effective action is more entitled to their nondefective perfection than the recipients, and that mere negations praise only by expressing positive fullness: absence of sleep expresses complete life and sustenance, absence of ignorance complete knowledge, absence of fatigue complete power, and absence of a partner complete dominion. The qualification “containing or entailing no deficiency” is essential. It does not authorize transferring every creature-specific trait or material mode to the source. Particular claims about perception, speech, height and other revealed predicates retain their own eligibility and interpretive arguments. [F250B035, opening and face 54][F250B035] [F250B022, faces 70–72][F250B022] [F250B076]

Face 79's uniqueness reasoning has an exact structure. If two alleged bearers are equal, neither is strictly higher than the other. If unequal, only the higher can occupy the proposed highest role. Its parallel argument from absolute subjugation says that an unsubdued equal defeats exhaustive supremacy, whereas a subdued alleged equal is not a peer. On these premises the role is unshareable. This is stronger than weak maximality, which allows tied maxima; replacing the source's strict highestness with “nothing is greater” would lose the decisive premise. Conversely, defining the desired role as exclusive does not independently show that an actual original must occupy it. The text's pure-perfection account, giver-priority, natural signs and revelation are offered as warrant for that richer applicability. Their force must be appraised rather than hidden inside the word “necessary.” [F250B022, faces 79 and 89][F250B022] [F250B076, §§1–3][F250B076] [F250B108]

The first-volume printed 231–233 comparison also grants its supposed peer actual creating, benefiting and protecting, before proposing partition, dominance or common subjection. The world's interrelation counts against wholly separated domains, and complete overcoming is asserted to exclude partnership. A harmonious pair therefore does not answer the full argument merely by avoiding conflict: it must address the claimed perfection of unshared dominion and the warrant for the alternatives. The fly analogy separately concerns powerless alleged gods; their observed incapacity cannot alone exclude every intrinsically capable original pair. The stronger sovereignty and coordination premises carry that extension. [F250B035, chapter 20][F250B035] [F250B079] [F250B096]

These arguments enrich rather than replace the productive account. A rival whose formal assumptions omit strict highestness is not thereby a countermodel to the full highestness argument. A conditional proof that includes strict highestness does not establish its philosophical eligibility either. The source itself distinguishes generic necessary existence from identifying the particular knowing, willing and beneficent God. Equally, many inseparable attributes of one necessary qualified bearer are not many gods: cognitive distinguishability and essential co-requirement need not be external assembly. This blocks an equivocation about composition without automatically classifying every proposed plurality of originals as one bearer's attributes. Productive unity, pure perfection, strict supremacy and bearer individuation thus retain distinct positive warrants and distinct burdens. [F250B029] [F250B035, 002:355–362 and endpoint cluster][F250B035] [F250B022, face 61][F250B022]

### 9.4 Nature unity and productive explanation

Two primary comparisons clarify the positive unity argument without reducing it to a bare objection to plurality. O'Connor's *And This All Men Call God* begins its relevant discussion with an ultimate necessary being whose aseity is distinguished from the status of a necessary emanation. It argues that the character of such a being should form an intelligible intrinsic unity, rather than a collection of traits whose conjunction remains unexplained. This is a positive demand on the relation between necessity and nature. It does not make numerical identity follow merely from the word *unity*, or prove that every difference of intrinsic character is an optional external attachment. [O'Connor 2004, pp. 419–423][unity-oconnor-2004]

In *Is God's Necessity Necessary? Replies to Senor, Oppy, McCann, and Almeida*, O'Connor further considers the connection between necessary existence and intrinsic nature, including the inadequacy of treating existence as an ontologically prior bare item to which a nature is subsequently attached. The comparison motivates a principled account of why the relevant nature is necessarily instantiated. It also exposes the additional work required when distinct intrinsic characters are said to be contingently attached to an otherwise common necessary basis. The existence of a distinction does not by itself establish that attachment model. [O'Connor 2010, pp. 311–313][unity-oconnor-2010]

The present productive argument should therefore identify the resource doing the explanatory work. If proposed members are wholly derivative in the relevant adequacy, redescribing their mutual arrangement as a unified nature does not supply that adequacy. If their intrinsic natures already include nonreceived adequate resources, the rival has granted originals whose joint operation must be assessed at that stronger level. The argument cannot move between these cases by treating every distinction as a separable part, or every unified description as a single numerically identical bearer. A numerical conclusion requires its own nonduplication and dependence premises.

Aquinas's *Sententia libri Metaphysicae* VIII, lectio 5 provides a useful different comparison. Matter and form are unified as potency and act; their unity does not require a further linking entity of the same kind. The discussion nevertheless retains the agent that brings potency to act in generation. It also allows a cause that sustains a substance without a process of motion in the relevant immaterial cases. Thus an intrinsic account of why a thing is one does not in that text abolish every productive explanation of its being. [Aquinas, VIII.5, especially nn. 5, 10 and 13][unity-aquinas]

For the current question, the distinction is between an account of the unity of an actual composite and an adequate source of its actuality. A productive cause of the composite need not, by that description alone, lie outside every constituent; that stronger claim needs the relevant dependence facts. What remains excluded is an alleged act whose availability already presupposes the whole actuality it is meant to supply. This respects both the positive intrinsic-unity account and the independent productive question. It neither turns the historical comparison into an endorsement of every surrounding metaphysical commitment nor treats intrinsic unity as an unexplained substitute for productive adequacy.

These comparisons are incorporated from the complete public derived *Sixteenth Report*, whose original private document has not been received here. The temporal criterion and these unity discussions retain their separate argument roles. Current primary inspection covers the specified passages; it is not a rereading of either author's whole work or a reconstruction of the report's historical research session.

#### Attribute profiles, numerical identity and the cost of a bridge

A worked comparison makes the last distinction precise. A formal reconstruction of Spinoza studied by Yuki Nakamura separates identity from agreement on **all** attributes, identity from sharing **one** attribute, and the possession of every realized attribute by a designated god. These are different statements. The received transfer screen preserves useful proofs and counterexamples while declining to import their predicates as this chapter's original-bearer ontology. The following account reconstructs those arguments from the five received public reports and registers. It does not newly authenticate the external paper, the Arabic passages or a Lean execution. [Transfer screen][profile-screen] [Auxiliary-axiom register][profile-register] [Scope discussion][profile-scope]

Write $`S(x)`$ for substance, $`G(x)`$ for the designated god predicate, and $`R(a,x)`$ for attribute incidence. In this comparison, incidence entails substancehood of its bearer and $`G(x)`$ entails $`S(x)`$. Define the complete profile $`\Phi(x)=\{a:R(a,x)\}`$. The profile is complete **for this specified relation**, not automatically complete with respect to every real distinction. The register's three relevant conditions are:

| Condition | Exact content |
|---|---|
| A22, profile injectivity | For substances $`x,y`$, $`\Phi(x)=\Phi(y)`$ implies $`x=y`$. Classically, distinct substances must differ on some attribute. |
| A12, shared-attribute identity | $`R(a,x)\land R(a,y)`$ implies $`x=y`$. |
| A14, nonempty profiles | Every substance has at least one attribute. |

**Equality is not overlap.** A22 proves its positive identity conclusion immediately: assuming distinct substances with equal profiles would supply, by the inequality formulation of A22, an attribute belonging to exactly one, contradicting profile equality. Sharing an attribute does not supply equality of the profiles. For an explicit incidence-only control, take four substances $`0,1,2,3`$ with profiles $`\{2,3\},\{2\},\{0\},\{1\}`$, respectively. All profiles are distinct and nonempty, so A22 and A14 hold, but 0 and 1 share attribute 2, so A12 fails. This transparent control concerns the displayed incidence conditions; it is not an assertion that this table instantiates every class in the historical formalization or represents possible original sources. [A22 and the exact identity question][profile-screen]

Conversely, A12 together with A14 implies A22. If two substance profiles agree, choose an attribute of the first using A14. It belongs to the second as well, so A12 identifies them. The nonemptiness qualification cannot simply disappear: two distinct attribute-free substances satisfy A12 vacuously but violate A22. A14 is a sufficient background condition for this implication, not asserted to be its weakest possible premise. The positive result and the failed unqualified inference should be retained together.

The original register calls A22 a PSR for substance distinguishability. Its written content, however, is an attribute-discrimination principle. It supplies no fact domain, explanatory relation or proof that a general sufficient-reason principle restricts individual differences to attributes. That additional restriction is substantive. An unrestricted predicate-discrimination formula, $`x\ne y\Rightarrow\exists P\,(P(x)\land\neg P(y))`$, does not supply it: choose $`P(z):=(z=x)`$. The formula is then a logical separation, not an explanatory account of the difference. Restricting predicates to specified attributes, an explicitly bounded definable language or essential properties changes the problem and needs its own justification. “Definable” alone is not enough if parameters and equality still permit this same singleton predicate. The received scope discussion leaves the developed restricted reconstructions open. [A22][profile-register] [Thoroughgoing PSR][profile-scope]

#### Distributed realization and a common bearer

The second argument distinguishes three further conditions:

| Condition | Exact content |
|---|---|
| A25, plenitude | Every attribute realized by a substance is possessed by **some** designated god; the witness may depend on the attribute. |
| A26, god uniqueness | Any two designated gods are identical. |
| A15, universal possession | **Every** designated god possesses every attribute realized by any substance. |

**The positive transfer is A25 together with A26 implies A15.** Fix any designated god $`g`$ and any incidence $`R(a,s)`$ on a substance. A25 supplies a designated god $`h`$ with $`R(a,h)`$. A26 gives $`h=g`$; substitution yields $`R(a,g)`$. Because the selected $`g,a,s`$ were arbitrary, A15 follows. This argument does not derive A26. It uses precisely the common-bearer premise that the attribute-dependent existential witnesses alone lack. [A15 and the uniqueness premise][profile-screen]

A two-substance incidence control isolates the failure of plenitude alone: let both substances be designated gods, with profiles $`\Phi(0)=\{0\}`$ and $`\Phi(1)=\{1\}`$. Every realized attribute has a god-bearer, but neither god has the other's attribute. A25 holds and A15 fails, even though these two profiles are distinct and nonempty. Conversely, with one attribute-bearing substance and **no** designated god, A15 is vacuously true while A25 is false. Thus the first control proves non-entailment in one direction, not an unconditional strict-strength ordering between the two principles. A26 alone is also insufficient: keep the two distinct profiles but designate only substance 0 as a god. God uniqueness holds while that god lacks attribute 1. These are elementary controls on the displayed clauses, separate from the source's richer three-element countermodel.

There is a useful **relative equivalence**. Assume A22 and the existence of a designated god. Then A15 implies A25 by using that existing god for each realized attribute. It also implies A26: for any gods $`g,h`$, each attribute of either belongs to the other by A15, since both are substances. Their complete profiles agree; A22 gives $`g=h`$. Together with the preceding positive transfer, this proves, on that background,

$`\mathrm{A15}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ (\mathrm{A25}\land\mathrm{A26})`$.

The existence and profile premises specify the background of the equivalence. Counting one named axiom on the left and two on the right proves neither explanatory reduction nor logical inequality of strength. Likewise, uniqueness among gods is not the claim that every substance is that god. Under A12, A14, A15 and an existing designated god $`g`$, the stronger conclusion has a short separate proof: any substance $`s`$ has an attribute by A14; A15 puts it in $`g`$; A12 gives $`s=g`$. In the ordinary proposition layer described by the screen, these premises are fields already assumed by the class. The proof neither establishes the God-existence premise nor derives the class's identity principle from an otherwise unspecified PSR. [Current declarations and relative background][profile-screen]

#### What the supporting axioms do, and what the finite witnesses test

The surrounding register matters because the preceding formulas do not float free of an ontology. Its A1-exclusivity condition separates being in itself from being in another. A8 and A9 identify those respective conditions with being conceived through itself and through another. Consequently the two conceptual conditions are disjoint: a bearer satisfying both would, by the bridges, satisfy both ontological conditions and contradict exclusivity. That deduction is positive, but the ontological–conceptual coextensions are premises, not consequences of the mere conjunction used to define substance. A10 says an attribute-object is conceived through itself. Together with A8 and the definition of substance, it makes that attribute-object a substance. Thus a formal attribute can be an object on the same carrier as its bearer; the definition does not already make it an inseparable intrinsic qualification in this chapter's sense. [A1ₑ and A8–A10][profile-register]

Other bridges answer different questions. A11 connects the two clauses used for *causa sui*, involving existence and a nature requiring existence. A18 connects involving existence with existence at every world. A19 and A20 connect the conceptual predicates with, respectively, no dependence on a distinct object and dependence on some distinct object; A19 permits a self-loop. A21 equates the non-indexed causal relation with the world-uniform indexed relation. The separate A16/A17 commitments supply mode-to-substance dependence and exclude the reverse substance-to-mode dependence. Neither asymmetry follows merely from naming the two sorts or adopting conceptual coextension. The register's classificatory labels, such as “definitional” or “light,” do not remove these interpretation costs. [Modal bridges and asymmetry][profile-register]

The distinction between an explicit definition and a further causal premise is especially clear in A14 and A13. With $`R(a,s)`$ defined as substancehood of $`s`$ together with the primitive essence-perception relation, A24's existence of such a perception for every substance is equivalent to A14: attach the already supplied substance hypothesis in one direction and project out the perception in the other. This is a genuine unfolding equivalence. The reported A13 route is different: A23 supplies self-causation at every world; a causal-existence bridge supplies existence at those worlds; A18 converts that result into involving existence. The screen warns that the inspected proof's class context already includes A13, and that no reverse proof was authenticated there. The informal label “equal-strength translation” must therefore not be received as an independently established, target-free equivalence. A bridge between necessity and involving existence alone does not infer a self-causal relation. [A23–A24][profile-register] [Assumption-footprint caution][profile-screen]

The causal extensions also preserve a meaningful failed generalization. The substantive A4 connects an effect's intelligibility to its cause. A5's no-common-nature/no-intelligibility condition is restricted to substances in the inspected extension. With “same nature” represented by shared attributes and therefore confined to substances, applying that A5 indiscriminately to modes would exclude the mode-to-mode causation the intended theory needs. The restriction repairs that particular encoding problem; it does not by itself supply a completed account of modes. Moreover, the extended causal class described by the screen inherits the target-containing proposition class. Adding that class wholesale to an independence experiment would already assume what the experiment seeks to test. [A4ₛ–A5ₛ][profile-register] [Missing substantive constraints][profile-screen]

The historical source screen accordingly distinguishes its inspected repository commit from the arXiv v2 presentation. The earlier attributes-as-modes construction failed the intended A10 requirement. The pinned replacement uses all-substance models with nonuniform incidence: four elements for the A12 witness, three for the A15 witness. In the latter, two are designated gods and the third has no attributes; the full plenitude-plus-uniqueness class is not instantiated, because uniqueness fails. The repaired models are reported to instantiate `StatedAxioms`, **not** the target-containing `Pars1Axioms`. In the inspected stated class, A1, exclusivity, A2, A7 and A8–A11 have substantive content, while A3–A6 are literal true placeholders and A12–A15 are absent. “Full stated register” must retain that exact ceiling. Two further limits survive the repair. The models have no modes, and `expressesEternalEssence` is set uniformly true. Their finite carriers do not encode an actual infinity of attributes. These choices need not defeat a counterexample to a universally quantified statement over the **declared** class, but they preclude treating formal satisfaction as a warrant for a fully faithful Spinozistic world or multiple perfected original sources. The source also distinguishes an identifying reading of *sive*, where nature-sharing is represented by attribute-sharing, from a disjunctive reading requiring an independent nature predicate. #### Return to the source's affirmative unity argument

The inherited Arabic feedback explains why rejecting a transfer is not rejecting unity. It reports a return to *Darʾ* electronic units 790–793, approximately IV, 251–260: the passage introduces a reported objection, affirms unity while criticizing a proposed proof, and distinguishes a shared concept from one numerically common external constituent. It also separates an intrinsic qualification's requiring its bearer from its being efficiently produced by another. The feedback reports all four electronic units read, not a new printed collation, manuscript witness or whole-volume reading. Those are the source of the present attribution and locators. [Inherited Arabic feedback][profile-arabic] [Reported primary loci][profile-dar]

Two readings of the profile relation therefore require different bridges. If its objects are individually possessed intrinsic qualifications, two bearers' qualitative perfection does not establish identity of their qualification-tokens and hence does not establish equality of numerical attribute sets. If its coordinates are instead shared qualitative predicates, A22 assumes those predicates exhaust individuation. Neither a common description nor the proof from injectivity establishes that exhaustiveness. Adding haecceitic or first-person discriminators removes the equal-profile premise; restricting the coordinates to pure perfections requires its own argument. And retaining the formal implementation without reinterpretation carries its attribute-as-substance consequence rather than silently replacing it with bearer-indexed inherence. Sections 10.16 and 12.14 already preserve the related generic-predication and intrinsic-qualification distinctions; this worked example identifies the extra premise in this particular transfer.

Finally, A25 is possession of attributes, not complete provision of an actual field's productive resources. Importing A25 plus assumed god uniqueness into an argument intended to establish original-source uniqueness would relocate that conclusion into A26. It would not improve the productive argument by proving its missing premise. The affirmative account in §§9.2–9.3 instead gives its own reasons concerning actual efficacy, complete original agency, unborrowed perfection and the scope of sovereignty. The inherited Arabic criticism preserves that account rather than endorsing multiple necessary originals. ### 9.5 Local response and finite productive augmentation

The nonduplication judgment in §9.2 requires a comparison of actual productive content. Several weaker properties must not be mistaken for that comparison: an agent can have an intrinsic exercise; its input can occur nontrivially in an operation; changing it locally can change the output; adding its entire exercise can change the endpoint; and its addition can strictly enlarge the complete work in the relevant order. These are different assertions. In particular, positive local response does not establish a strict finite change from a specified solo history to a specified joint history. [R18-G094, §§2–3][R18-G094]

An elementary polynomial separates the claims without presuming a causal interpretation. On $`[0,1]^2`$ let

```math
F(x,y)=x+y-3xy+x^2y+xy^2.
```

Then

```math
F(0,0)=0,\qquad
F(1,0)=F(0,1)=F(1,1)=1,
```

while

```math
F_x=1-3y+2xy+y^2,
\qquad
F_y=1-3x+x^2+2xy,
\qquad F_x(1,1)=F_y(1,1)=1.
```

Both partial derivatives are strictly positive throughout $`[0.9,1]^2`$. For example, $`F_x`$ increases with $`x`$ there because its derivative is $`2y\geq1.8`$, and increases with $`y`$ because $`-3+2x+2y\geq0.6`$. Its minimum is consequently $`F_x(0.9,0.9)=0.73`$. Symmetry gives the same bound for $`F_y`$. Thus both inputs have genuine local response around the joint point, yet the displayed solo and joint endpoint values are equal. [R18-G094, §3.1][R18-G094]

The missing premise is visible along the full comparison path. Put

```math
g(y)=F(1,y)=1-y+y^2,
\qquad g'(y)=-1+2y.
```

The derivative integrates to $`-1/4`$ from zero to $`1/2`$ and to $`1/4`$ from $`1/2`$ to one. Its positive final response therefore leaves $`g(1)=g(0)`$. The path parameter describes this mathematical comparison; it does not establish an actual temporal episode of destruction followed by reconstruction. [R18-G094, §3.2][R18-G094]

There is a positive theorem with the missing global premise. If $`g`$ is nondecreasing throughout $`[0,1]`$ and $`g(1)>g(1-\varepsilon)`$ for some $`\varepsilon>0`$, then

```math
g(1)>g(1-\varepsilon)\geq g(0).
```

A positive left derivative at one supplies such a strict final comparison. Alternatively, for continuously differentiable $`g`$, nonnegative derivative everywhere and positive derivative on a nonempty interval give strict endpoint growth by integration. This is ordinary monotonicity reasoning. Its application requires a justified complete-work ordering and a warranted monotonicity claim along the **entire** relevant augmentation, not only near its endpoint. Global injectivity of every conceivable productive operator would be more than this argument needs. [R18-G094, §3.3][R18-G094]

Coefficient signs do not provide the missing productive interpretation. The same polynomial is

```math
F(x,y)=x(1-y)^2+y(1-x)^2+xy,
```

a sum of nonnegative terms on the declared domain, while the endpoint comparison still fails. A negative coefficient in the expanded basis is not itself a destructive causal event, and nonnegative summands do not establish global monotonicity. Likewise, multiplying the scalar by a fixed nonzero vector or time profile $`H`$ preserves the equality $`F(1,0)H=F(1,1)H`$. Increasing the dimension of an output profile does not prove that it represents the complete productive history. [R18-G094, §§3.4–4][R18-G094]

Three targets must remain distinct. A created-effect profile records stipulated observables. A complete created history would also have to account for production, preservation, interaction or destruction wherever the ontology makes these relevant. A total actual inventory may additionally include the original subjects and their uncreated proper exercises. Adding the latter to an inventory does not make them extra created products. A provenance relation is also not automatically another created entity. Equality of profiles therefore proves neither numerical identity of whole histories nor equality of their complete productive work. Conversely, merely giving the histories different source labels does not prove more created work. [R18-G094, §4][R18-G094]

A conditional finite provision model sharpens the distinction: coalescence and priority-A policies have the same complete Boolean created-output table a∨b, but different actual entire-A provision when both inputs occur. No decoder from that table alone recovers both provision values. Moreover, an at-most-one entire-provider relation can hold while no entire provider exists; the cooperative example retains both same-act solo outputs without making either input an entire actual provider. Independent positive output accounting or cancellation can exclude a specified unchanged joint effect, but the model does not warrant those premises for reality or establish transworld numerical identity. [Baseline141-81](https://github.com/theislampill/orthemology/blob/ffca0abdf25079ef7639fe19776a21db60272fc4/research/t20-v6-20261012/sources/1084730563b2669a32112843a1f29e27eee3e31da0ec609281346cc6fb0b84ee/ProvisionIdentity.lean)

The strongest affirmative argument concerns that complete actual efficacy. It maintains that an independently original producer's adequate exercise should be effective through its own original resources; an added genuinely productive peer cannot be treated as doing nothing, and cannot silently diminish, redirect or complete what was being held fixed as the first producer's complete efficacy. If the peer makes a real additional contribution and the full account faithfully retains productive content, the comparison must either register further work or show that the first contribution was not already the alleged complete original provision. Fixed intrinsic willing or bodily movement alone is weaker than this fixed **contextually complete efficacy** premise. The latter needs substantive warrant; it cannot be manufactured by defining the output comparison to be strict. [R18-G094, §5][R18-G094]

This preserves the source rationale in §9.2. The relevant discussions distinguish an agent's proper act from an externally supplied part and distinguish standing ability from actual execution. Their original-specific no-foreign-completion and pure-perfection arguments have more content than the bare assertion that an added helper increases a scalar. The source report's historical returns to *Majmūʿ al-fatāwā*, *Jāmiʿ al-masāʾil* and the perfection discussion retain their contextual roles and earlier overlap; unsuccessful PDF or screenshot access in that inquiry is not represented as successful visual collation here. [R18-G094, §§1, 5][R18-G094]

The strongest surviving reply grants distinct intrinsic powers and acts while proposing a primitive joint manifestation with the same stipulated work as an available solo history. It denies that every change of productive relation is receipt of a constitutive perfection. It does **not** thereby make both subjects exclusive providers of the entire actual origin. The rival still needs a defensible interpretation of real production, appropriate complete efficacy, the wisdom of its particular undertaking and the adequacy of its full history. The polynomial establishes none of these. It refutes the shortcut from local sensitivity to finite augmentation, while leaving the independently motivated original-efficacy argument and its live classification dispute intact. [R18-G094, §§6–7][R18-G094]


### 9.6 A reason for particular means without a unique best outcome

A source of actual determination is not automatically a reason for preferring one outcome, and a reason for a particular means need not presuppose a unique value-maximizing outcome. The finite coordinated-means example makes these distinctions exact. It supplies a conditional instrumental rationale while leaving the eligibility of the proposed original subjects and ends to the substantive arguments above. [R18-G098, §§2–4][R18-G098]

Let the active settings be $`\mathbb Z_3`$, with addition and multiplication modulo three. When both agents act, stipulate

```math
F(a,b)=2(a+b).
```

When one is idle, stipulate $`F(a,\mathrm{idle})=a`$ and $`F(\mathrm{idle},b)=b`$. Each agent retains every solo target in its standing repertoire. For a fixed joint target $`q`$, successful coactive plans are exactly

```math
(a,b)=(q+t,q-t),\qquad t\in\mathbb Z_3.
```

Indeed these pairs give $`F=2(2q)=q`$, and $`F(a,b)=q`$ conversely gives $`a+b=2q`$, hence the same parametrization with $`t=a-q`$. There are three successful plans; mere success does not select one. [R18-G098, §2][R18-G098]

Now suppose the **complete practical context** is fixed by exchanging the agents: they have equivalent roles for this undertaking, the supplied reasons distinguish neither side, and the planning norm requires a plan invariant under that exchange. Invariance gives $`a=b`$. Then $`F(a,a)=4a=a`$, so the successful invariant plan is uniquely

```math
(a,b)=(q,q).
```

This proves the conditional symmetric-means result. Both agents can implement their own $`q`$-setting from the supplied target and norm, without receiving the peer's actual exercise as an input to the local policy. No claim that $`q`$ is the uniquely best ultimate end was used. The rationale is avoidance of an unsupported differentiated assignment under the stipulated symmetric reasons. Equal powers alone would not establish those reasons: de re relations, actor-relative duties or other relevant circumstances can break the practical symmetry even when the standing repertoires match. [R18-G098, §§2–3][R18-G098]

The symmetry must preserve the entire declared operation. The map

```math
(a,b)\longmapsto(a+c,b-c),\qquad c\ne0,
```

preserves the coactive sum but changes solo outputs: the first agent's solo $`a`$ becomes $`a+c`$ and the second's solo $`b`$ becomes $`b-c`$. Across their three settings each, all six comparisons change. Treating this free cycle as a symmetry of the full law would therefore manufacture a selection obstruction by dropping the idle cases. The source's historical finite enumeration reports 216 setting/output permutation triples, 18 preserving the coactive table and six preserving the full table; with outputs fixed de re, the corresponding counts are three and one. These bounded historical counts corroborate the distinction, while the displayed solo calculation already shows why the proposed nontrivial shift is not a faithful symmetry. [R18-G098, §§2, 5][R18-G098]

The general selector principle is already developed in [Objective Normativity, §8.10](objective-normativity-and-corrective-cognition.md#810-structural-covariance-content-recoding-and-semantic-identification): an equivariant choice must be fixed by the stabilizer of its complete context. Its finite converse chooses a stabilizer-fixed candidate at an orbit representative and transports it; two transports to the same context differ by an element of that stabilizer, so the result is well-defined. Here the diagonal candidate supplies precisely the required fixed point. A multiplicity of successful plans is thus not itself an impossibility result. The relevant action, admissible candidates, full reasons and equivariance requirement have to be identified first. [R18-G098, §2][R18-G098]

Particularizing data can instead select every successful plan. Add $`d=a-b`$. Solving the sum and difference equations in $`\mathbb Z_3`$ gives

```math
a=q+2d,\qquad b=q-2d.
```

For fixed $`q`$, the value $`d`$ is in bijection with the three successful plans. Exchanging agents sends it to $`-d`$, with only $`d=0`$ fixed. The extra coordinate therefore carries selection information; it does not, merely by being recorded, supply a fitting reason for its value. Copying a chosen plan into a determination record explains how that record fixes execution, not why the plan is justified under the unchanged reasons. [R18-G098, §3][R18-G098]

This can be stated without confusing two success contracts. A plan family descends to a coarser context record exactly when it is constant on that record's fibres, by the established factorization criterion. If the task requires the declared role-specific $`d`$, a $`q`$-only record generally cannot recover the plan: different $`d`$ values share $`q`$ but require different actions. If the task requires only achieving $`q`$, the $`q`$-only diagonal policy works for every context. At $`q=0`$, for example, both $`(0,0)`$ and $`(1,2)`$ achieve the endpoint, but only the former matches the $`d=0`$ plan requirement. Endpoint success is weaker than satisfying the complete reason or assignment certificate. [R18-G098, §§2–3][R18-G098]

The historical source comparison preserves parallel distinctions in the account of willing. Its *Majmūʿ* reading separates antecedent capacity from a contemporaneous determining condition, and cosmic willing from command, love or approval. Real means remain causes within the complete decree; deleting those means while holding the entire determination fixed is not automatically an admissible alternative. Wise succession and an act's fitting occasion also differ from deficiency in standing power. An explanation through a particular actual willing need not be an external efficient donor or a unique numerical optimizer; nevertheless, the generic assertion that there is willing does not yet explain why this particular willing obtains. [R18-G098, §1][R18-G098]

The equal-bread or equal-path discussion requires an attribution qualification. In the examined *Bayān* context, the reasonless-selection reply is reported as al-Rāzī's position within a criticized analogy; it cannot simply be quoted as the responding author's final account. The response affirms an unreceived particular willing while retaining the question of particular determination. Two suspect electronic strings were quarantined in the source inquiry rather than silently emended or treated as verified print readings. No new primary collation is claimed here. The source's wisdom argument also distinguishes our ignorance of a detailed reason from proof that no reason exists; conversely, a successful mathematical adapter does not establish the actual wise reason it represents. [R18-G098, §1][R18-G098]

The example accordingly earns a real but bounded credit for the concordant rival. It gives an instrumental rationale under symmetric complete reasons, without a unique ultimate optimizer or reciprocal efficient donation of the local choices. It does not establish that the proposed peer-valued undertaking is perfectly wise, explain every particular target and occasion, or change the actual coactive origin from joint support to individual entire provision. Varying a few declared occasions is not a model of a beginningless history. Holding standing resources fixed can leave particular determinations open; holding the complete actual determination fixed cannot be used to demand a different effect without changing the premise. These limits preserve both the conditional means argument and the stronger productive-efficacy question. [R18-G098, §§4–5][R18-G098]


### 9.7 Necessary agreement and complete original efficacy

Necessary agreement leaves two different questions: which exercises are possible together, and whose original resources actually provide an undertaking's complete productive basis. A correction to the first inference does not settle the second. The source comparison of Baillie and Hagen's power argument, Gordon's direct criticism and Amini's parallel critique isolates this distinction while retaining the affirmative original-efficacy appraisal. Their related historical ancestry also prevents treating these philosophical discussions as independent empirical convergence. [R18-G307, §§1, 4][R18-G307]

Baillie and Hagen deliberately analyze non-normative power, allow nature-relative restrictions, and use maximality to exclude radically limited agents. Their criterion combines power for every individually possible achievement, unsurpassability and some effective power; it does not rule out equal power by definition. Their objections to necessary harmony concern another's determination restricting ability, possible divergence as a condition of personal distinctness, and complete productive sufficiency. These are distinct claims, followed by the nested-necessity argument and a further criticism of universal frustration. The source reports their express development of al-Ghazālī's position and discussion of Scotus and Ockham; Amini engages related antecedents. The stronger productive-perfection application below must therefore be argued at its own scope rather than silently inserted into the initial non-normative definition. [R18-G307, §1][R18-G307]

Let $`F`$ mean that one agent brings about $`s`$, and $`H`$ that the other brings about an incompatible $`r`$, in the same respect and occasion. Use one metaphysical accessibility relation. Necessary nonconflict and separate attainability say

```math
\mathrm{NC}:\quad\Box\neg(F\land H),
\qquad
\mathrm{EA}:\quad\Diamond F\land\Diamond H.
```

These assertions are compatible: the successful alternatives need not have a common completion. As a purely propositional check, an S5 frame with two mutually accessible worlds, one satisfying only $`F`$ and the other only $`H`$, satisfies NC and EA at both worlds. This is a check of modal scope, not a model of omnipotent subjects or a metaphysical possibility certificate. The stronger premise used in the disputed modal step is

```math
\mathrm{STR}:\quad\Box(H\longrightarrow\Box\neg F).
```

**Conditional deduction.** STR and $`\Diamond H`$ yield $`\Diamond\Box\neg F`$: choose an accessible $`H`$-world and apply STR there. In S5 this implies $`\Box\neg F`$, contradicting $`\Diamond F`$. In equivalence-frame semantics, the chosen world has the same accessible component as the initial world, so its universal absence of $`F`$ covers every alternative accessible initially. The deduction is valid on its stated premise. NC does not supply the extra inner necessity in STR; the two-world scope check also exhibits that failure. [R18-G307, §2][R18-G307]

Four possible substitutions would change the argument. Necessitating the conditional $`H\to\neg F`$ gives NC, not STR. From actual $`H`$ and NC one gets actual $`\neg F`$, but necessitation cannot be applied while the contingent $`H`$ assumption remains undischarged. Necessary existence of the agent, or necessary agreement of agents, is not necessity of this particular determination $`H`$. Finally, one may hold $`H`$ fixed and restrict the inner alternatives to those preserving it; absence of $`F`$ on that restricted class can be true, but the inner operator is then different from the unrestricted outer metaphysical operator. The same-operator S5 inference cannot be transferred without another premise. [R18-G307, §2][R18-G307]

A substantive power standard can motivate a stronger premise. An absolutely adequate original might be required to retain effective ability under independently fixed peer determinations, rather than possess only an antecedent capacity or a counterfactual ability whose exercise covaries with the peer. This is a robustness and eligibility claim, not another manipulation of NC. Likewise, ruling out one eligible achievement is not yet total impotence: that generalization needs contrary-target assumptions for every relevant act. Nonoccurrence of an act and productive achievement of its contrary are not automatically the same target. [R18-G307, §§2–3][R18-G307]

Agent distinctness itself supplies neither unrestricted independent choice combinations nor possible disagreement. Two necessarily equivalent will-contents need not be one numerical act or one subject; ownership of proper acts and first-person reference remain distinct. A theory of personal independence may impose counterfactual divergence, but it must defend that requirement. The conservative centered construction of §12.1 is enough to reject an automatic identity inference from semantic agreement, while leaving the actual realization and perfection of the proposed subjects open. The incompatible-guarantees argument of §12.2 similarly retains its own common-completion premise. [R18-G307, §§3, 7][R18-G307]

The productive question is stronger than mere concomitance. Distinguish: one willing necessarily accompanies the other; an intended effect is achieved through an agent's intentional activity whenever that willing occurs; and that agent originally provides the **entire actual productive basis** of the undertaking, including indispensable contributions. The first does not prove that the peer efficiently produces one's willing. The second is stronger than an accidental matching endpoint but does not entail the third. Conversely, an indispensable peer contribution is not removed from the undertaking's origin merely by showing that no intrinsic item was donated to the first agent. [R18-G307, §4][R18-G307]

The strongest affirmative application can be written with three explicit premises:

1. A perfected original's relevant actual undertaking must be adequately effective through its own original resources, without an independently original supplier of indispensable productive efficacy.
2. This undertaking's actual productive basis includes the peer's proper unborrowed exercise, which the first agent does not originally supply.
3. The peer's role is genuinely productive, rather than only an object known or a proposition entailed by the undertaking.

The second and third premises exhibit precisely the foreign original contribution excluded by the first. Hence the first agent's undertaking fails the stated requirement, without any contrary willing or disagreement; the symmetric argument applies to the peer. This conditional reasoning reaches the retained primitive-joint-support proposal at its strongest actual interpretation: that proposal grants both original roots, rather than making each individually the whole source. Its standing solo constructors can produce the same endpoint in another history, but that other history does not supply the missing origin of this actual one. [R18-G307, §4][R18-G307]

The first premise has independent motivation in the inherited account of complete effective agency. An actual receiving mode includes its indispensable productive efficacy in its explanatory target. Leaving an independently original contribution unexplained by this source makes the source's provision incomplete at that scope. The perfection comparison also distinguishes wholly adequate agency from essentially assisted agency and does not require an identity-preserving upgrade of the proposed subject. These are substantive reasons for the requirement, not merely a definition selected to imply uniqueness. They carry the affirmative weight already stated in §§9.2–9.3. [R18-G307, §4][R18-G307]

The surviving reply disputes the scope of **appropriate complete efficacy**. It accepts that the joint product has two actual original roots but proposes that each already adequate activity manifests nonexclusively in that effect, without the participant's own proper perfection being supplied by the other. The affirmative answers that this achieved agency remains productively incomplete at the original respect in question. Neither bare covariance of the wills nor the finite coordinated-means result resolves that classification. The rival owes an account of its appropriate efficacy and the eligibility of its peer-valued end; the affirmative owes the application of its productive-perfection norm to that undertaking. The modal-scope criticism does not refute a separately warranted three-premise productive argument. [R18-G307, §4][R18-G307]

Moral agreement also falls short of complete particular concordance. Agents can agree on every moral truth while permissible means, timing, equal goods or actor-relative duties leave several action profiles. Failure of moral agreement to entail complete concordance does not, conversely, prove that conflict is possible. A richer reason structure can require compatible plans. Section 9.6 gives one such conditional means rationale without a unique value-maximizing end; it does not establish the requisite symmetry or ultimate wisdom in every context. Necessary wise nonselection need not remove antecedent capacity, and common rational content need not be a third efficient controller. Yet a complete account of the particular ends, occasions and actual willings remains a further explanatory task. Not possessing that account is neither a proof of arbitrary willing nor a warrant to declare the account complete. [R18-G307, §5][R18-G307]

The literature comparison has a precise attribution boundary. The source reports Gordon's 2024 note 17 as a direct response to Baillie and Hagen: had the first agent willed the alternative, the peer could have harmoniously done so too. This challenges the inference from actual harmonious nonexercise to inability under a counterfactual conception of power. It does not establish that two subjects satisfy every adequate conception of omnipotence. Amini's 2009 paper is a parallel critique of related older arguments and does not discuss Baillie and Hagen. His at-most-one/existence distinction is sound, but universal or self-involving quantification alone is not an incoherence proof. A paradox needs the particular closure or incompatible-success requirements that generate it. If a warranted uniqueness argument makes joint omnipotence impossible, inability to realize that impossibility does not refute a possibility-qualified account of power without adopting the stronger unrestricted conception at issue. Ordinary mutual frustration also does not certify maximal efficacy, and it is not the retained rival's account of successful concordant activity. [R18-G307, §§1, 6][R18-G307]

The direct criticism thus succeeds at a local ability inference while leaving robust power and individually adequate actual provision as substantive responses. Its source acquisition used one published-format mirror for Baillie and Hagen, without a verified byte identity to the publisher's full file; the other reported readings have their own stated scopes. This exposition incorporates that public source comparison, not a new acquisition of the three papers. The routes of §12 remain distinct: universal mastery needs its universal authority premise; complete actual origin needs the proper-exercise and adequacy premises; incompatible guarantees need common admissibility. If a genuine productive defect is correctly recognized and practical conformance is supplied, self-knowledge can mediate exclusion, but it still does not establish the defect norm. [R18-G307, §§1, 7–8][R18-G307]


<a id="second250-uthaymin-unity-locus"></a>

The later Ibn ʿUthaymīn audit verifies a more narrowly scoped exposition in Māʾida lesson 24, Q5:73, where Q21:22 and Q23:91 are explained through separated creations, each deity's exclusive claim, conflict and domination; two travel-party commanders illustrate the disorder. That supplies an explicit exclusivity/conflict premise, not a theorem from numerical plurality alone. Intrinsically concordant co-producers are not separately tested in that bounded passage. Nor did the audit verify independent commentary chapters under Q21:22 or Q23:91. The earlier source's extended necessary-harmony arguments must therefore be assessed on their own evidence rather than either credited to or refuted by this later limited exposition. The action-ontology loci add vocabulary and activity controls, not another independent unity proof. [S250B-049, lines 61–77](https://github.com/theislampill/orthemology/blob/a7ff0e33d1a299db640041c46b1af81ca70851f6/experiments/orthemology-v5-successors/source-store/3deb84870b2d2de2da472946031d2886e06d03efbc76e9e2b6c6ff968e738b50/LOCUS_AUDIT.md#L61-L77) [S250B-049, lines 102–109](https://github.com/theislampill/orthemology/blob/a7ff0e33d1a299db640041c46b1af81ca70851f6/experiments/orthemology-v5-successors/source-store/3deb84870b2d2de2da472946031d2886e06d03efbc76e9e2b6c6ff968e738b50/LOCUS_AUDIT.md#L102-L109)

#### The source's cooperation argument and its precise transfer claims

The received cooperation studies reconstruct an argument against plural original makers, not merely an expectation that rivals might disagree. The Aṣfahāniyya and Minhāj discussions distinguish unborrowed standing power, complete determining agency, an intrinsic act and its external product. They explicitly examine necessary concord, preserved powers, willing assistance, optional coalescence and a third efficient cause. Common benefit or foreknowledge cannot simply be inserted as an efficient origin of the very wills producing the beneficial event. A common reason is not thereby a third maker; conversely, naming it does not explain the complete determination and distribution of productive roles. These are substantive explanatory claims, rather than a prohibition on every relation or harmless concomitance. [F250H48] [F250H149]

The strongest positive route has several stages. Reciprocal origination of the powers needed for origination cannot supply original efficacy. Equal complete makers cannot each exclusively produce the same numerical effect in the same respect. If their effects necessarily require each other's completion, the source challenges their alleged original self-sufficiency. If distinct effects contingently coalesce, the coalescence requires a productive explanation: opposition conflicts with the specified complete determination, while consent is assessed as assistance under the preceding efficacy argument. Independent domains would therefore remain separate; their separation conflicts with the actual causally interconnected creation. Connectedness here means the relevant connected field, not merely that each node has a neighbor. Neither this argument nor its illustrations automatically establish a universal SourceMode principle for every admissible undertaking. [F250H48]

Two explicit arguments in Majmūʿ 20:175–181 sharpen that route. **Exclusive completion (B6)** connects complete power and decisive will with production through that agent alone. With exercised independently sufficient original provision and same-respect nonduplication, exclusion of another complete original provider follows. With only outcome entailment, it does not: two implications that an outcome occurs say nothing by themselves about its exclusive provenance. The source supplies the stronger causal interpretation. Its unchanged-agent comparison also excludes a misleading analogy: doing half the work jointly and all the work alone changes exertion, act, instruments or determining will even if standing strength persists. A faithful test holds the target, relevant productive state and actual determination fixed. [F250H48] [F250H217]

**Concentration of powers (B5)** gives a further positive perfection argument. Powers distributed across two bearers can, the source argues, be united with increased efficacy. It then infers that each partner admits fuller independent power, cannot supply its own missing completion, and therefore lacks necessary self-sufficiency. The argument is not exhausted by saying that an effect has two inputs. Five propositions must nevertheless remain distinct: a united profile is realizable; this very partner can possess it; the improvement is an eligible perfection of that partner; its completion requires another; and such dependence contradicts intrinsic necessity. The received independent review finds genuine support for the first and a serious rationale in unborrowed efficacy, but does not find the identity-relative transfer established by the illustrations alone. A new collective bearer is not each old member, and concentration of a profile is not literal fusion of numerically distinct necessary subjects. The Minhāj perfection argument can supply the stronger conclusion if the concentrated capacity is independently warranted as a pure perfection applicable to each alleged original. It cannot assume that each already provides all the other's productive resources to prove that each must be the whole provider. [F250H217]

This distinction fixes the countermodel test. When B5, B6 or the transition from intrinsic unborrowed power to independently complete efficacy is itself being tested, its disputed conclusion is not an admissibility premise. A challenge must preserve independently retained upstream commitments, not the conclusion it contests. The inspected finite models still fail to represent the full upstream power, will and perfection profile: endpoint alternatives do not represent unrestricted target power, contribution tables do not interpret complete determination, and an outside-field source is not a rival original within this field. Their weaker separations remain valid. No full upstream-premise-preserving countermodel was produced in these studies; that negative finding neither proves the bridges nor certifies that no such model is possible. [F250H149] [F250H217]

The source-contextual successor appraisal preserves a **provisional affirmative judgment of one complete original source of the actual connected creation**, separately from its acceptance of at least one actual Necessary Being. Its reasons concern complete original provision, integrated agency and productive perfection. Withholding unrestricted identity-relative transfer or universal SourceMode does not cancel that positive, defeasible assessment. Nor is the assessment a theorem inferred from the absence of a counterexample. These paragraphs consolidate the received studies; their reported Arabic and scan readings and historical model inspections are not newly performed primary-source work or kernel execution here. [F250H51]

<a id="third-cohort-b-source-faithful-cooperation-test"></a>

The dated source-context guide supplies a further rule for assessing this cooperation argument. A test of the disputed P2b conclusion must not include P2b among its antecedents. A serious challenge may deny that conclusion while preserving the independently retained antecedents in their strong source-faithful meanings. Conversely, dropping an independently retained antecedent of the tested inference does not isolate that disputed step; a disputed completion, exclusivity or identity-relative transfer conclusion must not be required as its own antecedent. The reported absence of an inspected full-premise countermodel establishes neither the truth of every premise nor metaphysical uniqueness. Historical attribution, strongest argument reconstruction, model-premise comparison and philosophical warrant remain distinct evidential tasks. [T750B618]

This distinction also protects the affirmative Athari-Taymiyyan account from an invalid activity control. A global empty extension may separate persistent capacity from activity under reduced assumptions; it does not preserve independently defended always-active or anti-inactivity premises. General activity is not eternal instantiation of every kind, ending one token is not total inactivity, and a renewed intrinsic act is not by definition a created bearer or externally received perfection. The guide reports separate earlier causal and later perfection arguments; their overlap is not another historical witness. Its linked reading receipts, modern translations and scans were not acquired here, and the guide is not a new primary-text reading or a fresh proof replay.

<a id="foundation250-b-actual-order-appraisal"></a>

**Actual order and the scope of the recorded appraisals.** The source's case for one Creator is not exhausted by excluding two complete producers. The sixth collection joins actual derivative capacities, matched recipients, coordinated goods, genuine finite agency and a common final orientation into a cumulative explanation. A finite agent cannot originate every condition of its own awareness, desire, will and power. The human-action argument distinguishes simultaneously required causes from contested indefinitely successive conditions; it does not require a blanket prohibition of beginningless temporal history. One origin of the dependent order can explain fitted capacities without making the resulting agents or their benefits fictitious. These are affirmative considerations, not merely the absence of an available rival. [F250B147, E145–160][F250B147] [F250B173]

The historically dated appraisals nevertheless make different comparative judgments. The middle-section reader on 7 October provisionally prefers common creation within its admitted necessary-being and basic-recognition starting point. The first-section reader credits the same integrated-order evidence but withholds that comparative conclusion from this volume alone: the actually presented celestial argument relies on circular motion not being natural, its dependence on volition, the limits of the outermost sphere's simple motion, and a universal ranking of final ends. These historically specific physical and evaluative premises are not certified by successfully reading the passage. Both readers give stronger endorsement to the local power/contribution/product distinctions than to an unrestricted all-perfections result. The combined appraisal preserves this difference rather than counting it as a vote. [F250B084] [F250B131, “Two assessments kept separate”][F250B131] [F250B173] [F250B185, E125–134][F250B185] [F250B213]

These are bounded historical assessments, not a reversal of the current affirmative appraisal developed in §§9.2–9.7 and 10.4 with additional argument. A defeasible common-source inference need not eliminate every imaginable alternative; a bare cooperative relation table does not show metaphysical eligibility. Nor does counting one source as simpler establish all of its personal and perfect predicates. The comparison concerns explanatory coverage, coherence, independent warrant and the cost of stipulated coordination. In particular, an actual-order inference and the stronger universal claim about every eligible original's exclusive source mode remain different questions. The full collection's received-body completion supplies broader context for that distinction, not another independent witness for its conclusion. [F250B028] [F250B131]

#### The connected Darʾ–Minhāj comparison

The wider reading records locate the preceding distinctions in connected arguments. *Darʾ* 9, recorded electronic 016:717–725, permits noncausal concomitance of a bearer and its attributes before arguing that two intrinsically capable originals would each require independent efficacy. The further steps at 016:739 and 776–779 concern interdependent products and the deficiency of partition or alternating full sourcehood. They are substantive arguments beyond same-token nonduplication. The reply at 749–750 distinguishes choosing not to perform one of one's own incompatible alternatives from having a fitting exercise blocked by another agent. It therefore does not simply make contradictions eligible objects of power. The modern comparison must separately warrant the passage from intrinsic capacity to unilateral efficacy and the transfer from a joint product to each producer's intrinsic completion. [F250-C021] [F250-C121]

*Minhāj* V03L0269–0276 presses the source of agreement itself. Where each will is a productive condition of the other's completed willing, a circle in part of the determinant remains a circle. A beneficial created outcome or foreknowledge of that outcome is not automatically an independently antecedent coordinator of the wills producing it. This is an explanatory-direction objection, not the claim that divine knowledge is temporally learned from a creature. Conversely, the source's own distinction between concomitance and productive donation requires testing whether the proposed harmony has that productive role. Ordinary collaborators retain distinct intrinsic acts and powers; the common effect does not become one intrinsic act inhering in two bearers. [F250-C020] [F250-C103] [F250-C198]

The studies also preserve the positive intrinsic-action alternative. Complete will with power entails its intended effect, yet an eternally fixed sufficient cause of one coeternal individual world is rejected. V03L0239 and L0246 exclude an outside giver of divine will and intrinsic acts; they do not classify every renewed exercise as the manufacture of a separate bearer. The changing act, the created product, the standing attribute and whole-bearer existence remain distinct. These connected source grounds strengthen the efficacy argument while leaving its full-role application open to the exact objections above. Reading their authored study records is not a new inspection of the underlying Arabic witnesses. [F250-C020] [F250-C103] [F250-C198]

The *Darʾ* 8 account at recorded P0412–P0421 positively ranks originating and preserving above merely moving or arranging what is supplied. At P0847 the comprehensive source supplies preparation, recipient bearers and capacities as well as the final effective act. This is a genuine positive conception of sourcehood, not merely a label for the first term in a chain. The accompanying distinctions prevent substituting a loved end or commander for an efficient origin, or treating the absence of a condition as a positive producer of a negative entity. Likewise *Darʾ* 9, 015:321 answers the duplication objection: producing a thing at its existence does not mean adding existence to a thing already independently actual. These arguments support an effect-indexed productive interpretation without proving that an arbitrary finite interface exhausts its relevant grounds. [F250-C111] [F250-C121]

### 9.8 Composition, proper exercise and original possession

A proposed concrete whole should be tested at its strongest rather than rejected as a mere collection-name. An integrated bearer with unified powers and acts is a candidate subject; its being composite does not by itself decide whether it originally provides the relevant field. Conversely, integration, causal autonomy from outsiders and an adequate endpoint repertoire do not yet establish complete original supply of the whole actual productive history. The latter includes the actual exercises, resources and receptions through which its result occurs. A characterization of what the whole can accomplish is weaker than an account of how this occurrence has its efficacy. [N250B-237] [N250B-241]

The conditional assembly objection can be stated with one proper exercise. Let b be a member distinct from the proposed whole w, and let m be b's own unborrowed productive exercise in the respect at issue. Suppose the whole's `HistoryComplete` claim covers the actual efficacy of m in that same productive relation. The inherited `UnborrowedActs` condition excludes another source of that very original exercise; applying it to this coverage identifies w with b, contradicting their stipulated distinction. One such exercise is enough. The argument needs neither a finite list of members nor a temporally first event. But it needs **productive** coverage of m, not merely membership of m in a set of facts true of the whole. Calling an inventory “complete” cannot supply that relation. [N250B-237] [N250B-241]

This gives four substantive responses rather than a grammatical verdict against wholes. A theory can make the whole original and its members' relevant efficacy derivative. It can preserve original members while assigning the whole only their narrower joint role. It can regard the alleged members as intrinsic powers of one bearer rather than numerically distinct original agents. Or it can defend genuine joint original ownership while explaining why its productive accounting differs from the inherited exclusivity relation. The fourth response cannot retain an unchanged `HistoryComplete`/`UnborrowedActs` inference when it has changed their intended relation. None of these descriptions alone establishes the actual candidate's eligibility or supplies the full field. [N250B-237]

The accounting sequel isolates the hardest version of the fourth response. A received mode of action and the source's own exercise are not interchangeable. If the whole actually furnishes the actuality or efficacy of the member's exercise, that exercise is received in the relevant respect, whatever the theory calls the relation. Yet an anti-donation principle alone does not show that every claimed constitutive co-possession is such furnishing. Independence from outside the composite is weaker than unborrowed original possession; constitutive dependence is not automatically efficient receipt. The critic must establish the productive dependence or give an independently warranted account of proper-act individuation. [N250B-236] [N250B-242]

The latter route has positive content. A proper intrinsic exercise is the subject's actual agency, not an event to which an actor label may be indifferently appended. Holding a physical occurrence fixed while changing the alleged subject need not hold the same proper exercise fixed. One occurrence can realize two subject-indexed acts without becoming one original act co-owned by two subjects. Accordingly, a serious counterproposal must jointly warrant distinct bearers, the same token proper exercise, original possession in the same respect, complete original accounting and unchanged numerical identity. Failure to establish that conjunction limits the counterproposal; it is not by itself a proof that every constitutive theory is impossible. Direct rational understanding of agency can in principle bear on individuation, but its reach to the original case needs argument. [N250B-236] [N250B-242]

The literature comparisons in these studies sharpen rather than settle this target. Whole-level autonomous governance or integration is weaker than exhaustive original provision. Cooperative unifying powers may themselves depend on the cooperating parts. Numerical sameness invoked by a constitution account cannot simply replace numerical identity in the inherited uniqueness proof. These are the source studies' attributed comparisons, not fresh inspections of the underlying works or demonstrations that their entire theories fail. Likewise, the Minhāj example targets an actual reason-responsive correction, not a change to a textual header or a covariantly relabelled output. Its granted local received agency does not automatically establish an original whole bearer. [N250B-236] [N250B-237]

The articles and their exact-scope acceptances establish this conditional argument and its accounting burden while withholding new actual P1/P2 closure at their dated stage. That is a limit on these routes, not a replacement for the later cumulative affirmative appraisal in §§9.7 and 10.4. It preserves both a real objection to borrowed efficacy presented as original and the remaining task of warranting the productive relation for a proposed concrete subject. [N250B-241] [N250B-242]
