### 10.5 Coherent assignments across locally indexed worlds

The preceding arguments keep one source fixed while following its actual productive contributions. A different question arises when proposed worlds are described in separate local coordinates: which local entries, if any, can consistently represent one selected bearer? Equal labels do not establish that correspondence, and a coherent correspondence does not by itself establish numerical identity. The finite construction below makes the missing mathematical structure explicit. It concerns a declared alignment of descriptions; the alignment graph is neither a causal graph nor the accessibility relation of a modal logic. [Finite modal identity transport, §§2–3][transport-proof]

Let $`W`$ be a finite nonempty set of worlds with a nominated actual world $`a`$. Let $`\Gamma=(W,\mathcal E)`$ be a connected undirected graph. Each world has a finite outer domain $`D_w`$ of indices. For every oriented edge $`v\to w`$, supply a bijection $`g_{vw}:D_v\to D_w`$, with $`g_{wv}=g_{vw}^{-1}`$. Choose one orientation of each undirected edge and denote that set by $`\mathcal E^+`$. Connectedness makes the outer-domain cardinality $`n`$ common, possibly zero. An index available in the outer domain need not represent something existing at that world. Existence $`E_w\subseteq D_w`$, whole-existence reception $`C_w\subseteq D_w`$, and other predicates are separately specified. No equation such as $`g_{vw}(E_v)=E_w`$ is assumed: that would already impose persistence of existence.

For arbitrary acceptance sets $`A_w\subseteq D_w`$, an accepted section is a tuple $`s=(s_w)_{w\in W}`$ satisfying both

```math
s_w\in A_w,
\qquad s_w=g_{vw}(s_v)\quad\text{on every oriented edge}.
```

The choice $`A_w=E_w`$ asks for an everywhere-existing compatible assignment; $`A_w=E_w\setminus C_w`$ also requires nonreceipt. These are filters on a correspondence, not ingredients that define identity into existence.

Choose a spanning tree rooted at $`a`$. Write $`t_w:D_a\to D_w`$ for the composite along its unique root-to-$`w`$ path, with $`t_a`$ the identity. For any oriented edge define the permutation of the root domain

```math
H_{vw}=t_w^{-1}\circ g_{vw}\circ t_v.
```

It follows the tree to $`v`$, crosses that edge, and returns along the tree from $`w`$. Tree edges give identity permutations. The permutations from the remaining edges, in one orientation each, generate all the closed-walk constraints. Their generated group is the rooted *holonomy group*. Define

```math
K=\bigcap_{(v,w)\in\mathcal E^+}\{b\in D_a:H_{vw}(b)=b\},
\qquad
F=K\cap\bigcap_{w\in W}t_w^{-1}(A_w).
```

**Section theorem.** Evaluation at $`a`$ gives a bijection between accepted sections and $`F`$. Its inverse is $`b\mapsto(t_w(b))_{w\in W}`$.

**Proof.** The tree-edge equations force every section to satisfy $`s_w=t_w(s_a)`$. On a remaining edge the section equation becomes $`t_w(s_a)=g_{vw}(t_v(s_a))`$, or $`H_{vw}(s_a)=s_a`$. Its acceptance conditions are exactly $`s_a\in t_w^{-1}(A_w)`$. Hence $`s_a\in F`$. Conversely, a root value in $`F`$ gives a tuple satisfying every edge equation and every acceptance condition. Its actual-world component is the original root value, so the two maps are inverse. □

This also gives an exact relation-tensor calculation. Let $`\delta(x,y)`$ be one when $`x=y`$ and zero otherwise. Then the Boolean expression

```math
\bigvee_{s\in\prod_{w\in W}D_w}
\left(
 \bigwedge_{w\in W}\mathbf 1_{A_w}(s_w)
 \ \land\!
 \bigwedge_{(v,w)\in\mathcal E^+}\delta(s_w,g_{vw}(s_v))
\right)
```

is true exactly when $`F`$ is nonempty. Replacing disjunction and conjunction by natural-number addition and multiplication counts the accepted sections and therefore gives $`|F|`$. Each full tuple contributes once; independently choosing a witness at each world before enforcing the shared edge bindings would compute a different condition. For $`n\ge 1`$, explicit permutation tables, inverses, tree transports and filters can be constructed and checked in $`O(n(|W|+|\mathcal E|))`$ operations. Enumerating the full product of domains is an alternative specification, not that efficient algorithm. [Finite modal identity transport, Theorem 1][transport-proof]

Although the chosen tree changes the displayed transports and generators, it changes neither the sections nor their actual-world values. Applying the theorem without filters shows that $`K`$ itself is tree-independent at the fixed root. On $`K`$, transport to a world is independent of the path; it need not be path-independent on every other index. The argument includes a one-world graph. If the common outer domain is empty, the nonempty world set ensures that there is no section or existential witness.

### 10.6 Full charts, selected points, and the singleton correction

Existence of one accepted section does not in general supply a full system of global coordinates. The following conditions are equivalent:

1. Every rooted cycle permutation is the identity on all of $`D_a`$.
2. A common set $`B`$ has bijective charts $`u_w:B\to D_w`$ with $`g_{vw}=u_w\circ u_v^{-1}`$ on each edge.
3. There are injective maps $`j_w:D_w\to B`$ with $`j_w\circ g_{vw}=j_v`$, where $`B`$ is their common image.
4. Every root index extends to exactly one section, without acceptance filters.

**Proof.** If all cycle permutations are identity, choose $`B=D_a`$ and $`u_w=t_w`$; the definition of $`H_{vw}`$ gives the edge factorization. Conversely, chart factors cancel around a loop, leaving identity. Inverse charts give the injective maps in the third condition. Conversely, transporting an index around a rooted loop gives $`j_a\circ H=j_a`$, and injectivity forces $`H`$ to be identity. Edge compatibility and connectedness make the images of all $`j_w`$ equal. Finally, the section theorem without filters identifies the fourth condition with $`K=D_a`$, which is the first. □ [Finite modal identity transport, Theorem 2][transport-proof]

The full-chart criterion is the finite permutation form of the standard synchronization result: full group-valued synchronization is equivalent to trivial holonomy. Gao, Brodzki and Mukherjee give that criterion and an elementary propagation argument in §2.1, Corollary 2.1. The point-valued question here is weaker: a nontrivial group action can fix one index without fixing all indices. No geometric classification, noisy estimation result or new discovery of synchronization is being claimed. [Gao, Brodzki and Mukherjee][gao-synchronization]

For example, take a triangle whose domains are $`\{0,1,2\}`$, whose two tree maps are identity, and whose remaining edge swaps $`0`$ and $`1`$ while fixing $`2`$. There is exactly one section, the constant $`2`$ assignment. There is no full chart system respecting those edge maps. A loop interpreted as literal, faithful identity for every local item could not identify two distinct indices in one domain. The same loop can consistently describe a proposed counterpart matching or a faulty identification; the mathematical data alone do not choose among these interpretations.

Separate loop witnesses are also insufficient. Partition six labels into pairs $`A,B,C`$. Let $`h_1`$ fix $`A`$ and swap within $`B,C`$; let $`h_2`$ fix $`B`$ and swap within $`A,C`$. They commute, and their product fixes $`C`$ while swapping within $`A,B`$. The four group elements have respectively six, two, two and two fixed labels, but no label is fixed by all four. Two triangles sharing the root realize the two generators with identity tree maps. Thus “each loop fixes some point” does not imply “some point is fixed by every loop.” The section theorem needs the latter, with the same point retained throughout. [Finite modal identity transport, §4][transport-proof]

There is, however, a useful simplification under stronger local hypotheses. Suppose each acceptance set is a singleton, $`A_w=\{q_w\}`$, and each edge preserves acceptance: $`g_{vw}(A_v)\subseteq A_w`$. Then necessarily $`g_{vw}(q_v)=q_w`$. The tuple $`(q_w)`$ is the unique accepted section, and every rooted cycle fixes $`q_a`$ by composing these equations. A further independent selected-point holonomy assumption is unnecessary. A triangular swap with no fixed accepted point can illustrate failure when eligible fibres have several members, or when preservation fails; it cannot refute this singleton conclusion while retaining its hypotheses. This corrects the dependency interpretation of the earlier unity proposal, not the underlying graph theorem. It still establishes only a section of the declared correspondence. [Singleton-fibre correction][singleton-correction] [Unity and identity proposal, §§3–5][unity-proposal]

Passive relabelling preserves all these conclusions. For bijections $`\pi_w:D_w\to D'_w`$, put

```math
g'_{vw}=\pi_w\circ g_{vw}\circ\pi_v^{-1},
\qquad A'_w=\pi_w(A_w),
\qquad t'_w=\pi_w\circ t_w\circ\pi_a^{-1}.
```

Adjacent inverse factors cancel, giving $`H'_{vw}=\pi_a\circ H_{vw}\circ\pi_a^{-1}`$ and $`F'=\pi_a(F)`$. Coordinatewise relabelling sends each accepted section bijectively to a new one, preserving both the Boolean answer and the count. Each world's other relations must be relabelled in every argument as well. This operation does not identify the valuations at different worlds: their existence and reception predicates may still differ arbitrarily. [Finite modal identity transport, gauge covariance][transport-proof]

### 10.7 An invariant average need not identify any individual

Linear and Boolean representations need an additional distinction. Give each local index $`x`$ a basis vector $`e_x`$, over either the real numbers or the Boolean semiring, and extend an edge permutation by $`P_{vw}e_x=e_{g_{vw}(x)}`$. A parallel family satisfies $`z_w=P_{vw}z_v`$. On a two-label triangle with a swap loop there is no point section, but $`e_0+e_1`$ is a nonzero parallel vector. Over the reals, $`(e_0+e_1)/2`$ is parallel and has coefficients summing to one. Even if every local existence filter accepts both labels, neither nonzeroness nor this normalization identifies a consistent individual. More generally, real vectors invariant under a permutation group are precisely those whose coefficients are constant on each orbit: invariance gives equality along orbit steps, and orbitwise constancy gives invariance. A nonempty finite orbit therefore supplies an invariant sum even when it contains no fixed point. [Finite modal identity transport, §4][transport-proof]

Relative to the declared basis, define the linear copy map and augmentation by

```math
\Delta_w(e_x)=e_x\otimes e_x,
\qquad \varepsilon_w(e_x)=1.
```

**Point criterion.** Over $`\mathbb R`$ or the Boolean semiring, the equations $`\Delta_w z=z\otimes z`$ and $`\varepsilon_w z=1`$ hold exactly when $`z=e_x`$ for one local index $`x`$.

**Proof.** Write $`z=\sum_x c_xe_x`$. Comparing the coefficient of $`e_x\otimes e_y`$ for $`x\ne y`$ gives $`c_xc_y=0`$; comparing a diagonal coefficient gives $`c_x=c_x^2`$. Over the reals, an idempotent coefficient is zero or one. The off-diagonal equations leave at most one coefficient equal to one, and augmentation leaves exactly one. Over the Boolean semiring the off-diagonal equations likewise forbid two supported indices, while augmentation requires nonempty support. Conversely, each basis vector satisfies both equations. The augmentation excludes zero, including when the domain is empty. □

Let $`M_{A_w}`$ be the diagonal map retaining exactly the coordinates in $`A_w`$. Adding $`M_{A_w}z_w=z_w`$ to parallelism and the point criterion gives precisely the accepted sections above: once $`z_w=e_{s_w}`$, the filter is membership and parallelism is the edge equation. The construction uses a standard basis-copy structure; Coecke, Pavlovic and Vicary describe the chosen-basis copy and deletion maps and the recovery of copyable basis elements. The elementary proof here separately establishes the real and Boolean cases and does not import their general Hilbert-space classification or a physical interpretation. [Coecke, Pavlovic and Vicary, introduction and §§2–3][coecke-bases]

The coefficient assumptions are substantive. Over $`\mathbb Z/6\mathbb Z`$, the vector $`3e_0+4e_1`$ is normalized and copyable: $`3^2=3`$, $`4^2=4`$, $`3\cdot4=0`$ and $`3+4=1`$ modulo six. It is not one basis vector. The criterion is therefore not asserted for every ring. Nor is it independent of the declared basis. Permutations preserve copying and augmentation, since both sides send $`e_x`$ to the corresponding relabelled basis expression. Under a general invertible linear change, one must transport the copy map, augmentation, filters and interpretation together. Keeping an old “one nonzero coordinate” reading after an arbitrary basis change is not faithful. Copying an index is an algebraic operation on a representation; it neither creates another individual nor makes every distributed system a single bearer. [Finite modal identity transport, Theorem 3 and coefficient control][transport-proof]

### 10.8 What full charts preserve in a modal description

Assume full charts $`u_w:B\to D_w`$, and separately supply the interpretation that $`u_w(b)`$ represents the same bearer $`b`$ at every world, including worlds where it does not exist. Define global-coordinate predicates and relations by

```math
\begin{aligned}
E(w,b)&\iff E_w(u_w(b)),\\
C(w,b)&\iff C_w(u_w(b)),\\
\mathrm{Dep}(w,c,b)&\iff \mathrm{Dep}_w(u_w(c),u_w(b)).
\end{aligned}
```

Here $`\mathrm{Dep}_w(y,x)`$ is a specified whole-existence reception relation, not a name for every interaction. Let $`R`$ and $`T`$ be finite resource and target sets, distinct from the bearer domain. For an actual intrinsic-resource relation $`I_a`$, set $`I(b,r)\iff I_a(u_a(b),r)`$. An actual resource predicate is not thereby turned into a world-indexed resource-existence predicate. Optional renaming of resource or target indices must consistently rename every affected relation argument. [Finite modal identity transport, §5][transport-proof]

An actual-anchored atom also needs a local interpretation at every evaluation world. For $`x\in D_w`$, define

```math
I_w^{a}(x,r)
\iff I_a\bigl(u_a(u_w^{-1}(x)),r\bigr).
```

Thus $`I_w^{a}(u_w(b),r)`$ agrees with $`I_a(u_a(b),r)`$ and with the global $`I(b,r)`$. Apply the same pullback $`u_a\circ u_w^{-1}`$ to every bearer argument of any actual-anchored mixed atom, including when it occurs under a modality. Resource and target arguments stay in their declared fixed coordinates, or are converted by their separately stipulated coordinate maps. The superscript $`a`$ identifies the fixed actual relation; the subscript $`w`$ records only which local bearer coordinates are used to evaluate it. This does not assert a different intrinsic relation at each world. In contrast, genuinely world-indexed atoms such as $`E_w`$, $`C_w`$ and $`\mathrm{Dep}_w`$ use their valuations at the evaluation world; no constancy of those valuations is assumed.

The conversion matters even when all local domains happen to use the same labels. Let $`W=\{a,v\}`$ and $`B=D_a=D_v=\{0,1\}`$, with $`u_a`$ the identity, $`u_v`$ the swap, and only $`a\mathcal A v`$. For one resource $`r`$, let $`I_a`$ hold only of $`(0,r)`$. At $`a`$, the globally interpreted formula $`\exists x\,(I(x,r)\land\Box I(x,r))`$ is true, witnessed by bearer $`0`$. Its local label at $`v`$ is $`1`$. Looking up the raw actual table at that destination label gives false and makes the displayed existential false, since bearer $`1`$ already fails the actual conjunct. The prescribed pullback takes destination label $`1`$ back to actual label $`0`$ and restores the correct truth value. With disjoint local domains, the raw lookup would not even have the declared type. This elementary example distinguishes the fixed actual relation from an accidental equality of coordinate labels.

**Language-preservation proposition.** These charts preserve the declared finite relational first-order language with equality, Boolean connectives and bearer quantifiers. They also preserve its modal extension when the local assignment semantics is explicitly the chart-induced one.

**Proof.** Interpret a global bearer assignment $`\beta`$ at $`w`$ as $`u_w\circ\beta`$. Atomic predicates agree by definition; equality agrees because the charts are injective. Boolean combinations preserve agreement. For a quantified variable, surjectivity makes every local value correspond to a global bearer value, and injectivity makes this reindexing exact. Thus both existential and universal quantification preserve truth. Now specify an accessibility relation $`\mathcal A`$ independently of $`\Gamma`$, and define the local box by

```math
\mathrm{Val}_v(\Box\varphi,\alpha_v)
=\bigwedge_{w:\mathcal A(v,w)}
 \mathrm{Val}_w\bigl(\varphi,
   u_w\circ u_v^{-1}\circ\alpha_v\bigr).
```

The transported assignment is $`u_w\circ\beta`$ when $`\alpha_v=u_v\circ\beta`$. Consequently each modal destination uses the same global assignment. Induction on formulas, including nested modalities, proves the claim. Quantification only over existing bearers is expressed by adding the appropriate $`E_w`$ guard, which the same induction preserves. □

This is a specified semantics whose preservation has been proved. It does not follow merely from an extensional translation that supplied no modal operators. Conventional nonempty-domain first-order semantics requires $`n>0`$. If empty outer domains are admitted instead, closed formulas can use the explicit conventions that an empty existential is false and an empty universal true; there are then no assignments to free bearer variables. The earlier section and tensor claims remain valid, but this is a different convention from a source semantics requiring a nonempty domain. [Finite modal identity transport and its independent review][transport-proof] [Modal-language review, §3][transport-review]

Under the fixed outer domain, the two universal quantifiers over bearers and accessible worlds commute. Thus both directions between $`\forall x\,\Box P(x)`$ and $`\Box\forall x\,P(x)`$ hold for unguarded outer-domain quantification. The corresponding unrestricted assertion is false for existence-guarded quantifiers. Let only $`v`$ be accessible from $`a`$, with outer domain $`\{0,1\}`$, existing domain $`E_a=\{0\}`$, $`E_v=\{0,1\}`$, and $`P`$ true only of $`0`$ at $`v`$. Then $`\forall^{E_a}x\,\Box P(x)`$ is true, while $`\Box\forall^{E_v}x\,P(x)`$ is false. Reversing the existence sets makes the first false and the second true. Charts alone impose neither domain constancy for actual existence nor an S5 accessibility frame. [Modal-language review, guarded-quantifier controls][transport-review]

In particular, the all-world same-bearer existence claim has the form

```math
\exists b\in B\ \forall w\in W:\ E_w(u_w(b)).
```

It differs from $`\forall w\in W\ \exists b\in B:\ E_w(u_w(b))`$, which permits a different witness in each world. The earlier resource-to-bearer argument already retains one witness; the new coordinates must implement that binding rather than replace it. For example, existence of an actual original resource with one uniformly existing, nonreceived bearer is expressed by

```math
\begin{aligned}
\exists t,r,b\quad&
 \mathrm{TargetReceived}(t)\land\mathrm{Relevant}(r,t)
 \land\mathrm{ResourceActual}(r)\\
&\land\neg\mathrm{ResourceReceived}(r)\land I_a(u_a(b),r)\\
&\land\forall w\in W\,
 \bigl(E_w(u_w(b))\land\neg C_w(u_w(b))\bigr).
\end{aligned}
```

The same target, resource and bearer remain under one existential scope. This formula neither supplies the original-adequacy premises nor identifies $`C_w(x)`$ with “has a supplier” without a separate representation assumption. Where necessity instead ranges only over worlds accessible from $`a`$, actual existence must be retained explicitly if $`a`$ is not guaranteed accessible. An empty accessibility set makes the box vacuous; adding actual existence then gives actual existence, not a nonvacuous alternative-world result. [Finite modal identity transport, §§5, 7][transport-proof]

<a id="receipt68-definable-root-and-reduced-descent"></a>

#### Definable actualizers and reduced descent

The selected-section theorem of §10.5 already separates coherence of a chosen root from flatness of an entire bundle. Its original finite transport record reported **647** two-state bundles, of which **323** were flat and **324** were not. The distinct review considered **55,944** bundles and **167,832** selected anchors across its triangle, square, diagonal and complete four-vertex graph families. These are historical populations for the fixed-bundle statement. They do not establish that an application chose the right cross-context identity maps, covered every relevant context, or interpreted a transported point as an actual source of reception. In particular, a nonidentity loop can fix the selected anchor. Whole-bundle nonflatness is not a counterexample to the selected-root theorem. [R68-S014] [R68-S015] [R68-S016]

A useful special case makes the actualization and dependence language explicit, including variation in the effect domain. At context $`w`$, let $`B_w`$ be the bearer set, $`E_w`$ the effect set, $`A_w\subseteq B_w\times E_w`$ the actualization relation, and $`D_w\subseteq B_w\times B_w`$ the relation “the first bearer depends on the second.” This $`D_w`$ is recipient-first; it transposes the supplier-first dependence notation used earlier in this work. Define

```math
U_w(b)\iff \forall e\in E_w\ A_w(b,e),
\qquad
N_w(b)\iff \neg\exists c\in B_w\ D_w(b,c).
```

For every edge $`w\to v`$, require bijections $`g_{wv}:B_w\to B_v`$ and $`h_{wv}:E_w\to E_v`$ that preserve and reflect both relations:

```math
A_w(b,e)\iff A_v(g_{wv}b,h_{wv}e),
\qquad
D_w(b,c)\iff D_v(g_{wv}b,g_{wv}c).
```

Take inverse maps on reversed edges and a connected context graph. If one context has a unique universal actualizer $`r`$ satisfying $`U(r)`$, then transport carries it to the unique universal actualizer in each other context. If $`N(r)`$ also holds, all these transported roots are underived in the stipulated dependence relation. Every loop fixes the unique root, so the roots form a coherent selected section even when the remaining bearers have nontrivial holonomy. [R68-S017] [R68-S018]

**Proof.** Given $`U_w(b)`$ and any $`e'\in E_v`$, surjectivity of $`h_{wv}`$ gives $`e'=h_{wv}(e)`$ for some $`e`$. Preservation gives $`A_v(g_{wv}b,e')`$. Applying the inverse maps proves reflection of universality. Similarly, a dependence witness $`D_v(g_{wv}b,c')`$ has a preimage $`c`$ under $`g_{wv}`$, and reflection would give $`D_w(b,c)`$. Thus absence of a witness is preserved and reflected. Bijection then carries a singleton universal-actualizer set to a singleton. Composed transport around a loop is an automorphism, hence must fix that definable singleton. The path-independence conclusion follows from §10.5. No claim that the loop fixes every bearer was used.

Both sorts must be included. Preserving bearers while omitting effects can turn “actualizes every represented effect” into a false claim about every effect. Omitting dependence reflection can turn an unrepresented supplier into apparent underivability. An arbitrary bijection, multiple candidate roots, a disconnected graph or an independently unjustified identity map breaks a different premise. Conversely, a full isomorphism requirement may be too restrictive for an intended modal application with genuinely varying structure. The historical primary record reports **1,728** structures and **2,064** automorphisms, including **336** nontrivial root-fixing automorphisms; its distinct review reports **20,736** renamed structure pairs. These are finite checks of the stated structure-preserving contract, not proof that that contract captures possible worlds. [R68-S017] [R68-S018] [R68-S019]

There is a related quotient formulation for a selected invariant subbundle $`S_w\subseteq B_w`$. Assume each edge transport restricts to a bijection between these selected fibres. Identify points connected by transport and let $`Q`$ be the resulting set of transport orbits. The natural map $`j_w:S_w\to Q`$ is injective exactly when no orbit contains two different points of the same fibre. This is equivalent to every closed-walk transport fixing every point of every selected fibre: a closed walk moving a selected point creates a same-fibre collision, while any same-fibre collision is witnessed by a closed transport walk. Under these conditions the $`j_w`$ form an injective common-image descent. The selected subbundle can satisfy them while the full bundle fails them. [R68-S027] [R68-S028] [R68-S029]

The common image is unique in the appropriate **reduced** sense. Suppose injective maps $`i_w:S_w\to U`$ commute with transport and $`U=\bigcup_w i_w(S_w)`$. The map $`[s]\mapsto i_w(s)`$ from $`Q`$ to $`U`$ is well-defined by commutation and is surjective by reducedness. To show injectivity, use connectedness to represent any two orbits in one fibre; equality of their images then contradicts injectivity of that fibre's $`i_w`$ unless the representatives, and hence the orbits, coincide. This gives the unique isomorphism commuting with the fibre maps. If arbitrary unused elements may be added to $`U`$, uniqueness of the entire codomain is false. The original audit recorded that omitted reducedness condition; §10.6's common-image construction already takes the image generated by the fibres. [R68-S028] [R68-S030]

The same audit retained three further defects: necessary/external flags had not been checked, effect maps and preservation of actualization and dependence had not been tested, and an intra-world unity passage had been presented as stronger cross-world evidence. The repaired record reports **979** labelled cases and **50,000** random three-fibre cases, with root descent surviving a nonflat full bundle. Its common-model witness has two contexts, a unique universal underived necessary external root, and plural coordinated wisdom, power and knowledge roles; those roles are neither all local to the root nor identified by the witness with the creator role. This is a formal consistency witness for the given predicates. It does not establish metaphysical adequacy or a source interpretation. The retained translated primary-source comparison is explicitly partial overlap, not an Arabic-text verification or direct evidence for the cross-world identification premise. [R68-S027] [R68-S028] [R68-S029] [R68-S030]

### 10.9 Restricting bearers can erase the grounds of their reception

A selected section has less preservation power than full charts. Let $`B_{\mathrm{sec}}`$ be the set of all compatible point sections. Evaluation $`s\mapsto s_w`$ is injective at every world: agreeing at one vertex forces agreement along every path. It need not be surjective. Thus replacing every local domain by these coherent sections can delete individuals needed as witnesses of other assertions.

The three-label swap triangle illustrates the problem. Only the constant $`2`$ section survives. At $`a`$, let $`\mathrm{Dep}_a(0,2)`$ be the only supplier edge and let $`C_a(2)`$ be true. In the full local domain, $`2`$ has a supplier. In the retained domain containing only $`2`$, there is no supplier edge. Copying $`2`$'s existence and reception predicates faithfully does not preserve their asserted connection with the dependency relation. A resource borne only by $`0`$ likewise loses its realization witness. This is a failure of the proposed restriction, not a defect in a previously proved implication using the full bearer domain. [Finite modal identity transport, §5][transport-proof]

Even full coherent identity does not justify restricting the supplier domain to necessary beings. Take two worlds $`a,v`$ and identity charts on $`\{b,c,d\}`$. Let $`b`$ exist at both, $`c`$ only at $`a`$, and $`d`$ only at $`v`$. Let the only supplier edges be $`\mathrm{Dep}_a(c,b)`$ and $`\mathrm{Dep}_v(d,b)`$. Both endpoints of each edge exist where that edge holds. The target is received at both worlds, with a changing supplier. Restriction to the necessarily existing domain $`\{b\}`$ removes both witnesses. Necessary existence of a target does not entail independence, and persistent receipt does not require one fixed supplier. These are separate predicates before any philosophical appraisal of the fixture's possibility.

There is an exact smaller condition than retaining every local individual. Let $`j_w:B_{\mathrm{ret}}\to D_w`$ be injective retained-domain maps, and induce

```math
\mathrm{Dep}_{\mathrm{ret}}(w,c,b)
\iff \mathrm{Dep}_w(j_w(c),j_w(b)).
```

**Witness-preservation theorem.** At a specified retained target $`b`$ and world $`w`$, local and retained supplier existence agree if and only if

```math
\bigl[\exists y\in D_w:\mathrm{Dep}_w(y,j_w(b))\bigr]
\ \Longrightarrow
\bigl[\exists c\in B_{\mathrm{ret}}:
             \mathrm{Dep}_w(j_w(c),j_w(b))\bigr].
```

**Proof.** A retained supplier always maps to a local supplier by the definition of the induced relation. The only possibly missing direction is exactly the displayed implication. It therefore is equivalent to equality of the two existence truth values. Negating those values also preserves agreement. Conversely, agreement gives that local-to-retained implication. □

Injectivity is appropriate when retained labels are to distinguish retained individuals; the elementary existential equivalence itself needs only the stated map and induced relation. Surjectivity is sufficient but stronger than necessary. If both retained $`c`$ and omitted $`d`$ supply a target, retaining $`c`$ preserves existence of a supplier, although supplier counts and claims about $`d`$ can change. Absence of a retained supplier is evidence of full local nonreceipt only when the displayed condition is justified at that target and world. [Finite modal identity transport, Theorem 4; review, §1][transport-proof] [Witness-preservation review][transport-review]

Suppose the intended reception predicate satisfies $`C_w(x)\iff\exists y\,\mathrm{Dep}_w(y,x)`$. Copying $`C_w`$ preserves that representation only if the condition holds at every pair for which the equivalence is asserted. A contract quantified over all worlds and bearers cannot silently be replaced by a check only at actually existing targets. For actual resource realization, the analogous precise requirement is

```math
\bigl[\exists y\in D_a:\ E_a(y)\land I_a(y,r)\bigr]
\ \Longrightarrow
\bigl[\exists b\in B_{\mathrm{ret}}:
 E_a(j_a(b))\land I_a(j_a(b),r)\bigr]
```

for each actual resource in the needed scope. This requires some suitable retained bearer, not every bearer of the resource. Neither condition establishes the philosophical truth of its local relations.

Preserving these existential statements still does not preserve every premise. Retain a necessary bearer $`b`$ and omit an actual, contingent bearer $`c`$; let reception and dependency be empty, and let an actual resource be intrinsically borne by $`b`$. Both supplier preservation and actual realization hold. Yet the universal claim “every actual contingent bearer is received” is false in the full domain because of $`c`$ and true after restriction. The independent review supplies this control to distinguish the two existential conditions from preservation of an entire quantified theory. Removing counterexamples can make a universal statement easier to satisfy. Full language preservation above keeps its bijective-chart hypothesis. [Independent modal-transport review, §4][transport-review]

### 10.10 What is—and is not—unified by the construction

The correspondence itself is scientifically relevant information. On two worlds with outer domains $`\{0,1\}`$, identity alignment and empty dependency relations, set $`E_a=\{0\}`$. Compare $`E_v=\{0\}`$ with $`E_v=\{1\}`$. The structures at $`v`$ are isomorphic under a swap, so their same-world first-order sentences agree. Nevertheless, the first system has one bearer existing at both worlds and the second has none. A record of each world only up to independent local isomorphism cannot determine this same-bearer target. By contrast, passively swapping both $`E_v`$ and the alignment in the first system preserves its answer. Independent renaming of a valuation while holding correspondence fixed changes the represented data; simultaneous renaming of both does not. [Finite modal identity transport, §6][transport-proof]

This limitation does not forbid a richer qualitative account from specifying its own correspondence, nor show that unnamed descriptions lack concrete bearers. Dasgupta's *Individuals* explicitly brackets the relevant a priori modal dispute, and its extensional language comparison leaves modal expansions for further work; its comparison models have nonempty domains. *The Bare Necessities* discusses qualitative individuating roles and counterpart semantics while separating necessitation from grounding. Those observations support a scope limit here, not a refutation of either account. A many-valued or nonfunctional counterpart relation is outside the bijection theorem, and a counterpart interpretation can have a different modal target. Successful modal truth preservation also supplies no semantics for essence, explanatory priority or grounding merely by preserving extensions. [Dasgupta 2009, pp. 37, 63 n. 40, 64][dasgupta-individuals] [Dasgupta 2011, §§4–5][dasgupta-bare-necessities]

Several further notions of unity therefore need their own arguments. A unique eligible token at each world, a unique coherent section, numerical identity of its represented bearer, mereological simplicity, integrated agency, and universal productive scope are different conclusions. The earlier unity proposal separates them through useful conditional controls. Read in their corrected scope, these controls do not certify the metaphysical possibility of every named rival, and they do not cancel the later affirmative appraisal in section 10.4. [Unity and identity proposal, §§2–7; later reconciliation][unity-proposal] [Singleton-fibre correction and status reconciliation][singleton-correction]

For numerical identity, one may give each world a different token, choose flat transports linking them uniquely, and still interpret the tokens as counterparts rather than one individual. The unique section then exists without the additional identity interpretation. Conversely, one may hold a bearer numerically fixed while changing its role predicate at another world. Persistence of the bearer does not establish persistence of every role. These controls distinguish what the stipulated relations say; they do not resolve the underlying theory of identity.

For bearer-local roles, consider a system with three parts, one knowing, one selecting, and one realizing an outcome. Declaring a system token whose role predicate means “some part has this role” makes every role available to that system. It does not establish that one part has them all, or that the resulting aggregate is the individual required by another argument. A genuine organized collective may be an appropriate bearer for some purposes, but the change of granularity and incidence must be stated. Even one substrate that bears all the powers need not integrate apprehension, selection and realization in the same reason-guided episode. The affirmative agency comparison in section 12.4 concerns that stronger relation, not merely a list of capacities.

For ontological scope, a unique role bearer can have proper parts under the declared mereology, and the same incidence data can leave competing theories of properties undecided. A common root may coexist with attributes realized only by coordinated nonroot members. A single source description can also admit two proposed mappings to different worldly referents; co-reference within the source does not authenticate either mapping. Finally, a unified and integrated agent may actualize only a proper subdomain. Extending that conclusion to universal Creatorhood needs its independently justified productive domain and bridge. None of these inferences is supplied by counting sections. The source proposal's translated attribute-locality premise is likewise source-relative; it is not a new primary verification or a consensus claim about a theological school. [Unity and identity proposal, controls and source scope][unity-proposal]

The finite mathematics thus supplies exact conditions for preserving the candidate whose philosophical grounds have been separately argued. It does not reconstruct possible worlds from observations or extend finite conjunctions automatically to infinitely many worlds. Standing capacity, an act-kind, an individual act and a created effect remain different types; neither an empty act extension nor a permanent possibility supplies a necessary particular. No premise that every emergent act is created, no automatic inference from a new relation to borrowed perfection, and no actuality-from-possibility principle enters these proofs. In particular, this account of labels and witnesses neither completes the unfinished programme for an n-person noetic field nor replaces its original scientific objective.

### 10.11 Attribute incidence and a common bearer

Coherent transport answers whether local descriptions can retain one selected individual. It does not decide which attributes that individual bears or what an attribute is. Those questions should be separated even before modal transport is considered. The relevant finite incidence arguments can be stated without selecting a theory of properties. They make explicit both the force of a common-bearer conclusion and the information it leaves open. [Attribute incidence and bearer integration][attribute-incidence] [Property interpretation and bearer underdetermination][property-interpretation]

Let $`A`$ be a finite nonempty set of attribute coordinates and $`B`$ a finite nonempty set of eligible bearers at a fixed world, time and respect. Let $`I\subseteq B\times A`$ be the independently interpreted incidence relation. Write

```math
B_a=\{b\in B:I(b,a)\},\qquad
L(I)\iff\forall a\in A\ \exists b\in B\ I(b,a),\qquad
C(I)\iff\exists b\in B\ \forall a\in A\ I(b,a).
```

The interpretation of $`I`$ must specify whether an entry means actual possession, a standing capacity, a qualified exercise, or merely a functional role. These predicates cannot be substituted for one another because they share a label. Where attribution requires guards, the admitted entry must satisfy those guards in the same interpretation. Neither an incidence matrix nor the following proof supplies that substantive interpretation.

There is a useful intermediate measure. A subset $`S\subseteq B`$ **covers the attributes** when every attribute is borne by at least one member of $`S`$. Define

```math
\beta(I)=\min\{|S|:S\subseteq B,\ \forall a\in A\ \exists b\in S\ I(b,a)\},
```

with $`\beta(I)=\infty`$ when there is no cover. This is the minimum number of bearers needed for the represented package; it measures neither causal integration nor the number of substances in reality. [Attribute-bearer cover criterion][attribute-cover]

**Incidence and cover proposition.** Under the stated finite nonempty-domain assumptions,

```math
L(I)\iff\beta(I)\lt\infty,
\qquad
C(I)\iff\bigcap_{a\in A}B_a\ne\varnothing
       \iff\beta(I)=1.
```

The number of common bearers is $`\left|\bigcap_{a\in A}B_a\right|`$. Thus existence and uniqueness are different conditions.

**Proof.** A cover supplies an incident bearer for every attribute, so it implies $`L(I)`$. Conversely, if every attribute has a bearer, the finite set $`B`$ itself is a cover. A common bearer belongs to every $`B_a`$ and its singleton covers the attributes. Conversely, a one-member cover has a member incident to every attribute. Because $`A`$ is nonempty, the empty subset cannot cover it; hence a one-member cover makes the minimum exactly one. Finally, common bearers are precisely the members of the displayed intersection, which proves the counting and uniqueness statement. □

The distinctions have small exact controls. With two attributes and $`B_K=\{u\}`$, $`B_W=\{v\}`$, where $`u\ne v`$, local availability holds and $`\beta=2`$, but there is no common bearer. With three attributes and

```math
B_K=\{u,v\},\qquad B_W=\{v,w\},\qquad B_P=\{u,w\},
```

each pair of attributes has a common bearer, while the total intersection is empty and $`\beta=2`$. If every attribute instead has bearer set $`\{u,v\}`$, then $`\beta=1`$ but there are two common bearers. If some $`B_a`$ is empty, no cover exists. These are controls for arbitrary incidence systems; no additional geometric or logical intersection principle has been assumed. The nonempty-attribute assumption is material: an empty attribute family has an empty cover of size zero, although every available bearer satisfies its universal condition vacuously. [Attribute incidence, local and pairwise controls][attribute-incidence]

A positive attribution argument can establish more than local availability. Suppose an independently fixed interpreted bearer $`d\in B`$ satisfies every $`\mathrm{Guard}_a(d)`$, and the accepted rules give $`\mathrm{Guard}_a(d)\Rightarrow I(d,a)`$ for each $`a`$. Applying each rule gives every $`I(d,a)`$, and therefore $`C(I)`$ with witness $`d`$. The inference is valid. What the common target supplies is **sameness of subject across the applications**; the guards and rules still supply its attributes. Merely reusing a title or printed name does not establish that sameness. If the applications concern separately introduced $`d_a`$, one needs an identity or common-realization argument before exchanging the quantifiers. [Attribute incidence, fixed-target argument; historical rereview][attribute-incidence] [Bearer-integration rereview][attribute-incidence-review]

#### Bearer-integration evidence and two superseded approvals

The bearer-intersection study's recorded mathematical result must be separated from its failed admission history. The [first cold audit][receipt-g-03] announced no blocking defect, and its [no-repair disposition][receipt-g-02] preserved the frozen theorem, model and checker. A subsequent [custody correction][receipt-g-04] showed that this approval contradicted the frozen source-check result, which had reported failure on a wording locator. The earlier `PASS` and no-repair statement are therefore superseded evidence and cannot support admission. The [V2 repair][receipt-g-06] changed the source probe to an actual phrase in the supplied translation, preserving the failed result and leaving the mathematical relation model unchanged. The [V2 source receipt][receipt-g-15] reports four dependency-member hashes, one translation hash and five locators matching, with Arabic-primary verification and source truth still unestablished.

The [V2 cold audit][receipt-g-05] and [no-further-repair statement][receipt-g-07] did not complete the chain either. The distinct rereview stopped before semantic execution because the model was invalid YAML: one field had been opened as a sequence and then followed by a mapping key at an incompatible level. The [structured-data audit][receipt-g-08] preserves that setup failure and rules out V2 admission. The [V3 repair][receipt-g-13] separates the speech coordinates and their implication status into a valid mapping without changing the theorem, source statement or authority ceiling. The later [V3 cold audit][receipt-g-09], [distinct rereview][receipt-g-10] and [final repair disposition][receipt-g-12] report the parsed model and successful scoped checks. These records preserve both earlier defects; they do not retrospectively claim semantic execution of the blocked V2 attempt.

The [primary relation record][receipt-g-14] reports 74,954 finite incidence matrices, including 57,164 locally populated and 20,938 pairwise-intersecting systems. Of these, 39,374 have local availability without a common bearer, and 3,174 have pairwise intersections without a total intersection. All 19,804 fixed-witness cases passed and no criterion failure was reported. The [distinct result][receipt-g-11] used bitmasks instead of the primary set representation, reporting the same exhaustive population through four attributes and four bearers, 25,000 larger sampled systems and no criterion, fixed-witness or sampled failure. These are source-reported execution results; no original model parser or checker is run here. The present cover-number, uniqueness and empty-attribute qualifications have their explicit proofs above and are not additional historical test claims.

The [admission record][receipt-g-01] is correspondingly limited. An independently fixed interpreted bearer can support the positive attribution rule, but a repeated title or source string cannot supply numerical identity. The pairwise counterexample concerns arbitrary set systems; a warranted additional intersection principle would be a different hypothesis. Plural neutral examples are not complete interpretations of a source theory that already fixes one Creator as its target. Nor does one bearer alone establish derivational unity when its attributes remain independently variable primitives. The qiyās rule's local qualifications do not themselves supply global unity. Capacity, occurrence, qualified predication, Divine Name, revealed content and identification of uncreated Speech remain distinct stages. The elementary set-theoretic application claims no general novelty or historical theorem identity, and its translated-source access does not establish Arabic-primary confirmation, external source-specialist review or owner adoption.


### 10.12 Bearer granularity and the information retained by a profile

Once the complete incidence relation and bearer identity are fixed, common-bearer existence is determined. A rival with no common bearer cannot preserve those very data and change $`C(I)`$. This corrects an ambiguity in treating distributed realization as another interpretation of the *same incidence reduct*. Distributed realization can preserve a coarser observation or performance profile while changing incidence. It is not a counterexample to the incidence proposition. [Property interpretation, shared reduct and plural-realization control][property-interpretation]

The distinction is invariant under harmless changes of labels. Suppose $`f:B\to B'`$ is a bijection, the attribute coordinates retain their meanings, and $`I'(f(b),a)\iff I(b,a)`$. Then $`B'_a=f(B_a)`$. A member of every $`B'_a`$ has a unique inverse image belonging to every $`B_a`$, so

```math
\bigcap_{a\in A}B'_a=f\left(\bigcap_{a\in A}B_a\right).
```

Consequently common-bearer existence and its exact number are preserved. A subset covers before relabelling exactly when its image covers afterwards, and the bijection preserves its size. Hence $`\beta(I')=\beta(I)`$ as well. This is a change of coordinates within the same incidence interpretation.

A change in granularity is different. Let $`q:B\to C`$ be a surjection assigning fine-grained bearers to system labels. Define the coarse relation by

```math
J(c,a)\iff\exists b\in B\,[q(b)=c\land I(b,a)].
```

This relation means that *some bearer assigned to the system has the attribute*. It does not say that the system directly instantiates the original attribute in the original respect.

**Granularity proposition.** If $`S`$ covers $`I`$, then $`q(S)`$ covers $`J`$. Thus $`\beta(J)\le\beta(I)`$, using the extended order with $`\infty`$ greatest. Common-bearer existence can become true under this operation even when it was false before.

**Proof.** For every $`a`$, choose the witness $`b\in S`$ supplied by its cover condition. Then $`J(q(b),a)`$, and $`q(b)\in q(S)`$. Therefore $`q(S)`$ is a cover and has at most $`|S|`$ members. Taking a minimum proves the finite case; the case $`\beta(I)=\infty`$ is immediate from the extended order. For strict change, take three bearers $`b_K,b_W,b_P`$, each bearing exactly its named attribute, and map all three to one system label $`c`$. The fine-grained package has $`\beta(I)=3`$ and no common bearer, whereas all three $`J(c,a)`$ hold and $`\beta(J)=1`$. □

This is precisely a change from $`\exists b\,\forall a\,I(b,a)`$ to the weaker requirement that, for each attribute, some potentially different bearer lies in the chosen system. It can be an appropriate description of a collective. What it cannot do is establish that the collective is the individual required by an argument whose predication remains bearer-local. In particular, coarse relabelling does not identify the three original bearers. Nor can this existential aggregation conjure an entirely uninstantiated attribute: if no fine-grained bearer has $`a`$, then no coarse system has $`a`$ under the displayed definition.

An external profile can omit bearer assignment altogether. Consider three functional modules with binary input $`x`$ and values $`k=x`$, $`w=k`$, $`p=w`$. Observe only the input-output map $`x\mapsto p`$. Assigning all three modules to one bearer and assigning them to three distinct bearers gives the same map, $`p=x`$, and the same module-level transition equations. Under direct role incidence, however, the first assignment has a common bearer and the second has none. This construction proves a limitation of that specified observation map, conditional on admitting both bearer assignments. It does not establish that two concrete physical or metaphysical realizations are possible, or that a functional input register is genuine knowledge. If the observation includes the full bearer-incidence relation, the pair is already distinguished.

Even a common bearer need not make one represented operation guide another. Compare the preceding equations with $`k=x`$, $`w=x`$, $`p=w`$, placing all modules on one bearer in both systems. Their ordinary input-output maps agree, but the second selection reads $`x`$ directly rather than the value of $`k`$. An intervention fixing $`k=1-x`$ while retaining $`x`$ makes the first output $`1-x`$ and the second $`x`$. Thus a suitable additional causal test distinguishes this particular pair, whereas additional unperturbed trials do not. This is an elementary specified mechanism, not an experiment already performed, a general consciousness test, or a sufficient analysis of acting for an apprehended reason. It identifies the extra causal information that mere possession and ordinary success can omit. The stronger practical comparison remains the one developed in section 12.4.

### 10.13 Connected attribute arguments and numerical co-reference

A connected argument can link different attribute roles without identifying their bearers. Conversely, co-instantiation can hold without a derivation connecting the attributes. To state this precisely, let $`V`$ be a finite nonempty set of role coordinates and $`\mathcal H`$ a family of nonempty dependency supports, each a subset of $`V`$. Join two distinct coordinates when some support contains both. The resulting undirected graph records which roles participate together in the selected dependencies; it does not by itself record the variables or individuals appearing in the complete propositions. [Source-derivation integration, connectedness and bearer semantics][source-incidence]

**Connected-support proposition.** This graph is connected if and only if every partition of $`V`$ into at least two nonempty blocks has a support meeting more than one block.

**Proof.** If the graph is connected, choose vertices in different blocks and a path between them. Some consecutive pair lies in different blocks. A support containing that pair crosses the partition. Conversely, if the graph is disconnected, take its connected components as blocks. Any support with vertices in different components would itself connect them, so no support crosses this nontrivial partition. □

That theorem concerns the selected representation. It neither establishes a unique representation of a source nor proves that the dependencies are true. A graph mixing attributes, actions and methodological eligibility conditions must keep those sorts distinct; a guard is not another bearer merely because it is a node. The received source analysis required precisely this correction, together with separation of textual co-reference from worldly identity. [Source-incidence correction, scope and node sorts][source-incidence-correction]

The numerical limit needs an actual model construction. Use one bearer variable $`x_v`$ and unary role predicate $`P_v`$ for each role $`v`$. For every ordered support $`h=(v_1,\ldots,v_m)`$, add a relation $`T_h`$ of the corresponding arity. Consider only the weak relational assertion

```math
\exists (x_v)_{v\in V}\left[
\bigwedge_{v\in V}P_v(x_v)\ \land
\bigwedge_{h=(v_1,\ldots,v_m)\in\mathcal H}
T_h(x_{v_1},\ldots,x_{v_m})\right],
```

where the finite tuple of quantifiers ranges over the bearer domain. No further axioms of these relation symbols are imposed. If a selected representation also contains method guards, hold their separately typed values true; do not turn them into bearer variables.

**Bearer-partition construction.** Every partition $`\Pi`$ of the role set has a model of this weak assertion whose role-bearing individuals are exactly the blocks of $`\Pi`$.

**Proof.** Let the bearer domain be the set of blocks and write $`[v]`$ for the block containing $`v`$. Set $`P_v=\{[v]\}`$. Interpret $`T_h`$ as the singleton containing the tuple $`([v_1],\ldots,[v_m])`$. Assign $`x_v=[v]`$. Every unary conjunct and every relational conjunct is then true. The registered support family is unchanged. Its graph can therefore be connected while the partition is discrete and the role bearers are all distinct. If the partition has more than one block, no individual belongs to every $`P_v`$; if it has one block, its member bears them all. □

The hypothesis is deliberately exact. **Absence of an equality symbol is not enough** to license this construction for an arbitrary theory. The equality-free sentence $`\exists x\,(P(x)\land Q(x))`$ already requires a common bearer through its one variable. Likewise, $`\exists x\,P(x)`$ together with $`\forall x\,(P(x)\Rightarrow Q(x))`$ supplies one. Fixed relation interpretations, functional constraints, typing conditions or other premises can also prevent arbitrary bearer assignments. The construction applies when the stated weak relational expansions are actually admissible. A role graph that has forgotten the variable bindings of a richer source cannot establish that the richer source permits those expansions.

For the converse separation, take one bearer $`g`$, make every role predicate true of it, and register no cross-role dependencies. Common incidence holds, although a role graph with at least two vertices is disconnected. Adding all the selected dependencies can give a connected, common-bearer description; the two facts still have different premises. A source with genuine cross-role arguments is consequently richer than a flat list of labels, without connectedness doing the additional work of an identity proof.

Textual co-reference can supply that identity premise **within an accepted source interpretation**. If a correctly reconstructed proposition attributes the relevant roles to one referent, a realization denying the co-reference fails that proposition. This is a legitimate restriction of the model class, conditional on the proposition and its applicability. It is not a derivation of its truth from graph topology. The source analysis also separates the creed's propositions, the commentator's endorsement or correction, translation adequacy and external application. Its particular criticism of an argument from shared necessary-existence predication does not refute every unity argument. The generic-versus-numerical distinction already established in section 2 remains in force. [Source-derivation integration and its corrections][source-incidence] [Source-incidence correction][source-incidence-correction]

### 10.14 Property interpretation beyond incidence

Fix an incidence structure $`R=(B,A,I)`$. An **interpretation expansion** retains this structure while adding whatever objects, relations and semantic commitments a proposed account of attributes requires. Its data should state the truth conditions of predication, bearer identity, causal and modal commitments, and any relevant source or function premises. Merely naming an expansion “realist,” “conceptualist” or “powers-based” does not establish those commitments or their coherence. [Property interpretation, interpretation profiles][property-interpretation]

Some elementary expansions illustrate what the reduct omits. A predicate-only presentation uses unary predicates $`P_a(b)\iff I(b,a)`$ and adds no attribute objects. An object presentation adds a separate sort $`U=\{u_a:a\in A\}`$ and stipulates $`\mathrm{Inst}(b,u_a)\iff I(b,a)`$. A particularized-quality presentation instead adds the tokens

```math
T=\{(b,a):I(b,a)\},
```

with bearer map $`\mathrm{bearer}(b,a)=b`$ and kind map $`\mathrm{kind}(b,a)=a`$. A bearer has an $`a`$-token exactly when $`I(b,a)`$; tokens of the same kind can be related by the stipulated resemblance relation. For example, if two bearers have one shared role, the object presentation has one role object instantiated twice, whereas the particularized presentation has two tokens with different bearers. Both recover the same incidence facts. In each case the verification is immediate from the defining equivalence, and the common-bearer set remains $`\bigcap_aB_a`$.

These are explicit limited presentations, not proofs of a complete metaphysical theory of universals or tropes. Reifying a predicate symbol does not establish a universal's reality; indexing a pair does not establish a concrete quality. Nor does reproducing finite resemblance judgments establish identity of all intensional, causal or modal facts. The constructions show exactly why the incidence table alone fails to adjudicate those additional commitments when the proposed class admits the different expansions.

A scheme-indexed presentation can similarly use a relation $`\mathrm{Class}(s,b,a)`$ with $`\mathrm{Class}(s_0,b,a)\iff I(b,a)`$ at the recorded scheme $`s_0`$. The recorded table need not determine its extension at other schemes, or settle whether the classification depends constitutively on an intellect. Conversely, if the admitted interpretation independently requires scheme-independent truth, an expansion violating that requirement is excluded; it cannot be reintroduced by pointing only to agreement at $`s_0`$. Powers and pattern interpretations likewise require independently specified manifestation, causal or pattern structure. A bare finite table does not establish dispositional essence, sparse naturalness or explanatory compressibility. These qualifications preserve the rivals as questions requiring substantive comparison, without certifying every named theory as a realization of every table.

Likewise, the occurrence of every attribute on one bearer leaves open whether that co-instantiation is primitive or grounded, whether the bearer is concrete or abstract under the intended semantics, and whether a further source predicate applies to it. A connected syntactic derivation is not already a metaphysical grounding relation. The same incidence structure can support incompatible additional assignments to these omitted coordinates only when the admitted class genuinely permits those assignments; the table alone supplies neither their truth nor their possibility. The concrete-resource and original-source arguments earlier in this chapter therefore retain their own interpretation premises.

The general identification condition is elementary but useful. Let $`\mathcal M`$ be the admitted class of interpreted models, let $`\pi:\mathcal M\to\mathcal P`$ be the registered information profile, and let $`\tau:\mathcal M\to Q`$ be the particular conclusion to be identified. The profile may include incidence, specified responses to interventions, and other independently interpreted data. Identification means there is a function $`f:\pi(\mathcal M)\to Q`$ with $`\tau=f\circ\pi`$.

**Profile criterion.** Such a function exists if and only if every two admitted models with the same profile have the same target value.

**Proof.** A factorization gives $`\tau(M)=f(\pi(M))=f(\pi(N))=\tau(N)`$ whenever the profiles agree. Conversely, assign to each realized profile the common target value of its models. The assumed agreement makes this assignment well-defined and gives the required factorization. The empty admitted class has an empty realized profile and supplies no actual model or conclusion. □

In particular, two genuinely admitted expansions with the same recorded incidence and responses but different ontology conclusions obstruct identification by that profile. Merely placing opposite labels on two tuples does not establish their admission as complete metaphysical theories. The result is conditional on their actual interpretation and on every imposed constraint. This is an application of the profile criterion already used in the normativity and recognition treatments, with no new mathematical novelty claimed. [Property interpretation, bounded underdetermination conclusion][property-interpretation]

If additional observations have values determined by $`\pi`$ alone, equal-profile models still agree on them: composing each observation function with the same profile gives the same answer. Further instances of an invariant kind of measurement therefore cannot separate that pair. An added intervention or semantic premise can change the situation by distinguishing the pair, or by independently excluding one member from the admitted class. It need not separate every other pair. The module intervention in section 10.12 provides one explicit example of the former possibility; an independently warranted same-subject proposition provides an example of the latter for bearer incidence.

The ontology of attributes and mind-body reduction ask different questions. The first concerns what, if anything, attributes are; the second concerns whether the relevant mental attributes reduce to physical ones. A thin incidence signature containing neither a reduction relation nor constraints on it cannot settle that second question. Adding either truth value for a free reduction claim while keeping its incidence reduct fixed demonstrates formal independence at that thin scope. It does not show that every fully developed theory of properties admits both reductions or their denials. Likewise, a stance on mental irreducibility does not, by itself, choose between the object and particularized-quality presentations. The missing work is the account's actual reduction and ontology commitments. [Property interpretation, distinct axes and reduction control][property-interpretation]

Function fixation is another distinct question. A specified causal contribution, selected history, design relation or source-relative normative purpose must have its own content and warrant. Even when one of those relations fixes a function, no bare incidence theorem decides whether its bearer has universals, tropes or powers. Defining the function-fixing relation so that only a favored ontology can satisfy it would assume the proposed conclusion unless the restrictive definition has independent justification. The affirmative function arguments and their negative controls are developed in the normativity work; this observation neither replaces them nor reopens their already qualified results. A source-relative account of an intrinsic disposition likewise needs a separate property interpretation if that is the question being asked. [Property interpretation, function and ontology][property-interpretation]

### 10.15 Guarded attribution and the scope of the result

The received attribute study places its source-based inference under six conditions: intrinsic excellence; deficiency of total absence in the relevant respect; removal of essential creaturely limitation; the relevant source relation; attribution to the bearer rather than a mere conduit; and attribution without equating the source's mode with the creature's. Those are stated premises of a school-relative a-fortiori argument. The fixed-target proof in section 10.11 explains how several such valid applications can converge on one subject, while locating their common reference separately from the local eligibility conditions. It gives no warrant to omit a guard merely because an attribute is observed in a creature. [Attribute incidence and its source-ancestry note][attribute-incidence] [Source-relative bearer attribution][attribute-source-note]

A bearer-local predication rule can exclude transferring an attribute to a conduit while leaving the general ontology of that attribute open. Predicate truth can be restricted to the qualified locus, a particularized quality to its bearer, or instantiation to the relevant individual. These presentations can agree on the local prohibition. Their agreement does not authenticate every additional ontology or remove an ontology-specific source constraint. The source claim is used at the public study's declared translated-source scope; the present argument does not claim fresh receipt or authentication of its exact translation, Arabic text or wider apparatus. The ordinary incidence proofs above require none of those unavailable primary bytes. [Property interpretation, attribute-locus rule][property-interpretation] [Source-relative bearer attribution][attribute-source-note]

Nor does one bearer of knowledge, volition, power and life supply every later conclusion about speech. Speech capacity and actual speech remain different; actual speech and a praiseworthy qualification remain different; capacity does not itself authorize a divine name; an occurrence does not identify a revelation; and a created expression does not establish the source-relative predication of uncreated content. Each step needs the corresponding occurrence, normative, naming, semantic or source premise. Formal articulability or command-response behavior alone supplies none of those theological identifications. These are limits on the stated premises, not a denial of a fuller source argument that supplies the missing premises. [Attribute incidence, speech distinctions][attribute-incidence]

The same allocation applies to the other kinds of unity. A common incidence bearer does not by itself have to be mereologically simple, necessarily retain its attributes, or satisfy the identity and existence conditions across worlds. Sections 10.5–10.10 already give the exact transport conditions and counterexamples. Causal integration requires more than common incidence, and informed agency requires more than a causal connection carrying arbitrary signals. Section 12.4 supplies the separate positive argument about understanding and owning a fitting reason. Neither the new finite examples nor a general powers label settles that argument.

The positive conclusions are therefore exact. A sound fixed-subject attribution gives a common bearer; complete incidence determines whether one exists; an independently justified co-reference premise can exclude distributed assignments; and a suitable causal intervention can distinguish mechanisms which ordinary performance leaves together. A substantive property theory can also restrict the admissible expansions through warranted constitutive, causal, modal or source commitments. Its restrictions must be assessed as arguments, rather than treated as consequences of an impoverished profile.

These limits do not retract the affirmative source-unity judgment in sections 9–10.4. That judgment uses actual original production, the nominated received field, fitting original efficacy, mediation and nonduplication. Those premises contain more than local role availability or external response equality. A control satisfying only the weaker incidence or role-graph conditions is not a countermodel to that stronger argument. Conversely, the stronger argument should identify the independently warranted interpretation and premise that excludes a proposed rival. The present results make that comparison more precise: they show what the weak representation proves, what it erases, and where additional evidence or argument can change the conclusion.
