### 10.16 The selected source argument and its interpretive conditions

The preceding distinctions can now be applied to the actual source argument selected by the received analysis. Its point is not merely that an abstract graph can be connected. The analysis reports a particular pattern of arguments in Ibn Taymiyya's commentary on al-Asfahani's creed, distinguishes those arguments from the creed's assertions, and identifies the additional co-reference premise under which they concern one subject. The resulting account has substantive source-relative content while retaining the separate burdens of interpretation and external truth. [Selected source argument, §§1–3 and 6–8][source-incidence]

#### Source strata and the eight selected supports

The received analysis locates the creed's predications at translation lines 68–95 and the commentary's endorsement and distinctions at 97–128. It reports further commentary at 481–548 and 1761–1816. The creed, the commentary's evaluation of an argument, the English rendering, and the subsequent formal abstraction therefore have different roles. An endorsement of the attributed package does not endorse every proposed proof of it. The source note describes the English text as a supplied 2024 translation based on two Arabic editions; it does not report verification against the Arabic or completed specialist confirmation. The exact translation is not newly received here. **The line numbers below are the received analysis's locators in that translation, not independently checked primary-text citations.** [Source custody and strata][source-incidence] [Selected source loci and ancestry][source-selected-loci]

There are ten selected coordinates: creation, specification, choice and command are ground or action coordinates; volition, knowledge, ability, life and speech are attribute coordinates; pure-perfection eligibility is a method condition. The last coordinate is not a tenth bearer or an additional divine attribute. The eight registered supports are as follows. The arrows describe the reported direction of an argument, subject to its interpretation and qualifications; the undirected supports used for connectivity discard that direction. [Selected typed graph][source-incidence] [Exact support registry][source-selected-model]

| Reported argument route | Reported translation locus | Qualification retained in the selected representation |
|---|---|---|
| Creation or engenderment to volition | 124; 500–502 | A commentary route concerning the relevant source, not an inference from any unexplained event to an arbitrary willing subject. |
| Volition to knowledge | 500–503 | The knowledge attribution belongs to the reconstructed source argument. |
| Specification to volition | 538–548 | Specification is retained as a separate ground or action coordinate. |
| Choice to ability | 523–530 | The source note presents this as the commentary's repair of the creed's compressed ability argument. |
| Knowledge together with ability to life | 534–536 | The registered premise is joint; neither knowledge nor ability is silently made sufficient on its own. |
| Command or legislation to speech | 124 | This is the legislative route. |
| Engenderment to speech | 124; the model registry gives 124–128 | This cosmological route is explicitly attributed to the majority of the Affirmation Folk; it is not reported as an unqualified consensus. |
| Creator relation and pure-perfection eligibility to a qualified attribute | 1761–1816 | The prose states a general guarded route; the selected support specializes it to creation, the eligibility condition and speech. |

The last row requires care. Its general source discussion includes hearing and sight as well as speech. The ten-coordinate registry nevertheless selects speech for this support; hearing and sight are not additional vertices in this graph. Moreover, using the creation coordinate in the support does not identify the full Creator relation with a bare event predicate. Applying the attributed rule still requires the relevant source relation and the eligibility conditions of section 10.15. The specialization is part of this selected abstraction, not a claim that the source discusses only speech. [Selected graph and exact source loci][source-incidence] [Source-locus note][source-selected-loci] [Exact support registry][source-selected-model]

**Connectivity of this registry.** Starting at volition, the first three supports reach creation, knowledge and specification. The joint knowledge–ability–life support reaches ability and life; choice is reached through ability. The cosmological speech support reaches speech from creation, and the legislative support reaches command from speech. The guarded support reaches the remaining method condition. These paths include every one of the ten coordinates, proving connectedness of the undirected support graph. Section 10.13 therefore applies to this concrete registry: every nontrivial partition of its coordinates is crossed by a selected support.

This is a representation-specific integration result. In particular, replacing a joint premise by the two edges of a graph does not license either single-premise inference. Nor are all supports indispensable to connectedness: deleting the cosmological speech support leaves creation connected to speech through the selected guarded support. The two routes still have different source premises and qualifications. Topological redundancy does not establish inferential interchangeability or permit transfer of one route's warrant to the other. The registry is neither asserted to be the source's complete argument nor a uniquely minimal representation of it.

#### What the accepted source interpretation adds

A positive source-relative derivation can be stated without asking graph connectedness to identify an individual. Suppose an independently interpreted source referent $`g`$ is the subject of the relevant creation, specification, choice and command claims. Suppose the reported argument rules have been correctly reconstructed, are accepted for this comparison, and preserve that subject through their applications. Creation gives volition; volition gives knowledge; choice gives ability; knowledge together with ability gives life; and command gives speech. Specification supplies a further route to volition. The cosmological route to speech is available under its distinct traditional premise, and the selected a-fortiori route is available under its distinct source and perfection guards. Thus the five selected attribute predicates apply to $`g`$ under these premises. This is an application of the fixed-subject argument in section 10.11, not an additional proof that the subject has been identified. [Positive source-relative construction][source-incidence]

The co-reference premise has its own reported textual basis. The received analysis reads the creed's necessary Creator, unity, knowledge, ability, life, volition, speech, hearing and sight as predications of one referent, and reads the opening commentary as affirming that package while allowing criticism of particular arguments. Accepting that correctly reconstructed co-reference excludes a model which assigns its intended predicates to distinct subjects. Accepting the substantive argument relations also excludes an otherwise identical description that merely collects labels on one bearer and omits every registered dependency. These are two different restrictions, with positive content of their own. Neither is obtained by counting vertices. [Textual co-reference and source-relative restriction, §6; positive construction, §8][source-incidence]

The plural construction in section 10.13 remains a control on the weak relational projection. It is not a model of an accepted same-subject proposition that it contradicts. Likewise, a finite automaton can realize a formal dependency pattern without its registers thereby becoming genuine knowledge, willing, first-person ownership, choice because an end is fitting, wisdom or theological speech. A claim that an impersonal mechanism realizes the full intended source predicates would require further semantic evidence; assigning their names to registers does not supply it. The source argument can consequently exclude these weak realizations at its own premises without converting the weak graph into a source-neutral proof of the richer predicates. [Source-relative integration and its controls, §§7–9][source-incidence]

#### Eight questions between a source record and an external conclusion

The received analysis distinguishes eight questions which should remain separate in assessing this application. They are not eight homogeneous observations, a numerical confidence score, or a universally necessary sequence for every possible argument. In particular, external truth is the target to be warranted, not an input which may be asserted to prove itself. [Source, formal and world coordinates, §2][source-incidence]

| Question | Its role in this application |
|---|---|
| Are the exact source bytes available? | Identifies the text actually examined. The original analysis reports a hashed translation; the present reconstruction has the analysis and its locators, not a fresh receipt of that translation. |
| Is the selected passage correctly delimited? | Establishes which words and context support the claim. A reported line range records a locator; checking it requires the corresponding text. |
| Is the translation adequate for this inference? | Concerns whether the relevant distinction survives translation. A connected graph cannot settle this question. |
| Is the claim attributed to the correct source stratum? | Separates the creed's statement, the commentator's endorsement or repair, and a position reported from another group. |
| Has the proposition been reconstructed correctly? | Concerns quantifier scope, subject binding, joint premises, modal force and qualifications. The support graph retains only part of this content. |
| Is the proposition accepted for this comparison? | Determines which substantive source premises the comparison admits. Formal satisfaction alone does not confer that acceptance or its warrant. |
| Do the selected predicates co-refer as claimed? | Supplies the relevant common subject within the interpreted source proposition. It cannot be replaced by a shared printed label. |
| Do that referent and those predicates obtain externally? | Requires the independent evidential or philosophical support appropriate to the actual-world conclusion. It does not follow from the preceding bookkeeping or from connectivity alone. |

If translation adequacy, attribution, reconstruction or applicability is unwarranted, the corresponding use of this particular source route is unwarranted. The absence of that warrant does not make the proposition false, destroy the mathematical connectivity of the registered supports, or defeat another independently supported route. Similarly, accepting a source for a bounded comparison is distinct from showing that its claims hold externally. This makes the deletion controls precise: removing one of the route's required justifications interrupts that inferential use, rather than proving a global impossibility of reaching its conclusion.

#### A declared editorial standard and an attested occurrence

The source-use distinctions have a bounded positive historical application. The admitted occurrence assessment reports that the selected divergent reading is present in the imaged 1911 volume of *The “Summa Theologica” of St. Thomas Aquinas*, Part I, First Number, QQ. I–XXVI (London: R. & T. Washbourne). It separately reports the introduction signed W. L. naming the Leonine edition as the translation's revision and correction standard. These are two different findings: an observed printed occurrence and a contemporaneous declared editorial relationship. The declaration is defeasible evidence of practice; it does not identify the actual Latin exemplar or the person and operation responsible for this reading. [N250A-248]

The source's facsimile locator is https://archive.org/details/summatheologi01thom. Its reported locations are title PDF 7, declaration printed lxxvii/PDF 81, signature printed lxxxvi/PDF 90 and selected locus printed 20/PDF 114. The imaged volume's 1911 date must not be replaced by the catalogue's series-level 1912 label, and “First Number” identifies the part/range rather than independently authenticating first-edition status. The retained report describes a 460-page, 32,318,098-byte PDF with SHA-256 14cdf5aa0035d8a551a4da4ae87e5a303d7146a4dd45354e92d3ab0dca10de83, four visual inspections and a separate source review of those images and PDF identity. These are the admitted report's historical inspection claims, not fresh receipt or authentication of the primary PDF here, human-specialist review or complete edition authentication. [N250A-248]

A date-bound occurrence can rule out a proposed later stage as the first introduction of a feature already present in 1911. It cannot choose among earlier production hypotheses. Agreement with another witness likewise does not prove borrowing, correction or deliberate selection, and an editorial standard does not establish universal occurrence-level conformity. No probability is assigned to the remaining hypotheses. An identified working exemplar, translator's note, correction list, annotated proof or contemporary erratum could discriminate the local production decision; another mirror of the same wording cannot. [N250A-248]

This improves an actual input at the boundary where earlier source-effect results already require adequate identity and interpretation. It does not use their conditional conclusions to certify their own source premises. Quoted source, translated occurrence, acquisition root and present assertion remain different objects. The finding does not force authorial attribution from an objection-role convention, infer endorsement by a current carrier, establish theological truth or numerical identity, or authenticate an original medieval utterance. The preceding occurrence and source-context owners retain their original credit and inspection limits; this bounded extension does not silently replace their earlier status. [N250A-248]

#### The exact limit of the criticized generic-necessity argument

The source analysis reports a particular criticism at translation lines 481–495: sharing the abstract predication of necessity, together with individuation, does not by itself establish the real constitution on which that proposed uniqueness proof relies. This is narrower than a rejection of every argument for a unique necessary source. [Textual co-reference and the criticized proof, §6; exact generic-unity control, §9][source-incidence]

An elementary interpretation isolates the missing step. Take distinct objects $`a,b`$, interpret a generic necessity-role predicate $`N`$ by $`N=\{a,b\}`$, and let differentiating predicates $`D_a,D_b`$ have extensions $`\{a\}`$ and $`\{b\}`$. Interpret the proper-constituent relation as empty. Both objects share the generic predication, and their individuating descriptions differ, while neither has a proper constituent. Thus those predicative facts alone do not entail composition or numerical identity. To rule out this interpretation, an argument needs an independently warranted bridge from the relevant kinds of predication and individuation to real constitution, or some other premise excluding plurality. Merely treating two descriptive aspects as two constituents assumes the missing bridge.

This interpretation proves a limited semantic non-entailment. It does not establish that two actual necessary sources exist or are metaphysically possible; $`N`$ records the generic role at issue, not a complete theory of intrinsic necessity. Sections 3–10.4 supply the chapter's stronger resource, necessity, efficacy and original-production premises. Those arguments must be assessed under those premises, which the simple interpretation neither realizes nor refutes. The source report's co-reference proposition likewise retains its source-relative force without borrowing the criticized generic proof.

### 10.17 Function, property interpretation and the personal-source comparison

The remaining proper-function adjudication distinguishes the fixing of a function from its ontology and its ultimate source. Its accounts of prevalence, causal contribution, selected effect, design, learned objective, truth-linked function, properly situated operation, original disposition, and primitive or holistic normative order are substantially treated in [Objective Normativity and Corrective Cognition, §§3–8](objective-normativity-and-corrective-cognition.md). Their tests should not be restarted as if those arguments were absent. Prevalence records what is common, successful optimization records achievement of a specified target, and a warranted epistemic function requires the further truth, environment and operation relations appropriate to its account. The stronger positive source argument in that work's §5.4 remains intact. [Function and ontology adjudication][function-ontology-note]

The adjudication's remaining ontology inventory comprises practice-relative norm descriptions, conceptual or nonpersonal intellectual grounding, immanent norm properties, powers or dispositions, property dualism, impersonal teleology and personal teleology. These are not seven mutually exclusive packages on a single axis. Some concern what realizes a norm or attribute, some concern the mental–physical relation, and some concern the nature of a purposive source. Section 10.14 explains why a thin incidence profile cannot decide omitted commitments. It does not certify every complete theory named by this inventory, establish that all combinations are possible, or assign them equal evidential support. A developed rival must state how its actual commitments jointly satisfy the comparison's independently warranted requirements. [Ontology inventory][function-ontology-note]

A stronger proposed comparison therefore deserves its exact scope. It holds fixed one local bearer and one intellectual or representational ground of the registered contents, common functional attribute incidence, a represented fittingness orientation, truth and target-authority registers, causal guidance, finite articulability, actuality and efficacy. It then asks whether de-se ownership, personality, selection because an end is fitting, wisdom and actual speech are fixed by that description. This proposal improves on a comparison that gives its rival only disconnected mechanisms: shared content and common incidence have been explicitly included. But an intellectual or representational ground must not be identified with a personal subject merely by terminology; nor does calling it nonpersonal demonstrate that its full intended semantics is coherent. [Strengthened intellectual-ground comparison][intellectual-comparison]

The received reissue states the common-structure construction as a sketch: keep a neutral relational structure fixed and give two expansions different personal-target predicates, subject to the proposed constraints. ### 10.18 Mental hosting, attributed agency and candidate denotation

The remaining source arguments distinguish an external order from a notion representing it, and both from the bearer in which the notion is realized. That distinction matters to the transition from intelligibility to an original intellect. The notional-hosting study reconstructs a conditional principle: if the relevant notional representation is present, some mental host is present. Its wider claim that universals subsist mentally is supplied principally through El-Tobgui's secondary reconstruction; the Asfahani translation supplies a narrower use within a unity argument. Neither source role may be silently promoted to an independently checked Arabic primary proposition or a neutral theory of every abstract object. [R359-AI]

Even granting that hosting principle, four further transitions remain distinct. The studied order must itself have the required intrinsic notional character, rather than merely be representable. The hosting must be constitutive of that order, rather than a downstream representation of it. The order's underivability must transfer to the relevant host. Finally, the constitutive host must be unique. The study names these H7a through H7d. They are explicit hard premises, not consequences obtained by assigning the same label to order, notion and mind.

The positive conditional has a transparent argument. Grant the underived input order, the notional-hosting principle and all four bridges. Intrinsic notionality and hosting supply a mental bearer; constitutive hosting gives the required relation to the order; the transfer premise gives its underivability; uniqueness gives exactly one such constitutive host. Removing a premise removes the corresponding step. The proof establishes what follows from the package. It is not additional evidence that representation constitutes the represented order or that the host is underived.

The strongest comparison therefore preserves external impersonal order together with dependent minds whose notions represent it. An underived truth can be known by a derived thinker. Multiple downstream representers can also coexist with one stipulated constitutive host. The latter uniqueness claim is not that there is only one mind. Nor does the formal host-role conclusion by itself establish consciousness, de se ownership, agency, wisdom or speech. If a defended philosophical account makes genuine intellectual apprehension essentially a subject's apprehension, that account supplies a further premise and cannot be refuted by a thin formal predicate deliberately lacking it. The affirmative intellectual and practical arguments in §12 and in [Objective Normativity and Corrective Cognition](objective-normativity-and-corrective-cognition.md) retain that richer scope.

Both primary editions report 8,192 valuations per declared class, 2,624 base models and 1,424 models in their broader full-bridge class; their separately restricted queries have their own denominators. In the revised query set, 224 of 512 notional-underived cases lack a constitutive host; 64 of 656 structural-underived cases lack a mental host; and 32 of 128 cases without the transfer premise lack the claimed underived host. Among 64 fully guarded query cases the exact host conclusion has no countermodel, but 16 lack the personal-subject predicate. The distinct three-host symbolic report retains satisfiable controls for downstream representation, nontransfer and multiple representers, and an unsatisfiable failure of the full guarded conclusion. These source-reported finite facts preserve the change from the earlier looser “intellect role” wording to the narrower constitutive-host conclusion. They establish no metaphysical possibility, explanatory parity or source truth. Its eight frozen-hash rows and nine source-anchor checks likewise remain historical custody statements, not new source verification here. [R359-AI]

#### What source co-reference can supply

The source-bundle study supplies a different positive premise: an accepted proposition can directly attribute its selected roles to one interpreted subject. For the finite six-role abstraction—creator, knowing, able, living, volitional and speaking—separate existential claims permit different witnesses. With $`B_q`$ the eligible bearers of role $`q`$, a common role bearer exists exactly when $`\bigcap_qB_q\ne\varnothing`$, by §10.11. Acceptance of a correctly reconstructed proposition applying all six roles to one $`g`$ supplies a witness in that intersection. This source-relative co-reference has substantive force; it is not derived merely from the roles' separate availability. [R359-AK]

The source strata remain distinguishable. The receipt attributes the creed sentence to its author and the endorsement to the commentary, using different reported translation loci. The English rendering and its note of two Arabic editions constitute translated-primary access, not a fresh critical verification of the Arabic. Translation adequacy and proposition reconstruction are prerequisites to the intended co-reference. Source acceptance, referent identity and world adequacy are additional questions. The commentary's affirmation of volition and speech also does not authorize unrestricted Divine Name status for *al-murīd* and *al-mutakallim*. Preserving the attribute does not require erasing the naming qualification.

At this scope, a distributed assignment with no common source-role bearer conflicts with the accepted co-reference. The formal comparison retains this uncertainty instead of using a modern personality label to settle the historical meaning of every attribute.

The historical three-bearer enumeration reports 117,649 nonempty role-set assignments: 12,097 have a common bearer and 105,552 do not. Its minimal control places speaking on one bearer while the other five roles occur on another. The 24,194 personal-false/personal-true expansions over common-bearer assignments show only the extra target's freedom in that neutral signature. The distinct three-bearer symbolic analysis keeps separate source and world predicates: a common source bundle can coexist with an empty world counterpart until the explicit identity/world bridge is supplied; the selected bundle then transfers. They do not close source-specialist review or settle which richer interpretation is correct. [R359-AK]

#### Source objects, admissible interpretations and external reference

The referent study makes the world bridge more precise. Let $`g`$ be a source-discourse object, $`W`$ a candidate-world domain and $`\mathcal H`$ a declared family of admissible source-to-world interpretations. The expression $`h(g)=w`$ is an interpretation or denotation relation between these roles, not an assertion of cross-sort numerical identity. Define the image fibre and the candidate-world role-bearer set by

```math
F_{\mathcal H}(g)=\{h(g):h\in\mathcal H\},\qquad
U_W=\{w\in W:w\text{ satisfies every selected translated role}\}.
```

If the source proposition gives the selected roles to $`g`$ and every admitted map preserves those positive roles, then $`F_{\mathcal H}(g)\subseteq U_W`$. When $`\mathcal H\ne\varnothing`$, this yields a candidate-world role bearer. Nonemptiness is doing existence work: a coherent source proposition alone does not establish an admissible world interpretation. Source bytes, passage, translation, attribution, reconstructed proposition, acceptance, role preservation, referent eligibility, version and world adequacy cannot be hidden inside an unexplained word “admissible.” [R359-AP]

Relative denotation is determinate exactly when $`|F_{\mathcal H}(g)|=1`$. If the family is also **role-complete**, meaning that every member of $`U_W`$ is the image of $`g`$ under an admitted map, then $`F_{\mathcal H}(g)=U_W`$. Under those hypotheses the relative uniqueness condition is equivalent to uniqueness of the candidate-world role bearer. Without role completeness, another structural constraint or external anchor may fix the image while several objects satisfy the role bundle. Such a restriction can be warranted, but its information comes from that further premise. Arbitrarily admitting only the map to a preferred object does not make the source roles select that object.

Positive-role preservation is also weaker than complete-profile preservation or reflection. The image can have unregistered features not constrained by the selected positive predicates. A complete source interpretation may need negative, intensional, modal or subject-binding content that this reduced map does not carry. Even unique denotation within every candidate world leaves the actual candidate world undecided. A change of translation, version or reconstructed role set can change both $`\mathcal H`$ and $`U_W`$; earlier denotation does not transfer merely because a filename or source label persists.

The primary referent receipt reports 512 world signatures, 169 nonempty interpretation families and 22 hidden-anchor witnesses. Its distinct injective-embedding analysis uses 256 signatures in four-object candidate worlds, 143 nonempty role-complete embedding cases, 1,144 independently restricted map families and 300 hidden-anchor witnesses, alongside 67 multiple-role-bearer signatures and a multiple-world control. Those denominators describe different constructions and remain distinct. Eight frozen-hash rows and nine translation-anchor checks are reported, with no new Arabic-primary or actual-world verification. The standard image-fibre argument therefore clarifies what a source interpretation can establish while leaving its authority and application premises assessable. It does not replace the stronger original-source argument with a merely formal denotation. [R359-AP]

<a id="r359-bz-realizer-selection"></a>

### 10.19 Eligible realizers and selection across isomorphic descriptions

An existence claim about realizers needs a nonempty domain and a precise account of what counts as eligible. For a required instance $`x`$, distinguish its applicability set $`\operatorname{App}(x)`$ from the efficacy witnesses available for an applicable candidate. A combined realization fibre can be written

```math
R(x)=\{(a,w):a\in\operatorname{App}(x),\ w\in\operatorname{Eff}(x,a)\}.
```

An empty applicability set and a nonempty applicability set with no efficacy witness both leave $`R(x)`$ empty, but for different reasons. A total choice of a realizer over a finite required instance set exists exactly when every required fibre is nonempty. An empty instance domain would make the universal assertion vacuous and establish no actual realized case. These distinctions prevent the formal success of a selection statement from being confused with a supplied productive resource. [R359BZ-I]

Natural selection under changes of description asks a stronger question. Fix one isomorphism class of finite structures. Suppose eligible realizers are transported along its isomorphisms, with identity and composition respected, and eligibility itself is preserved by that transport. At a representative structure $`M`$, its automorphism group acts on the eligible fibre. A natural choice over this class exists exactly when that fibre contains a point fixed by every automorphism.

For necessity, a natural choice at $`M`$ must be unchanged by every automorphism of $`M`$. For sufficiency, choose an eligible fixed point $`r`$ at $`M`$ and transport it to each isomorphic structure along any isomorphism. Two such isomorphisms differ by an automorphism of $`M`$; its fixing $`r`$ makes the transported choice independent of which isomorphism was used. Compatibility with further transport follows from composition. The proof concerns the specified transport and eligible fibre, not an unspecified notion of sameness. [R359BZ-I]

Nonemptiness alone is insufficient. Two eligible realizers interchanged by an automorphism form a nonempty fibre with no fixed point. Conversely, several eligible fixed points can yield several natural choices; existence does not imply uniqueness. A distinguished marker or additional eligible relation may remove a symmetry and supply a choice, but its warrant comes from that enrichment. A natural choice over one isomorphism class also does not provide a uniform formula over every model of an arbitrary theory, nor does it demonstrate a unique metaphysical source. Those stronger claims require the appropriate logical, semantic and world-application premises.

The retained source history records four repairs, including the nonempty-sort and uniformity distinctions. Its partition analysis reports 1,155 partitions, 16,067 fibres, 12,161 positive cases and 2,302 transitive cases. The distinct group method uses thirty-nine groups, 131 fibres, twelve transitive cases and 750 sampled cases. These populations describe different finite constructions; they are historical results, not new executions or a proof that actual productive eligibility has been authenticated. The source-to-world and underivability questions remain the ones stated in §10.18 and in the earlier positive adequacy argument. [R359BZ-I]

<a id="r359-bz-lineage-root"></a>

### 10.20 A common upstream lineage and what it does not supply

There is a separate finite graph criterion for a common upstream source. Let $`G=(V,E)`$ be a finite nonempty directed acyclic graph, with an edge directed from an upstream contributor towards a downstream vertex. Reachability includes the length-zero path. Call the graph upstream-directed when every pair of vertices has a common ancestor. The following are equivalent: upstream directedness; exactly one vertex of indegree zero; and a vertex from which every vertex is reachable. [R359BZ-J]

Every vertex in a finite DAG has an indegree-zero ancestor: repeatedly follow an incoming edge backwards; finiteness and acyclicity force the process to terminate. If the root is unique, each of these ancestor paths begins there, so it reaches every vertex. A vertex reaching every vertex is a common ancestor for every pair. Finally, if two distinct roots existed in an upstream-directed graph, their common ancestor would have to equal each root, because a root admits no nontrivial incoming path. Thus they could not be distinct. This establishes the equivalence under the stated hypotheses.

The direction and boundary conditions are essential. Two upstream branches can merge at one downstream vertex without sharing an upstream root. A directed cycle can supply common ancestors through cyclic reachability while having no indegree-zero vertex. An infinite chain can also have a common ancestor for every finite pair without having a first root. The finite nonempty DAG contract excludes these cases; suppressing those hypotheses would change the result.

This is a lineage theorem. Reaching every vertex does not by itself show that one root is the completely adequate productive source of every effect. The edge registry must represent the relevant relation in the same respect, include the contributors required by the claim, use an appropriate bearer granularity and justify closure against omitted external sources. A path of influence is not automatically a path of complete adequacy. The local adequacy and propagation premises in §§10.1–10.4 supply a different kind of argument when their conditions hold.

A common lineage also need not identify the bearer of every attribute attributed along it. Distribution, mediation and co-instantiation remain separate questions. The finite graph can organize a proposed common-source explanation and make an omitted contributor or merger visible. It cannot establish the interpretation of an edge, the source's intrinsic necessity, its personal ownership, or actual-world uniqueness solely from the root count.

The source reports 33,867 primary DAG cases, including 10,106 cases satisfying its root criterion. The distinct record uses 4,165 graphs: 572 acyclic and 3,593 cyclic, with 2,426 rootless upstream controls, together with 50,000 sampled cases. The cyclic controls test the stated boundary rather than refuting the finite DAG theorem. These are historical source-reported checks. No graph enumeration was run here, and no new general graph-theorem origin is claimed. [R359BZ-J]



A unique root is fixed by every automorphism of the registered graph, since an automorphism preserves indegree zero and hence must preserve its sole witness. This invariant identification remains identification of the graph vertex. For the separately guarded productive corollary, compositional sufficiency, effect coverage, root concreteness and closure against external contributors must hold in the intended interpretation. Completeness of the vertex list alone does not establish completeness of the edge relation. A root with a downstream contributor requiring an unregistered second input, or a root vertex denoting a distributed collective, illustrates why those extra premises cannot be inferred from the finite graph equivalence. [BZ-J01] [BZ-J03] [BZ-J04] [BZ-J05]

### 10.21 Common formal models and the burden of a richer interpretation

The impersonal comparison must preserve the neutral constraints it is offered to explain, while also respecting what a formal interpretation can establish. The C record illustrates both requirements. Its earlier PASS concerned a declaration about conclusions; it was not by itself evidence that a false-valued predicate had the intended rich interpretation. The audit identified an under-typed Creator predicate and a functional claim that had been asserted without an instantiated model. Those findings remain part of the source history rather than disappearing behind the successful label. [R359BZ-C]

The revised construction uses a two-world constant-domain interpretation in which the named objects $`o`$ and $`x`$ are present throughout the two worlds. Their necessary existence is a fact stipulated in that finite interpretation. It does not make every relation involving them necessary, determine an actual world, or establish a complete theory of original productive adequacy. Likewise, an empty extension for a registered Creator predicate says what is false under that predicate's specified interpretation. Applying the result to a richer account of creatorhood requires its typing, definition and complete premises; the mere possibility of writing an empty predicate does not provide that account.

The retained neutral-profile and common-bearer controls therefore have a conditional force. If two admitted interpretations preserve the complete neutral constraints but differ on an additional personal or source target, those constraints do not entail that target within the declared class. This is the exact profile principle of §10.14. A rich source or philosophical premise can legitimately restrict that class, but it must be stated and warranted. Conversely, a formal impersonal expansion must not be rejected merely because it lacks a target that was never entailed by the weaker premises. The comparison neither establishes equal explanatory merit nor demonstrates that every thin-signature interpretation is metaphysically realizable.

The R construction makes the shared core more substantial. It links the multi-output coupling described in Objective Normativity §8.18, an exact potential, the finite content transports of §4.6 in that work, and the complete boundary law of its §8.19. Those relations constrain the combined interpretation together. Their input identifications and compatibility are part of the construction; separate success of several components would not, without those links, establish that they form one model. The result remains a selected formal union rather than a proof that every neutral result in the corpus has been jointly realized. [R359BZ-R]

The common-bearer arithmetic is exact and illustrates a further distinction. With four eligible bearers and three independently selected nonempty role sets, there are $`(2^4-1)^3=3,375`$ assignments. For a given bearer to have all three roles, each role set must include it, leaving $`2^3=8`$ possibilities per role. Inclusion–exclusion over the four possible common bearers gives

```math
4\cdot8^3-\binom42 4^3+\binom43 2^3-1=1,695.
```

The remaining 1,680 assignments have each role available but no bearer common to all three. If empty role sets are allowed, the unrestricted three-set count is instead $`16^3=4,096`$. These domains must not be conflated. The calculation identifies a common witness for the formal role sets; it does not interpret those roles as full Divine Knowledge, Will or Power, or prove that their conjunction amounts to personal agency. [R359BZ-R]

Necessity, externality, source acceptance and the additional $`N`$ expansion in the record also retain their separate status. They are stipulated conditions or interpreted coordinates of the finite model. A neutral comparison that does not accept a source contract has not refuted that source's accepted predication; accepting the contract changes its premises. A Boolean role proxy is also insufficient to certify a stronger account's actual semantics. The source's false flag, separately varied extension and eight repair findings remain visible under these distinctions.

The positive result is a more demanding formal rival than a disconnected list of functions: a single admissible structure can carry the selected coupling, potential, transport and boundary relations while leaving the further target underdetermined. The remaining philosophical comparison concerns the warrant for that structure's interpretation, its explanatory stopping points, and the substantive bridges that would select or exclude it. It is not resolved by assigning a favorable name to one carrier, by asserting that the formal model is actual, or by treating a source-relative premise as if it had been derived from the neutral core. The affirmative productive, cognitive and practical arguments elsewhere in this work continue at their own premises. [R359BZ-C; R359BZ-R]



The exact C structured record names the nine empty target extensions as agency, creatorhood, intellect, personality, revelational identification, actual speech, speech capacity, unified common bearer and wisdom. That explicit list is stronger evidence about the stipulated interpretation than the V1 field merely saying that conclusions were withheld. It still does not prove that the predicates capture every richer philosophical definition. The selected records report their original model and checks; reproducing those reports here is not a new execution or an independent verification of all the original model-owner bytes. ### 10.22 Granting one bearer leaves further predicates to establish

The common-model argument in §10.21 leaves several transitions open. A stronger structural grant can isolate what remains after numerical co-location is conceded: suppose the declared neutral model assigns its structural roles to one bearer. That grant removes one specific multiplicity objection within the model. It does not by itself show that the roles share a derivation, reduce to one primitive or explain their own coordination. A single carrier can hold several unexplained primitive relations. The later one-bearer audit uses this stronger grant to locate the remaining bridges, while retaining the rival's explanatory burden. [R44-BG01] [R44-BG03]

The underlying logical argument is elementary but conditional on a precise model class. Let a reduct retain all the registered neutral structure and let $`P`$ be a proposed further predicate. If two admissible expansions agree on that entire reduct and disagree on $`P`$, no sentence about that reduct which is true of both can entail $`P`$ over a class admitting both expansions. The expansion in which $`P`$ is false is a countermodel. This is the usual reduct/expansion test for nondefinability or nonentailment, not a new general theorem. Its force depends on preserving every premise actually used by the proposed argument. If an argument already assumes actual understanding, for example, an expansion withholding understanding is not a countermodel to that richer argument merely because it matches a weaker register. [R44-BG01]

The declared neutral coordinates also require careful interpretation. Existence at two indices establishes persistence in that finite frame. An external-actuality status becomes a claim of modelled causal efficacy only through participation in the stipulated effect relation; it does not supply a general criterion of concreteness. Truth-labelled contents and an interpretation table are primitive semantic coordinates, not actual knowledge or intentional apprehension. A supplied target key and fitting-action set do not explain their authority or yield proper function. One bearer's faithful token production does not establish an intention to speak, speech capacity, an occurrent act of Speech, authorization of a Name or revealed content. The audit's eleven repairs preserve these distinctions rather than claiming that the rival explains the omitted notions. [R44-BG01] [R44-BG03]

The same discipline applies to an originator predicate. The source's scoped `CreatorClass` includes at least agentive, intentional origination under its declared bridge; it is not a synonym for an actualizer. An apparent countermodel obtained merely by changing an arbitrary name would not address that substantive target. Conversely, a finite effect relation alone does not supply the agency and intention required by the scoped predicate. Source-functional compatibility under one candidate interpretation likewise neither authenticates the source nor selects the actual world. The source-relative personal and Speech predicates retain their separate evidence requirements. [R44-BG01] [R44-BG03]

### 10.23 Local occurrences and a persisting root bearer

The transport and holonomy arguments of §§10.5–10.8 distinguish a coherent section from a globally identical bearer. The later modal-root reconciliation makes that distinction explicit in the types of its variables. Let $`W`$ be a declared finite frame, $`G`$ a global bearer sort, and $`O_w`$ a local occurrence sort for each $`w\in W`$. An occurrence-to-bearer map $`\beta_w:O_w\to G`$ specifies the chosen numerical-identity semantics. Local existence, root role, underivability and concreteness are separate predicates on $`O_w`$. An abstract order, if present, belongs to its own sort; it is not automatically a local concrete occurrence. [R44-BK01] [R44-BK03]

A scoped sufficient package can now be stated without mixing domains. Suppose a selected occurrence $`o_w\in O_w`$ exists at every world, satisfies the root, underivability and concreteness conditions there, and obeys

```math
\beta_w(o_w)=g
\quad\text{for one }g\in G\text{ and every }w\in W.
```

Then that one bearer has a concrete, underived root occurrence at every index of the declared frame. The proof is direct: for each index the supplied occurrence witnesses the stated predicates of the same $`g`$. If transport maps are part of the certification, one can additionally require that they carry the selected occurrences coherently. Their coherence certifies a selected lineage; the displayed identity condition is what identifies that lineage with one numerical bearer. It is a substantive bridge in this semantics, not an equality convention obtained for free from a constant-domain notation. [R44-BK01] [R44-BK03]

The conditions cannot be collapsed into worldwise existence. With two worlds, choose a root occurrence in each and a coherent transport between them, but let their global labels be $`g_0\ne g_1`$. Worldwise root coverage and a coherent counterpart lineage hold, while no common numerical bearer is supplied by those facts. This exhibits the distinction between $`\forall w\,\exists g`$ and $`\exists g\,\forall w`$ without denying that an additional identity theory could link the occurrences. Likewise, a root at the designated actual index need not have a root occurrence at another index. An abstract ordering structure supplies no concrete occurrence merely by satisfying order axioms. These are separate failures of identity, coverage and concrete exemplification. [R44-BK01] [R44-BK02]

Even the full package proves only frame-relative persistence. Extending the frame with a world lacking such an occurrence invalidates that conclusion over the larger frame. Absolute metaphysical necessity would require independently warranted modal semantics and the intended scope of worlds. Underivability also remains relative to the stipulated grounding graph: having no predecessor in that graph does not by itself establish aseity or nonborrowed actuality. The package is sufficient under its declared semantics; the source's deletion models do not prove that it is globally minimal across all possible semantics. Once identity is supplied directly, some transport conditions may instead function as certification guards. [R44-BK01] [R44-BK03]

A positive, relation-relative bridge is nevertheless available when the missing coverage premise is supplied. On one stated domain, distinguish the intended grounding relation $`G_w(y,x)`$ from its recorded representation $`R_w(y,x)`$. Suppose $`x`$ exists, no $`R_w(y,x)`$ holds, and the representation is **incoming-complete at this target**:

```math
\forall y\;\bigl(G_w(y,x)\Rightarrow R_w(y,x)\bigr).
```

Then no $`G_w(y,x)`$ holds: any intended ground would have been recorded, contradicting the recorded-root premise. Thus $`x`$ exists without an incoming ground **in that intended relation and domain**. The converse soundness condition $`R_w(y,x)\Rightarrow G_w(y,x)`$ is not needed for this implication. If the guard holds for each selected occurrence above and the occurrence-to-bearer interpretation transfers this property to $`g`$, the conclusion holds for that bearer throughout the declared frame. This is the source's elementary positive completeness lemma, not merely an ancestry warning. [SB-INCOMING-COMPLETE]

Soundness alone would not suffice. Let $`x`$ exist and have an intended ground $`y`$, while the recorded relation is empty. Then $`x`$ is a recorded root and the representation is sound, but $`x`$ is not nonborrowed. Incoming completeness excludes precisely this hidden-ground case. [SB-INCOMING-COMPLETE]

The coverage premise must itself be defended independently: specifying an edge-admission criterion and its domain is not evidence that no relevant ground was omitted. Nor may the domain be restricted just to preserve the desired root. Calling the relation-relative conclusion metaphysical self-subsistence still requires the intended grounding semantics; extending it to every relevant possibility requires modal adequacy. These are separate obligations, not consequences of the lemma or substitutes for the stronger source and actuality arguments developed elsewhere in this work. [SB-INCOMING-COMPLETE]

The historical implementation defects reinforce the typing issue. The first checker tested existence and underivability while omitting the separately declared root-role predicate. It also handled a constant-domain special case, which could not establish a claim about independent local occurrences and transport. The repair separated all four predicates and restricted that checker to regression evidence. The distinct review then used local occurrences with independently assigned global labels. These are recorded changes in the tested contract, not new computations performed here. [R44-BK01] [R44-BK03]

### 10.24 Whole-model preservation and the exact bearer boundary

The finite incidence and neutral-profile controls above can be complemented by a language-wide construction from the modal supplement. Let $\mathfrak A$ be a nonempty world-local many-sorted structure for the declared states, actors, records, observations, actions and histories. Its relations can include objective correctness, reference norms, semantic relations and deterministic or stochastic transitions. Hold their interpretation fixed; correctness is not defined as whatever an actor endorses.

At each of at least two worlds $w$, replace a concrete local carrier $d$ by a tagged copy $(w,d)$, existing only at that world. Transport each local relation and operation through the tagging bijection. Abstract mathematical values may retain a separate sort; this does not make their physical carriers necessary.

Every world-local sentence with quantifiers restricted to locally existing carriers has its old truth value. Atomic formulas are preserved by construction; Boolean connectives preserve the induction hypothesis; local quantifiers are preserved by the bijection. A shared-carrier bundle with the same local structures and modal frame therefore also agrees on Boolean and modal combinations of **closed local sentences**. Nevertheless, no tagged concrete bearer exists at every world.

The restriction is exact. A de re formula holding one individual fixed across modal operators, an essential-ownership clause, or a premise already asserting one necessary concrete entity is not covered by this preservation argument. Operational prediction, complete local histories and strategic payoffs can remain unchanged while cross-world bearer identity changes. A representation's tensor dimension cannot close a distinction its language does not express.

A second expansion makes the comparison stronger. Keep the old local sorts and relations, and add a separate outer concrete bearer $g$ existing in every world. In a new typed existential-dependence relation, put $g$ before every locally existing copied carrier, and put no edge into $g$. The union of possible dependence edges is a well-founded star. Every copied contingent carrier has a predecessor; $g$ is necessary and uniformly underived. Assign it the stipulated order-and-efficacy roles while withholding mentality. The original local theory is still preserved because its sorts were not enlarged and its relations were not replaced.

This expansion satisfies the specified structural necessary-root premises without forcing mentality. It is not a model of a richer theory that already warrants an intellectual-adequacy premise. Nor does an uninterpreted dependence edge establish that an impersonal source genuinely explains objective reason-responsiveness. The result distinguishes formal nonentailment, metaphysical possibility and explanatory adequacy; it does not equate them or displace the positive cognitive arguments in §12.

The source illustrates the boundary by three models with the same binary operational core, keep/flip actions, fixed truth predicate and exact local histories. Separate roots in the two worlds satisfy local foundation but fail contingent-root dependence. A shared impersonal root satisfies the strengthened structural foundation premises but withholds mentality. A personal version can add knowledge and contingent willing without forcing every effect to occur necessarily. These are separately interpreted models, not a proof selecting the personal model by stipulation or authenticating any source record carried in the operational core.

The common-root inference also has an infinite extension. In a nonempty well-founded complete dependence domain, upstream directedness—every two members have a common ancestor—implies a unique root and a root ancestor for every member. Each member's ancestor set has a minimal element; transitivity of ancestry makes it a genuine root. Two roots' common ancestor must equal each, so they coincide. Conversely, a universal root supplies a common ancestor. This extends the finite DAG argument in §10.20 without eliminating its interpretation requirements: ancestry is not complete productive sufficiency, and a vertex may denote a collective rather than one simple subject.

The incidence obstruction in §10.11 likewise has arbitrary order. For $n\ge2$ roles, give bearer $b_i$ every role except role $i$. Every proper role subfamily has a common bearer, but the whole family has none—even if each bearer necessarily exists. A positive compactness route needs a compact eligible-bearer space, closed role sets and the finite-intersection property over an exhaustive interpreted domain. These are additional premises, not consequences of a large incidence matrix.

Finally, suppose two or more agents independently choose desired outcomes in the same set $Y$ with at least two possibilities, and each is required to be completely efficacious on the single final outcome. A joint profile can satisfy all those demands exactly when every selected outcome agrees. Independent unrestricted choices include off-diagonal profiles, so they cannot guarantee simultaneous complete efficacy. This excludes that precise rival-sovereignty package. It does not refute necessarily concordant wills, separate effect domains or a common coordinating ground; agreement or correlated equilibrium alone does not establish one mind.

## 11. What a complete explanatory fact does—and does not—establish

Generic explanation provides independent logical comparisons. It must not silently replace productive provision or identify explanatory facts with individual bearers. The following results reconstruct the relevant explanatory principles of Koons and Pruss and the corpus's checked consequences and controls. They concern explicit relational assumptions; neither the proofs nor their counterinterpretations authenticate a metaphysical realization. [Koons and Pruss, §2][u-kp] [Plural-explanation analysis][u-psr]

#### Epistemic warrant for an explanatory principle

The relational proofs below answer what follows from specified explanatory premises. A separate question is why those premises should be accepted. The positive epistemic case begins with a real distinction: a belief that merely happens to match its object is not thereby formed through an appropriate truth-connected route. Vividness does not repair a broken route, and an invented reassuring probability does not establish its reliability. Section 2.1's causal intelligibility argument therefore retains its force. Yet an operative local route, an explanation of its background and a common external explanation of every plurality of basic natural facts are different claims. Their connection requires argument. [Epistemic warrant and explanatory scope, result and §§1–2][epistemic-psr-assessment]

Three arguments must be distinguished. Pruss's compressed epistemological discussion connects unexplained perceptions, objective probability and skepticism, while allowing apparent self-evidence to provide basic warrant even when reporting it does not persuade a dissenter. Disagreement alone is not defeat. Koons's 1997 argument instead uses empirical success to support a defeasible causal default and appeals to the provenance of traces, memories, records and future states; its causation need not necessitate the effect. Its further fact-to-being assumptions, teleological characterization, fact-individuation replies to regress and induction-based criticism of cosmological proliferation belong to that developed case, not to an exceptionless deduction from local cognition. Koons and Pruss's 2020/2021 argument has a more specific central target: our ability to know that we possess empirical knowledge, under a principle governing pluralities of basic natural facts. These positions cannot be evaluated as one claim that a single unexplained item immediately defeats every empirical belief. [Epistemic assessment, §1][epistemic-psr-assessment] [Same-manuscript completion, assessment update][epistemic-psr-completion] [Koons and Pruss][u-kp]

The stronger argument can be reconstructed through seven distinguishable commitments. This is an analysis of their dependence, not seven independent objections or an attribution of the present formulation verbatim to the authors.

1. **Local connection.** Empirical knowledge needs appropriate truth-connected grounds, including the relevant causal or modal connection. A coincidentally true appearance does not supply it.
2. **Relevant counterpossibility.** Failure of the restricted explanatory principle in an epistemically accessible scenario permits uncaused appearances or intermediary links in worlds relevant to the cognitive episode. Moving from an exception somewhere to such a local possibility, and then to its epistemic relevance, is substantive.
3. **Robust scope.** A priori assurance cannot arbitrarily privilege these particular data. The proposed class principle and its coverage of data and intermediary links must be robust and a priori knowable. The authors defend basic natural facts against several narrower restrictions.
4. **Chance.** Objective chances require an explanatorily prior basis. A genuinely unexplained event cannot simply be assigned a benign propensity, stable frequency or reassuring prior. Even a relevant frequency would concern belief-producing events, rather than events counted indiscriminately.
5. **Defeat.** The admitted errors must threaten the actual method: sufficiently close for a safety account, or incompatible with determinately high reliability for the probabilistic account at issue. Mere describability is not this relation.
6. **Epistemic access.** Knowing that we know requires excluding the bad modal scenarios. The authors argue that empirical support cannot independently certify the prerequisite of all empirical support, motivating an a priori route. This is not simply unrestricted knowledge-of-knowledge, or KK.
7. **Plural scope and realization.** The principle supplies an explanation external to each admitted plurality of basic natural facts, including their totality. A further particular-explanans assumption enters the supernatural conclusion. Those fact-class and ontology assumptions are stronger than an appropriate cause for one datum. [Epistemic assessment, §2, reconstructing the article's §§2–6 and 9–10][epistemic-psr-assessment]

The two-dimensional setting explains why first-order success does not settle the sixth commitment. An epistemic scenario represents a complete modal reality, containing its own actual and possible worlds. A belief can be safe in the actual scenario's local neighborhood without the knower being entitled to exclude another epistemically accessible scenario in which deceptive counterparts are close. Actual first-order knowledge, warranted confidence that one knows and knowledge that one knows must not be identified. The local construction below does not establish the latter two by checking a conditional inside one scenario. [Epistemic assessment, §2][epistemic-psr-assessment]

The *Darʾ* 8 study adds a complementary distinction between **a sound argument, a person's acquisition of knowledge, and a universally indispensable route to knowledge**. Its opening records Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Baṣrī's long attestation-and-attributes chain as a quoted proposal whose indispensability Ibn Taymiyya challenges, not as the latter's own required sequence. Reasoning may become necessary for someone who cannot otherwise meet the relevant epistemic duty without being the same first step for everyone. Rational grounds taught in a book remain assessable as rational grounds; the testimonial medium does not by itself turn their force into an appeal to authority. Neither does it authenticate the book's claimed divine authorship. [F250-C111] [F250-C178]

The closing source distinctions are equally precise: knowing an object, knowing that one knows it, and correctly identifying how the knowledge arose are separate. A later proof can articulate, confirm or restore earlier recognition without having produced it; an agent can misattribute genuine knowledge to a defective argument. The positive *fiṭra* account is not articulated neonatal omniscience. The recorded P1591–P1611 discussion distinguishes directional capacity, recipient aptitude, auxiliary teaching, removal of impediments and sufficient present conditions. The author's affirmation of actual Creator-directed recognition is stronger than the modern appraisal's independently supported claim that relatively basic recognition can be epistemically legitimate. Neither the study nor this distinction supplies a population-wide empirical validation or a diagnosis of every dissenter. A formal dependency graph therefore remains a map of its argument, not an automatic history of every warranted mind. [F250-C111] [F250-C178]

The same record distinguishes a semantic connection from its existential application. That an action has an agent does not, by the relation alone, establish that the observed transition is such a made action: the latter premise needs its own ground (P0199–P0200 and P0240–P0243). Nor does agreement on a conclusion establish agreement on one theorist's supposedly indispensable proof of it (P0244–P0258). In collective inference the ground must apply to the whole, rather than merely to each member; each token's beginning does not by itself give a succession its first token. These controls do not reject rational proof or all aggregation. They specify why a sound positive conclusion, a sound proof, a correct exegesis and the only possible route remain different achievements. [F250-C111]
