<a id="foundation250-b-ends-and-rights"></a>

**Final explanation, fitting desire and rights.** The sixth collection's positive teleology adds content to practical integrity. It distinguishes an action's originating cognition and power from the good sought through it; a fit end needs a reason for being worthy of desire rather than acquiring its warrant solely from the desire it is meant to explain. Unrestricted pursuit of conflicting wants can defeat durable welfare, and an efficient common order need not be a good order merely because it works. The text appeals to healthy disposition, experienced rest in divine remembrance, rational comparison and scriptural orientation together. Its account preserves knowledge, mercy and power as real components of flourishing while rejecting their reduction to detached abstract cognition or their treatment as substitutes for an appropriate ultimate object. These are substantive reasons and experiences offered in support of the final-end argument. [F250B185, E113–134][F250B185] [F250B147, E145–174][F250B147] [F250B173]

Three further bridges must stay visible. A transient good's inability to secure complete enduring welfare does not, from its later cessation alone, prove that it has no noninstrumental value. An objectively fitting prospective end need not, just by being fitting, already exist externally: the examples of Mecca before pilgrimage and a beloved before contact support one object/attainment structure, not every possible goal. And the universal derivation of motion from volition depends on the source's forced/natural/voluntary classification and its account of natural motion as restoration. These qualifications preserve the positive demand for nonarbitrary ends without turning it into an unexplained consequence of necessary existence. The source acknowledges the need for further clarification at E163 and later describes the argument as newly clarified at E203; that authorial assessment does not itself settle the bridge premises. [F250B147, E162–177 and E199–203][F250B147] [F250B173, §3][F250B173]

The intended conclusion is also normative, not a prediction that misdirected desire never occurs. Creatures can pursue a corrupt end, sincerely mistake a means, or enjoy an immediate good without intending its wider wisdom. A dependent human still acts and benefits genuinely. Universal willing of occurrences is therefore distinct from normative love and approval; a beloved local possibility may be omitted for an outweighing reason. The reciprocal-love discussion criticizes an allegedly complete ultimate orientation, not the psychological possibility of mutual affection. Neither this distinction nor its human examples supplies a divine-lying exception or settles the all-context veracity premise of §12.11. [F250B185, E021–032 and E061–072][F250B185] [F250B147, E187–202][F250B147]

The ethical context further prevents collapsing right into experienced injury. Proportionate treatment is owed even to a wrongdoer; sincere error can excuse a person without authorizing imitation; justice between other claimants differs from relinquishing one's own right. In the later right-and-harm discussion, a badly fitted artifact can fail its due function without itself feeling pain, an attempted wrong can fail to achieve its harm, and later benefit need not make an earlier wrong just. These comparisons support a category of violated right beyond felt harm. Applying that category to a self-sufficient divine bearer still needs the source's theological account of what is due; the artifact analogy alone does not prove it. Divine invulnerability and real love, approval and joy are jointly affirmed, and the received discussion's final sentence remains incomplete. Historical sectarian allegations and political narratives receive no certification from these local ethical merits. [F250B185, E033–046][F250B185] [F250B147, E237–251 and printed 248–252][F250B147] [F250B173]

**Practical classifications as controls on the analogy.** The later legal pieces sharpen the distinctions without becoming new metaphysical proofs. Equal reward credited to a prevented person's intention is not identity of performed action or an independent permission to omit a condition. Intending to “join” prayers cannot make a legally unavailable time available. Two departures from an ordinary form are not automatically worse than one: the source of a permitted substitute and the nature of the remaining prohibition matter. A condition's actually obtaining differs from a purchaser's direct knowledge that it obtains; a presumption of regularity does not abolish a known contrary condition. Paired terms can overlap when used alone and distinguish contributions when conjoined. These historical examples constrain transfers of “perfection,” “cause,” “independence” and “same result” across domains. They supply no contemporary legal advice. [F250B023, T10–T14][F250B023] [F250B119] [F250B213, legal cross-checks][F250B213]

The commercial examples test a classification by productive duties, entitlement and risk rather than by its label. A lease valid at formation can later end when its specified subject or entitlement ends. A sale of future produce, a lease under which the taker cultivates, and a partnership sharing realized yield allocate work and loss differently. Bodily labour and assets can make distinct contributions without identical powers or intentions; consumed seed is not returned capital. The relevant ability is ability to obtain the intended benefit, while negligent delay after that ability differs from innocent failure before it. Ordinary risk is managed rather than simply declared nonexistent. These are useful checks against inferring permanent availability from initial validity or identical agency from shared benefit. The source's awkward short contribution formula is not repaired, and its explicit copyist abridgment prevents representing the transmitted orchard answer as a complete original argument. [F250B112, T17–T18][F250B112] [F250B131, orthogonal material][F250B131]

#### Value, voluntary conditions and the scope of wise purposes

The connected studies give the positive wisdom account more structure than an appeal to an unspecified hidden end. The middle *Miftāḥ* discussion distinguishes an act's value, its agent's culpability, and the conditions for punishment after communicated proof. Calling an act intrinsically good or bad need not mean that its causal or normative character is invariant under every change of recipient, time or circumstance. The discussion culminating at main 1009–1012 distinguishes good arising from a command, from the act's own character, from both, and from a fitting resolve whose execution is not required. These are different grounds of evaluation, not four interchangeable declarations that every commanded event has an independently fixed character. *Darʾ* 8 and 9 likewise distinguish rational recognition of value from the additional message, maturity and opportunity conditions disputed in accounts of obligation and punishment. The historical rulings in those discussions are not present legal recommendations. [F250-C047] [F250-C111] [F250-C121]

Necessity through complete voluntary grounds is distinguished from coercion in *Miftāḥ* 921–922. Its rejection of the claim that choice must include every contrary at 1243 coexists with a positive affirmation of true created action, acquisition and choice at 1512–1515. *Minhāj* separates intrinsic impossibility from an act's foreknown nonperformance: the person can retain actionable capacity although the contrary occurrence is not compatible with all the actual foreknowledge facts held fixed. These accounts therefore do not identify free agency with independent self-origination, or infer actual alternative occurrence from a bare capacity. Nor do they settle every responsibility question merely by naming the will a cause. [F250-C020] [F250-C047] [F250-C115] [F250-C157] [F250-C159]

Attribution is equally important. Creating an act in a human bearer is not performing that act in the human respect; creating a color does not color the source, and enabling a false speaker does not make the speech source-owned. *Minhāj* V02L0185–0195 and *Miftāḥ* 1103–1141 retain real subordinate action and distinguish just reward from wages owed to an employer's benefactor: the source also supplies the capacities by which the rewarded act occurs. At 501–502 the human act is a real component of a joint downstream cause, while moral attribution is described as proportionate. This is not an independently specified numerical causal-credit calculus. These distinctions block a false identity of acts without by themselves exhausting responsibility for enabling another's harmful action. [F250-C047] [F250-C159] [F250-C190]

Explaining a motive does not settle an act's value. In the middle *Miftāḥ* debate, the same bearer may produce contrary effects under different conditions, and psychological explanation is compatible with a further judgment about their worth. Wise optional means can themselves be benefits even where the source could achieve the final result otherwise. *Minhāj* V02L0253–0283 supplies a related qualification: correction and repentance may deepen humility and care, but do not authorize deliberately doing wrong to obtain those benefits. Not every penitent is thereby better than every never-offender. A remedial good, permission for its occasion and a universal ranking rule remain separate. [F250-C047] [F250-C159]

The source's response to suffering also has a definite boundary. Explaining some consequences of a selected embodied mode does not establish that selecting that mode was necessary, or justify every actual injury and quantity of pain. Beneficial interdependence among bodily capacities, environments and human practices can illustrate coordinated provision without making their inherited biology true. The final *Miftāḥ* discussion permits leaving a harmful dwelling for a beneficial alternative and affirms prevention and treatment through real causes; reliance is not the abandonment of available means. Its medical mechanisms and social generalizations remain attributed historical claims, not health advice or judgments about victims. [F250-C047] [F250-C115] [F250-C157]

Finally, efficiently willing an event and intending a beloved end are different relations. At 1164–1165 an enduring object of final intention need not be an object the intending agent produces. The termination of a means-series, the need for an enduring ultimate end, and identifying that end with God are distinct premises; the incomplete promised treatment cannot silently supply all of them. This preserves the affirmative account of knowledge, worship, justice and beneficence as positive goods, while leaving exact application and ultimate-end arguments open where the received treatment does. [F250-C047] [F250-C157]

### 12.11 Disclosure, truthfulness and authenticated reception

An intelligible world supplies material for inquiry. An intentional disclosure additionally involves an author addressing a recipient through meaningful signs. A natural indication need not be an assertion; a knower can remain silent; a capable speaker can utter a falsehood. These distinctions identify separate positive tasks rather than imposing a general prohibition on an argument to divine disclosure. Disclosure capability here means the ability to make the true content available through recognizable address; actual warranted uptake remains a further recipient condition.

**Constructive disclosure-capability proposition.** Fix a truth p and an eligible prospective recipient. Suppose the source jointly has the following capacities in one realizable situation: adequate knowledge of p and of the relevant signs and reception conditions; the ability to intend the recipient's grasp of p through recognition of the address; effective control of a realizable channel and the required recipient-enabling conditions; and an exercise compatible with its intrinsic nature and unborrowed excellence. Then it is capable of intentionally disclosing p through that situation.

**Proof.** Realize the jointly warranted intention, channel and reception conditions. By the first condition the signs have the appropriate understood content; by the second they function as intended address; by the third the source can bring about the required delivery and enabling conditions; by the fourth this is an eligible exercise of the same source. Their conjunction realizes the specified act of disclosure. ∎

The proposition makes the construction explicit. It does not deduce jointly realizable abilities from four isolated possibility claims. A speech act need not use a mouth, human language or discursive deliberation, but a particular communication does need a realizable sign-and-recipient relation. The source's pure-perfection route to communicative capacity can warrant these positive abilities where intelligent address is an eligible excellence. Merely failing to find an obstacle is weaker than that argument.

Actual authenticated disclosure adds an event, attributable authorship or authorization, determinate intended content and an adequate route for the particular recipient. Original productive causation is not automatically assertion: a source's creating a creature who lies does not make the lie the source's own address. A spectacular occurrence alone also does not identify the accompanying claim as an authorized message. A distinctive performance in an appropriate commissioning context may furnish positive evidence of source and messenger together, without first accepting the messenger's unsupported testimony. Its discriminating force depends on the actual performance, context and alternatives. That is an available evidential route, not authentication of a particular mission in this argument.

The current affirmative truthfulness argument is likewise retained. It concerns the original's own assertions or acts of certification under their actual communicative scope. Its public substantive owner, *Akmaliyya veracity crosscheck*, separates three premises: knowingly counterfeiting truth has a respect-specific declarative defect; that defect cannot form part of an overall fitting exercise of this original in any relevant context; and its actual exercises conform to substantive fittingness. The first premise does not, by itself, prove the second. Comprehensive Knowledge supplies awareness of the truth; actual source-owned assertion supplies the relevant communicative role. [*Akmaliyya veracity crosscheck*][kg-veracity]

**Source-owned veracity consequence.** Under those premises, every actual source-owned assertion is true. For suppose that such an assertion of p were false. Comprehensive Knowledge supplies awareness that p is false, so its certification incurs the stipulated declarative defect. The all-context integrity premise excludes that exercise from substantive fittingness, while actual practical conformance requires it to be fitting. This contradiction excludes the false assertion. ∎

The affirmative, defeasible appraisal supports the all-context integrity premise for the adequate original; the displayed proof does not establish that premise from a bare local defect. A finite agent's purportedly justified false assertion is therefore a relevant critic of an overgeneralized defect argument, not an authenticated exception in a fully qualified original. The source-specific appraisal also does not require a new theorem that every desirable end achievable by a lie has an equally fitting truthful substitute. Bare theoretical knowledge leaves deliberate deception logically open; a model omitting the all-context integrity premise does not refute the richer account. This preserves both the force and the stated warrant of exceptionless veracity without silently reopening an already considered objection.

Truthfulness is not identical with disclosing everything. Silence, selective communication, an evident test, permissible withholding and a false assertion have different contents and roles. Calling an apparently false promise a test does not resolve it without appropriate source-and-content evidence. Nor may “recipient reliance” be defined as already factive so that the truthfulness conclusion becomes automatic. A route based only on an unauthenticated message's claim that its author is truthful would be circular at the unresolved attribution point. Independent philosophical warrant, cumulative historical evidence or an already authenticated source can contribute different premises without that circle.

*Al-Nubuwwāt* connects wise commissioning with a discriminating indication of the genuine messenger and treats signs as purposive attestation. [*Al-Nubuwwāt*, electronic division 003][kg-nubuwwat] The conditional principle has force when actual commissioning and the relevant undertaking are established; it does not establish them merely by being stated. Nor does the general disclosure argument decide disputed school accounts of speech, a particular language or the identity of a revealed text.

Finally, source veracity and recipient warrant are not the same relation. A recipient needs an adequate source-and-content route and appropriate uptake. Attribution, reporting domain, interpretation, access and retention can each matter. Truthful initial delivery does not by itself guarantee all later audiences access to the same content; a continuing undertaking or other defended bridge would be additional. The existing treatment of [source truth, communicated authority and continuing access](../epistemology/recognition-warrant-and-restoration.md#8-source-truth-recipient-warrant-and-communicated-authority) supplies these recipient distinctions. The positive attribute argument supports a possible trustworthy source without replacing the historical and epistemic work of identifying an actual communication.

<a id="t20-veracity-signature-boundaries"></a>

**Which assumptions connect veracity and absence of counterfeit?** The selected independent boundary tests separate the semantic implications from the normative package. For arbitrary types $S,O,T,Q,E$ in their respective universes, a model $m:\mathrm{Model}(S,O,T,Q,E)$ and a source $g:S$, the two statements are

```math
\mathrm{Factive}(m,g)\land\mathrm{Veracity}(m,g)
   \Longrightarrow\mathrm{NoCounterfeit}(m,g),
```

```math
K(m,g)\land A(m,g)\land C(m,g)\land\mathrm{NoCounterfeit}(m,g)
   \Longrightarrow\mathrm{Veracity}(m,g).
```

Here $K,A,C$ are the source model's knowledge, awareness/coverage and control predicates, not new assumptions inferred from a speaker label. In the first direction a purported counterfeit contains an owned assertion and a claim of known falsity. Veracity makes the content true; factivity makes that incompatible with known falsity. In the second direction, take any owned assertion and suppose its content false. The $K,A,C$ premises supply the three additional components needed for a counterfeit, contradicting `NoCounterfeit`. The displayed source proof uses classical contradiction in this direction. Neither direction consumes the normative predicates $D,N,P$; factivity is not needed for the reverse direction. These implications therefore do not silently derive the all-context normative integrity premise used by the affirmative argument above. [R250-193, lines 69–85][R250-193]

The finite signatures exhibit why the qualifications matter. They are structural controls, explicitly not claims about metaphysical realizability or exhaustive knowledge:

- Set `missingExercise = {dropP with actual := fun _ _ _ => False}`. At source false it satisfies all six displayed predicates $K,A,C,D,N,P$ **and** `Factive`, but fails `ExerciseBridge`; it also satisfies `FalseOwned` and fails `Veracity`. Emptying the actual-exercise relation can leave the six labelled premises satisfied while breaking the link needed to apply practical conformance to an assertion. It is not a model satisfying the full bridge-bearing package. [R250-193, lines 9–20][R250-193]
- Set `nonfactive = {positive with knowsFalse := fun _ _ _ => True}`. At source false, $K,A,C$ and `Veracity` hold, but `Factive` fails; the particular relation `Counterfeit nonfactive false false false true` holds, and `NoCounterfeit` fails. A bare known-false label has been attached indiscriminately, including to true content. Conversely, `dropA` at source false satisfies $K,C$, `Factive` and `NoCounterfeit`, but not $A$ or `Veracity`. The first control isolates factivity in the forward implication; the second isolates coverage in the reverse, even when factivity is supplied. [R250-193, lines 22–38][R250-193]
- In `positive`, the source false satisfies `Package` and `Factive`, and `supplies false true` holds; nevertheless the distinct source true satisfies neither `Veracity` nor `Package`. It raises Lean's instance-synthesis size option to 100000, then supplies proof terms for these exact signature-level claims. No source, imported dependency or checker was executed in this incorporation. The file's reviewer designation does not supply a new independent review or an external philosophical assessment, and its Boolean interpretations do not authenticate an actual speaker or recipient's warrant.

<a id="t20-grounded-attestation-rule-mutations"></a>

**Three premise-erasing rule mutations.** Source ownership, current applicability and prospective authority perform different inferential jobs. The grounded-attestation controls expose this by extending the same imported rule relation in three explicit ways. These are positive derivations in deliberately altered systems, not declarations that the unchanged system endorses the resulting claims. [R250-082]

First define $\mathrm{AuthorshipOnly}(P,c)$ to mean $\mathrm{Rule}(P,c)$ or $(P=\{\mathrm{ownsDuty0}\}\land c=\mathrm{duty0})$. With only the root set $\{\mathrm{source}\}$, the source root supplies `ownsDuty0` and the added rule derives `duty0`. The source labels the missing condition source veracity. Second define $\mathrm{TimeErased}(P,c)$ to mean $\mathrm{Rule}(P,c)$ or $(P=\{\mathrm{duty0},\mathrm{ready}\}\land c=\mathrm{actNow})$. With roots `allRoots.erase occasion`, the inherited duty derivation persists by rule monotonicity, the implementation root supplies `ready`, and the new rule derives `actNow` without the occasion root. A duty's persistence and an implementation's readiness have not supplied the omitted current applicability. [R250-082, lines 5–29][R250-082]

Third define $\mathrm{GrantErased}(P,c)$ to mean $\mathrm{Rule}(P,c)$ or $(P=\{\mathrm{scopeNow}\}\land c=\mathrm{mayIssueNext})$. In `revokeProspective allRoots`, the `scopeNow` root still supplies that premise, so the added rule derives `mayIssueNext` despite the modeled revocation. Scope fit alone has been made to stand in for prospective authority. The three exact judgments are respectively `Derivable Base AuthorshipOnly {source} duty0`, `Derivable Base TimeErased (allRoots.erase occasion) actNow`, and `Derivable Base GrantErased (revokeProspective allRoots) mayIssueNext`. It imports the original rules, root interpretations and revocation operation from `OccurrenceControls`; those imported definitions were not independently read or executed for this incorporation. In particular, the displayed positive derivations must not be recast as fresh proofs of nonderivability in the unchanged rules, as observed misconduct by an actual source, or as a grant of authority to act.

<a id="third-cohort-b-informed-ownership"></a>

**Local truth and strengthened ownership have exact coverage conditions.** The direct veracity provider proves truth first for one owned token whose awareness and deliberateness are supplied. Assuming its content false, K supplies knowledge of falsity; ownership, awareness and deliberateness produce a counterfeit. D classifies its exercise as a shortcoming, N excludes fittingness, while the exercise bridge and P supply fittingness. This contradiction uses the false-to-known-false direction of K, not the converse factivity premise. Universal veracity then uses A and C to cover every owned assertion. Thus the local result does not hide comprehensive awareness or control in the assertion relation. [T750B661]

There is a legitimate stronger relation: define informed ownership of a token to mean original ownership **and** awareness **and** deliberateness. The local proof yields truth for every token in that stronger extension without separately assuming universal A and C for the original extension. But the two assertion extensions at the designated source g coincide exactly when A∧C holds for that source. In one direction, equality of extensions supplies awareness and control for each original assertion; in the other, coverage inserts those conjuncts. Changing the relation is therefore not a proof that the original source was universally aware and deliberate. Nor does it remove N, the substantive all-context integrity condition: the `dropN` veracity assertion is a deliberate negative control. The source's occasion carrier is arbitrary and does not certify an exhaustive metaphysical possibility space. [T750B646] [T750B661]

<a id="f250-a-token-purpose-and-content"></a>

#### Custody, certifying purpose and mission content

The received *al-Nubuwwāt* account gives the preceding disclosure distinction a concrete evidential structure. A natural occurrence can indicate its cause without being intended as a message. A ring, seal, private secret, gesture or utterance used by an envoy requires a further communicative relation, although context can reveal that intention without a previously agreed code. At S002L103–114, especially the historically controlled printed 768–772 and 777–781, the recipient must establish both that the sender supplied the marker with this envoy and that the sender supplied it **to certify**. Theft or loss, a dead sender, unauthorized use of the seal, and a commission merely to repair or use the object are expressly considered. When an alternative arises **and has force**, suspension follows; bare describability of a counterstory is not the rule. The application to divine signs at printed 779 itself asks about source, sending and intended certification. These distinctions belong to the source, not solely to a modern repair of it. [F250-A002-31-46] [F250-A086-58-78] [F250-A211-1-25] [F250-A011-27-55]

Authentication also has a content boundary. A token can warrant “the sender sent this envoy” without licensing every subsequent statement as the sender's assertion. The inquiry therefore needs the proposition actually certified, its authorized scope and the warrant for the sender's truthfulness. Generic divine production or providential sending is insufficiently discriminating: the source includes destructive winds and devils under providential sending, admits subordinate mediated action, and does not treat a distressed unbeliever's answered prayer as religious endorsement. Creating a channel or enabling an impressive deed is consequently not already adopting every claim associated with it. This does not demand an unmediated event. The work grants real contributions to created agents while denying that every such contribution is independently complete production. [F250-A036-51-61] [F250-A100-355-383] [F250-A172-31-41] [F250-A175-1-21]

The positive provision argument likewise has two stages. The Creator who forms a knowing, speaking person is argued capable of instructing and enabling recognition. Fitting actual guidance invokes Wisdom, Justice and Mercy in addition to capability; a demand to obey coupled with the destruction of every discriminating route would conflict with that purposive account. It does not follow that every local audience has already received every necessary item of evidence. Nor does mere nonperformance of a possible certifying act show incapacity. A definition under which a complete true sign cannot attest falsehood still requires identifying a real event satisfying the definition. The source's arguments about fitting means and ends are stronger than an appeal to regularity alone, but remain substantive premises rather than facts created by that definition. [F250-A002-23-29] [F250-A002-62-82] [F250-A036-29-49] [F250-A055-11-26]

The evidential routes are deliberately plural. Character, communicated content, independently grounded testimony and circumstances can support recognition without a universal requirement of a contemporaneous challenge or one individually exclusive wonder. Some signs precede a claimant's birth or follow death; one type can authenticate several truthful envoys. Familiar trustworthy character can defeat a fraud explanation without eliminating sincere error. Loss of a particular proof does not by itself refute the conclusion, while a matching contradictory claim may defeat that proof's discrimination. Reciprocal support is legitimate only where the routes have genuine evidential contact: a consensus whose authority rests wholly on prophecy cannot be the sole premise proving that prophecy, and repetition of one assumed credential is not independent corroboration. [F250-A002-44-60] [F250-A002-84-98] [F250-A010-18-43] [F250-A024-29-62] [F250-A036-63-87]

These are positive resources for actual attestation, not an authentication of every narrated incident. The further work is case-specific: establish the occurrence and relevant transmission, discriminate agents and purposes, identify the certified content, and appraise the available defeaters. A claim of eventual exposure of false messengers needs a defensible historical scope and timescale; merely repeating it does not supply a finite test. The unresolved universal S claim above neither closes this route nor rules it out, and an unauthenticated report cannot simply certify its own divine source. [F250-A055-19-36] [F250-A218-21-36] [F250-A073-49-77]

<a id="foundation250-b-interpretation-evidence"></a>

**Intended meaning, truth and the grade of evidence.** The original *al-Ṣawāʿiq* distinguishes explaining an expression, identifying its external fulfilment, and redirecting it to a non-apparent sense. It does not reject every interpretation. Interpretation reports another speaker's intention; an interpreter's newly stipulated usage does not by itself establish that intention. Lexical possibility must fit the actual construction, syntax, contrast, customary use and communicative purpose. Explanation can occur in another passage or through authorized demonstration. Knowledge of a predicate's meaning need not be an exhaustive account of its mode. Thus positive attribute interpretation is neither context-free word matching nor permission to assign an arbitrary opposite to public guidance. [F250B035, chapters 1–4, 9–16][F250B035] [F250B079]

Its guidance argument joins the speaker's adequate knowledge, expressive capacity and sincere purpose with the hearer's available means of understanding. A speaker who undertakes clear guidance in an essential matter cannot systematically supply uncorrected indications of the contrary and count that as the same successful guidance. This has a specified scope. The same work admits allusion, euphemism, irony and protective indirectness, and distinguishes lawful concealment from false assertion. It therefore does not impose exhaustive disclosure or guarantee that every adversarial inference is correct. Likewise, a messenger's truthfulness, actual utterance, intended meaning, knowledge and ability to communicate are separate questions. Arguments addressed to someone already accepting prophecy cannot establish that antecedent a second time; a denier requires the appropriate earlier argument. [F250B035, chapters 3, 11–12, 21–24 and 002:721–731][F250B035] [F250B079]

The positive attestation comparison is morally richer than success alone. The described false claimant publicly invokes divine authorization; sustained effective support in that specified guiding setting is argued to conflict with complete knowledge, power and wise justice. That gives the anti-false-attestation premise a rationale, while leaving the claimant's actual history and the signs' status as intentional attestation to be established. The source also supplies natural signs, reported miracles, character and content as distinct forms of evidence. Their factual premises are not independently authenticated by reading the report. The wider second-volume notes distinguish al-Razi's quoted testimony taxonomy and the criticized Mu'tazilite premise chain from the respondent's own position; an objection to the whole chain is not a denial of every shared moral judgment. [F250B035, chapter 12 and chapter 20][F250B035] [F250B022, faces 119–126 and 239–242][F250B022]

The recorded evidence-ranking rule is source-neutral: decisive evidence outranks probable evidence; competing probable indications require weighing; two true decisive proofs cannot conflict. This is compatible with forged reports, uncertain transmission, mistaken interpretation and differences of competence. Rejecting an endless succession of merely imaginable defeaters does not authenticate any particular claim of certainty. The source separately distinguishes a sign from its object and our knowledge of revelation from revelation's truth. A failure to know is not in general knowledge of absence, although missing expected testimony can be probative where strong reasons for its transmission are independently established. An inference from absence of divine knowledge requires comprehensive Knowledge, not ordinary human ignorance. [F250B035, second-polemic opening][F250B035] [F250B079] [F250B022, face 91][F250B022]

The work's fairness and competence rules also constrain its own polemics. Specialist accomplishment in medicine, mathematics or engineering does not transfer automatically to theology; the converse would be equally unwarranted. Possessing collected books is not mastery of their contents. Not knowing a dissenter is not proof of consensus, and an interlocutor's error elsewhere does not make every report false or every argument worthless. The sixth collection similarly distinguishes sincerity from correctness, grades weak narration separately from the plausibility of its lesson, and records explicit reconsideration of an earlier use of the Banu Qurayza precedent. Correctness, excused error, permitted diversity and blame are not interchangeable. The historical accounts of Husayn and Yazid and the devotional, ritual and commercial materials remain source-attributed arguments, not newly authenticated histories or present rulings. These substantive checks prevent either inherited authority or blanket dismissal from replacing inquiry. [F250B035, chapters 19 and 21–23][F250B035] [F250B084] [F250B185] [F250B023, T8–T11][F250B023] [F250B119] [F250B131]

### 12.12 Knowing a corrective target and securing a safe action

The distinction between source cognition and recipient uptake has an operational counterpart. Knowing which condition should be restored does not automatically identify an actuator that will restore it. Nor does source Wisdom by itself establish a proper function for every constructed artifact or endorse every occurring policy. The attribute study uses a bounded fault model to make the action distinction exact. Its roots are authenticated report-and-actuation identities in a specified corruption model, not ultimate ontological sources.

Let $`n=2f+1`$ such roots be available, with a fixed corrupt set C satisfying $`|C|\le f`$. Every honest root reports the true target $`\theta`$ and performs the specified correct repair when selected. Corrupt roots may report truthfully while retaining the ability to make a selected action fail. Assume distinct authenticated identities, no extra evidence distinguishing the unexposed roots, and a one-shot choice whose success is guaranteed by an honest root but can be defeated by a corrupt one. Since more than half the roots are honest, their reports identify $`\theta`$ by strict majority. This is a positive diagnosis result under the fault budget; it is not yet a safe-actuator certificate.

Suppose k distinct roots have exposed themselves by a report differing from that majority. They are corrupt and can be excluded. Put $`m=n-k`$ and $`b=f-k`$, with $`0\le k\le f`$. In the maximally ambiguous case all remaining roots report $`\theta`$, and every subset of b remaining roots is a possible remaining corrupt set.

**One-shot minimax failure bound.** Under these conditions, the optimal worst-case failure probability is

```math
\frac{b}{m}=\frac{f-k}{n-k}.
```

**Proof.** Uniformly choose among the m unexposed roots. At most b are corrupt, so failure probability is at most $`b/m`$. For the converse, take any distribution $`p_1,\ldots,p_m`$ over the unexposed roots. Averaging the probability mass of a uniformly selected b-element subset gives

```math
\frac{1}{\binom{m}{b}}\sum_{|B|=b}\sum_{i\in B}p_i
=\frac{b}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}p_i
=\frac{b}{m}.
```

Hence some b-element subset has mass at least $`b/m`$. Choose that subset as the unexposed corrupt roots and let them fail when selected. Their preceding truthful reports remain compatible with the observations, so every selection rule has worst-case failure at least $`b/m`$. When b=0 the bound is zero directly. Assigning weight to already exposed corrupt roots cannot improve the optimum: the adversary may fail on that weight as well. The two bounds coincide. ∎

At k=0 the value is $`f/n`$; if f=0 it is zero. A fixed deterministic first choice has worst-case failure one when corruption remains possible at the chosen root. The probability in the minimax result comes from the randomized selection rule, not an assumption that corruptions are probabilistically independent. The adversary may choose its fixed corrupt set after seeing the rule but before its random draw. Richer authentication evidence, a different fault budget, adaptive corruption or a changed action semantics produces a different problem. The formula is exact for the displayed symmetric uncertainty class, not every history in which k faults have been noticed.

An authenticated indication that a particular i is outside C changes the feasible corrupt sets and permits a guaranteed honest choice. Knowing only $`\theta`$ does not. A source's ability to disclose such an indication changes neither the actual evidence nor the choice until a suitable communication is received and authenticated. This gives the disclosure argument a precise positive use while keeping capability distinct from its exercise.

There is also an independent positive route through **fail-silent action**. Let R be the target set of restored states. Suppose an honest action maps every relevant state into R, while every corrupt action is either the identity or a correct repair into R. Assume the same fixed fault bound and executable access to f+1 distinct roots. Execute those actions in any order. At least one is honest, so its action reaches R; every later permitted action preserves R, either by doing nothing or by repairing again. Thus the sequence guarantees a terminal state in R. No revelatory message is required for this result. Destructive actions, a drifting target, reuse of one identity or an adaptive fault set would violate its hypotheses.

These propositions supply the ordinary proofs of the bounded comparison imported by the attribute study. They do not reproduce a wider controller, observation history or experiment, and they do not certify the truth of a human or theological corruption model. An original shared creator does not collapse multiple operational identities into one fault domain: that identification requires a relevant shared failure mechanism. Conversely, evidence of such a mechanism can invalidate the assumed budget. Ontological dependence, copied testimony, authenticated identity and control of an actual repair each have their own role. The distinction is compatible with the existing [target-based account of restoration](../epistemology/recognition-warrant-and-restoration.md#9-what-would-constitute-restoration), which also separates observed improvement from its causal explanation.

#### What a truthful attestation must supply to this action contract

The truthful-agency investigation fixes T0 as **not knowingly falsifying an in-scope attestation**, not factual omniscience. For p_i meaning that this actual root is outside fixed C, relevant source cognition, nonlying integrity and an actual owned assertion together imply p_i. Reference must bind its root, repair, target, authorization and version to the decoded action; an independently warranted causal contract must make p_i sufficient for the safe adequate intervention; and the recipient must have a warranted route to these facts without a defeater. External truth alone is not justified reliance. A coded root label can carry that assertion through an established convention, but an authenticated bare directive or a truthful lottery description need not assert it. [N250A041] [N250A048]

The deletion cases identify separate failures. A fully informed nonlying source may issue a harmful command without asserting safety; remain truthfully silent; attest only the correct diagnostic target, which corrupt roots can also report; supply a true snapshot without a warranted interval guarantee; or correctly name a safe root while an unverified transport actuates another. The snapshot case changes the fixed-C persistence contract and is not a counterexample under it. A single actual helpful assertion supplies pointwise information, not the message-availability and honesty policy over every compatible corruption set needed by a uniform communication theorem. Even eventual exposure of every lie can follow irreversible intervention and thus cannot alone furnish decision-time safety; this does not refute the source's separate character, mercy or wisdom arguments. [N250A041] [N250A042] [N250A048]

The separately reported dynamic family requires stronger content: lifetime taint C* bounded by B, command binding, close-before-acknowledge ordering (physical veto before acknowledgment), durable revocation and physical veto outside C*, thresholds q+r>n+B with q,r≤n−B, and reservation semantics preserving permission until revocation completes. The historical truthfulness report reverses that order in its phrase “acknowledgment-before-veto”; that wording is not adopted as the mechanism contract. Its associated reviews explicitly withhold certification of the dynamic proof and do not independently repair the ordering. The admitted original-interface bodies correct the historical reversal: the mechanism requires close-before-acknowledge. [N250A-026] [N250A-031] [N250A-033] A current good-root snapshot is not testimony to those lifetime conditions. This report retains that dependency description without certifying its proof, implementation or common consistency with the philosophical source premises. Neither T0 nor the token-purpose lemma builds this mechanism, causes an actual message, establishes R5 defeat or identifies the epistemic and operational roles as one metaphysical bearer. [N250A041] [N250A046] [N250A048]

### 12.13 Comparison and the composed positive account

The account can now be compared with rivals without replacing their positive proposals by absences. The relevant contrasts are these:

| Comparison | Positive content retained | Question for this argument |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intrinsic dispositional powers | Laws may follow from the nature of properties, rather than govern them from outside. Bird's “monistic” claim concerns the kind of fundamental properties, not a single concrete substance. [Bird, §§1–2][kg-bird] | Does that nature account for actual cognitive and practical excellence at the complete original, and does law necessity establish an actual bearer? |
| Immanent natural teleology | Aristotle treats nature as an intrinsic principle and allows purposive organization without observed deliberation. [*Physics*, II.1 and II.8][kg-aristotle] | Is natural directedness sufficient for the received episode's genuine apprehension and action for understood reasons? |
| Thinking necessitarianism | Spinoza attributes Thought and an idea of essence and consequences, while treating actual intellect and will as modes and denying free willing of another order. [*Ethics*, I.31–34 and II.1–3][kg-spinoza] | What warrants the relevant practical and modal distinction once cognition itself is granted? |
| Productive transcendence of intellect | Plotinus's One is a productive principle from which Intellect proceeds; it is not an inert placeholder. [*Enneads*, V.2.1][kg-plotinus] | Does the cognitive original-giver comparison apply across that proposed distinction, and with what eligibility warrant? |
| Coordinated plurality | Several agents can contribute to one plan; observed design alone does not identify one complete planner. [Hume, *Dialogues*, V.8–9][kg-hume-design] | Do the stronger complete-provision, unborrowed-exercise and actual-field premises of §§9–11 identify one original in the same respect? |

Each comparison concerns specified claims, not an exhaustive reconstruction of its author. An intrinsic relation between powers is not automatically an efficient donation from one bearer to another. Nor is a description of coordination already an additional real coordinator. The same standard applies to the affirmative account: assigning several excellences to one bearer is explanatory progress when the relations among apprehension, fitting end, willing and productive efficacy are defended. Reducing the number of names alone does not establish it.

The composed result is positive and conditional at its several inferential steps. The actual original and its productive scope come from the preceding arguments. Respect-specific priority and eligibility support original cognition; intrinsic determination supports its standing possession. Complete apprehension of actual productive determinations extends to their known effects, while the distinct pure-perfection argument warrants comprehensive Knowledge. Practical integrity connects that cognition with fitting willing and Wisdom. Jointly realizable communicative capacities support disclosure, and the affirmative truthfulness account concerns the source's own actual assertions. Authenticated reception and a suitable action model can then support determinate human knowledge or correction.

No step loses its force merely because it uses a defended philosophical premise. Equally, none acquires the next step's premises merely through composition. A skeptical control over thin productive relations does not negate the richer affirmative doctrine; an affirmative attribute appraisal does not authenticate an unexamined message or certify a safe actuator. The integration here supplies explicit connections, proofs and matched limits for the already developed arguments. It claims neither a newly discovered universal theorem nor a new adoption of a private accepted work.


### 12.14 Meaning, intrinsic attributes and particular acts

The source account of sound reason connects its epistemology with a substantive view of divine attributes. That part of the account belongs with the source argument developed here: a proposed original can be genuinely knowing, willing and active without possessing the creature's manner of knowledge, volition or action. Its claims must retain their **Atharī, source-relative character**, notwithstanding the predecessor's introductory description of them as the deliverances of sound reason without a school label. The following reconstruction preserves the arguments and identifies where their conclusions require more than a semantic distinction. It neither speaks for all theological schools nor supplies new historical authentication of the source's unattributed quotations. [*The Epistemological Architecture of Sound Reason*, §6–§6.3][pf-sound-reason]

#### Meaning without an exhaustive account of mode

The affirmative semantic proposal separates a predicate's intelligible content from the concrete manner in which its bearer instantiates it. Knowledge, for example, concerns apprehension of things as they are; sensory organs, memory dependence, inference and temporal acquisition describe some creaturely ways of knowing. Removing those dependencies need not remove every positive cognitive meaning. The source uses *bilā kayf*—without specifying the how—to affirm an attribute while withholding an unwarranted creaturely modality. Within that proposal, analogy preserves a meaningful point of predication while declining an identity of modes. It is not the inference that a predicate with wholly unspecified content has nonetheless been established.

The argument has three tasks. First identify the positive content attributed. Next justify its eligibility and application to the source. Then distinguish what is known of that content from what has not been warranted about its mode. Section 12.5's cognitive-eligibility argument does the second kind of work; the semantic permission alone does not. In particular, merely imagining a body-like manner of an attribute and then rejecting the attributed meaning because of that imagined manner would assume a conjunction the source account denies. But withholding a mode also cannot cure a contradiction in the specified content or a demonstrated intrinsic deficiency. Both positive meaning and the limit of its application remain answerable to reasons. [Sound Reason][pf-sound-reason]

The predecessor presses a self-undermining objection against a universal linguistic prohibition: if no human expression could meaningfully concern what exceeds creaturely experience, a meaningful assertion of that very prohibition about God would exceed its own limit. The objection reaches the **unrestricted prohibition** when it is itself offered as meaningful theological knowledge. It does not show that every theological predicate is intelligible, that finite language exhausts its object, or that a modest claim of incomplete comprehension defeats itself. “Some meaningful predication is possible” and “this particular predication is true” are different conclusions. A critic can accept the former while disputing the latter.

This account also clarifies the source's argument about perfection and relational exercise. Possession of an excellence does not, merely by its being an excellence, require every possible outward exercise or an eternal distinct object of that exercise. Mercy or forgiveness does not by that generic description establish an eternal creature needing it. The predecessor deploys this point against an inference from perfect love to eternally distinct divine persons: the inference needs a separately justified premise that this specific perfection requires that particular eternal relational realization. The distinction blocks an unargued step; it does not resolve every developed Christian account of love, persons and relations or establish its own full alternative theology. [Sound Reason][pf-sound-reason]

#### Standing perfection and actual exercise

The source distinguishes what a bearer necessarily is from what it actually does. On its positive account, divine existence and essential perfection are intrinsic, while particular acts proceed through Power and Will towards their effects. The created effect is distinct from its source and genuinely received. The source argues against identifying that relation with a necessary emanation in which no further account of willing is available. Its positive alternative is informed productive exercise, rather than an inert abstraction to which action has been denied. The fuller argument for the practical relation is supplied in §§12.4 and 12.9; the source's polemical description of a “philosopher's God” is not a sufficient characterization of every philosophical theology.

Two logical distinctions preserve the affirmative content. First, $`\Box E(g)`$ does not entail $`\Box\mathrm{Does}(g,a)`$. An interpretation with g existing in two worlds and a occurring in only one satisfies the first formula and denies the second. This proves non-entailment from the weaker formula; it does not authenticate the metaphysical possibility of those worlds under the complete source doctrine. Second, a necessary conditional connection between a complete exercise and its effect does not make that exercise necessary. The stronger issue—whether an entire necessarily wise nature permits distinct particular acts—retains the qualified comparison in §12.9. Merely writing “free” cannot decide it, just as an act's being determined by the source's own willing does not make it externally compelled. [Sound Reason][pf-sound-reason]; see also §§12.6–12.9.

The source's perpetual-activity claim has a related quantifier limit. It proposes enduring ability and voluntary activity without requiring one particular created effect to be everlasting. Formally, $`\forall t\,\exists x\,\mathrm{Produces}(g,x,t)`$ does not imply $`\exists x\,\forall t\,\mathrm{Produces}(g,x,t)`$. With integer times, let $`x_n`$ first exist at n and be produced at n. Every time has a particular production, while each product has earlier times at which it does not exist. This interpretation illustrates the quantifier distinction, not the actual beginninglessness of creation or a complete temporal metaphysics. The further source claim that the agent is prior to each particular effect and that the effect occurs upon its complete determination must retain its own interpretation of priority and exercise. It is not a proof that every divine act is a created external object.

Ontological dependence also differs from identity. A received person can be sustained by g while remaining a distinct bearer whose cognition and action are genuinely its own. This is compatible with §12.6's distinction between original provision of a thought and ownership of that thought. Calling a dependent subject either absorbed into its source or an independent rival substitutes a false dichotomy for those two relations. The source affirms real created subjecthood and orientation towards the Creator. Its further comparative claim that this is more secure than every physical account of personal identity is not established by the dependence/identity distinction alone; a developed physical account must be assessed at its actual arguments. [Sound Reason][pf-sound-reason]

#### Created measures, originating acts and speech

The time discussion separates temporal relations, the measure of motion in a particular created system, and the source's own proposed acts or duration. Treating created time as a measure belonging to a created substrate does not by itself prove that all meaningful order or priority is abolished when that system is absent. Conversely, rejecting a self-standing container does not establish the reality or nature of divine duration. The source's claims about “before,” spatial language and directional predicates require its substantive semantic and theological commitments. No cosmological measurement or modern physical theory is inferred from this conceptual distinction. [Sound Reason, §6.1][pf-sound-reason]

The same account distinguishes *ḥudūth*, coming to occur, from *khalq*, external creation, in its specified theological usage. Its proposed speech doctrine holds together an enduring attribute of speaking, particular acts occurring by Will, and those acts' subsistence in the speaker rather than their being detached external products. Thus a particular occurrence can be originated without being classified as created in that stipulated sense. This makes explicit which additional premise is rejected when one infers from temporal occurrence alone to external createdness. It does not establish that every school uses these words in that way or that the distinction alone proves the proposed ontology.

The predecessor presents two contrasting positions through that polemical lens: it attributes to the Muʿtazilī alternative the treatment of the relevant originated speech as created, and to the Ashʿarī account associated there with Ibn Kullāb an eternal inner meaning with created external verbal expression. It criticizes the former for joining origination to createdness and the latter for excluding originating acts from the divine subject. Those are **the predecessor's comparative attributions**, retained here to make its argument intelligible. They have not been newly checked against representative primary texts of either school and must not be treated as an exhaustive neutral taxonomy or an established verdict that those schools sever authentic revelation from its speaker. Their strongest formulations would require their own source-controlled comparison. [Sound Reason, §6.2][pf-sound-reason]

There is an additional bearer distinction even within the source's own affirmative account. A divine speech act, the content attributed to it, a human act of recitation, a heard acoustic event and a written token are not one object merely because they convey corresponding words. The source's reference to the Qurʾān as recited and heard cannot establish that a creature's vocal action subsists in God. The relevant account must determine what is attributed to the source and what to the created medium. This is the same safeguard used in §12.11: original production of a medium is not automatically authorship of every assertion it carries. The source's proposed parity between divine speech and divine action is an argument for consistent application of its subsistence/external-effect distinction; a successful formal parity does not authenticate a particular revelation or decide every disputed speech predicate.


<a id="second250-uthaymin-full-activity-premise"></a>

A later Ibn ʿUthaymīn locus audit gives a bounded source check on these distinctions. The official Arabic lecture transcripts at Nisāʾ 6, Q4:15; Nisāʾ 26, Q4:87; Nisāʾ 33, Q4:114; and Shūrā 6 distinguish essential capacity, the genus of voluntary activity, particular kinds, occurring tokens and their effects. Nisāʾ 33 expressly rejects an interval without activity on the substantive premise that acting is a perfection. An everywhere-empty activity interpretation therefore tests a reduced capacity-only signature, not this fuller doctrine. General always-activity does not require every kind or one particular creature to exist eternally, and the will-governed clause does not revoke the general activity premise. [S250B-049, lines 11–49](https://github.com/theislampill/orthemology/blob/a7ff0e33d1a299db640041c46b1af81ca70851f6/experiments/orthemology-v5-successors/source-store/3deb84870b2d2de2da472946031d2886e06d03efbc76e9e2b6c6ff968e738b50/LOCUS_AUDIT.md#L11-L49)

The supplementary Ghāfir 2, Q40:6 discussion makes succession belong to speech itself, contrasting it with the newly occurring object of hearing. Thus the reported view cannot be represented merely as new external objects of an otherwise wholly unchanged intrinsic speech act. At the same time, temporal novelty of an act is not by this source's usage a newly created divine bearer, a separate created entity or externally acquired perfection. A bridge between those claims needs an argument. This is inherited targeted transcript evidence, not a new Arabic reading here or independent historical evidence for Ibn Taymiyya's exact wording. The report establishes no print pagination or listened-to sentence timestamp; the recorded audio times are webpage section boundaries. [S250B-049, lines 21–29](https://github.com/theislampill/orthemology/blob/a7ff0e33d1a299db640041c46b1af81ca70851f6/experiments/orthemology-v5-successors/source-store/3deb84870b2d2de2da472946031d2886e06d03efbc76e9e2b6c6ff968e738b50/LOCUS_AUDIT.md#L21-L29) [S250B-049, lines 51–59](https://github.com/theislampill/orthemology/blob/a7ff0e33d1a299db640041c46b1af81ca70851f6/experiments/orthemology-v5-successors/source-store/3deb84870b2d2de2da472946031d2886e06d03efbc76e9e2b6c6ff968e738b50/LOCUS_AUDIT.md#L51-L59) [S250B-049, lines 79–100](https://github.com/theislampill/orthemology/blob/a7ff0e33d1a299db640041c46b1af81ca70851f6/experiments/orthemology-v5-successors/source-store/3deb84870b2d2de2da472946031d2886e06d03efbc76e9e2b6c6ff968e738b50/LOCUS_AUDIT.md#L79-L100) [S250B-049, lines 5–9](https://github.com/theislampill/orthemology/blob/a7ff0e33d1a299db640041c46b1af81ca70851f6/experiments/orthemology-v5-successors/source-store/3deb84870b2d2de2da472946031d2886e06d03efbc76e9e2b6c6ff968e738b50/LOCUS_AUDIT.md#L5-L9)

<a id="final189-b07-origination-type-control"></a>

The explicit origination type-control makes the preceding distinctions inspectable without purporting to establish a metaphysical possibility. Its object constructors are potential labels; a separate E predicate determines present existence. A G-act inheres in the ground and produces a distinct created effect. Within this declared signature, coming to occur need not entail external createdness or whole external receipt. Kinds and standing power remain predicates, not extra object bearers. [F189B-840](https://github.com/theislampill/orthemology/blob/a7ff0e33d1a299db640041c46b1af81ca70851f6/experiments/orthemology-v5-successors/source-store/e3e5480db5b874448b7f4448ce6bce66e426995afbcb45e31ce61f755e03fdfe/OriginationTypeControl.lean)

The frame has one everywhere-existing ground, possible fresh G-acts after every world, and particular emergent tokens that permanently cease after their indexed occurrence. G-empty is weaker than all-emergent-empty: an auxiliary created kind may remain when no G-act is present. The model separately permits an all-emergent-empty state and an actual alternating sequence of empty and active states. Those stronger stipulations do not follow from G-emptiness or modal renewability, and they do not preserve an always-active premise. The source explicitly disclaims attributing complete cessation to Ibn Taymiyya. Thus this is a representation control for the act/product, kind/token and modal/time distinctions, not a counterexample to the affirmative Athari–Taymiyyan account under its stronger substantive premises. [F189B-840](https://github.com/theislampill/orthemology/blob/a7ff0e33d1a299db640041c46b1af81ca70851f6/experiments/orthemology-v5-successors/source-store/e3e5480db5b874448b7f4448ce6bce66e426995afbcb45e31ce61f755e03fdfe/OriginationTypeControl.lean)

<a id="foundation250-activity-context"></a>

The received contextual audit gives the anti-inactivity claim a distinct causal rationale. Its electronically edition-bound Ṣafadiyya 2:142 passage argues that stripping the original agent of all successive voluntary activity even at a time would leave no sufficient change from which a fresh act could begin, absent an independent external enabler. This is stronger than persistent capacity. The separately reported later perfection argument against total inactivity supplies another rationale, not another witness for the same primary reading. Neither asserts that every kind or every token is always exercised. Beginningless possibility, actual beginningless activity, absence of an interval of total inactivity and absence of ultimate exhaustion are different temporal claims; formal application must specify the relevant times, intervals and event boundaries. [F250H53]

The same audit binds the statement about the impossibility of an eternal particular act to Ṣafadiyya 2:145, with the continuation at 2:146–149. Its point is not that the enduring power or will must itself be newly caused: that inference threatens a regress in the basis of agency. It distinguishes an enduring essential attribute or genus from a particular successive voluntary act and from a detached created product. The reported Salim electronic pagination and Adwa scan coordinates are distinct edition controls, not interchangeable citations or a newly collated manuscript witness. These stronger source commitments explain why the capacity-only empty-extension construction remains a valid reduced-signature control without becoming a countermodel to the fuller doctrine. [F250H53]

<a id="foundation250-bearer-application"></a>

The ontology audit imposes an application condition on the whole-bearer argument, not a retraction of its conditional proof. A temporally novel intrinsic act is not automatically a contingently existing whole bearer in its B-domain. Before applying ContingencyNeed, receipt representation or constitutive reception, the interpretation must admit the particular entity as the relevant bearer and identify the intended receipt relation. Support transport runs from whole-bearer receipt to resource receipt, not conversely. Power and kind predicates likewise need not denote second independently existing individuals. The source's distinction between intrinsic acts and created products supports these typing controls; it does not establish either universal denial of dependence or a frozen divine state. [F250H46] [F250H194] [F250H201]
